sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: Why does safe driving demand your undivided attention every second behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: Safe driving needs your full attention, because it involves constant and complex coordination between your mind and your body.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: How does the guide define a driving distraction, and which three groups are endangered by it?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: A distraction is anything that keeps you from operating the car safely, and every distraction puts drivers, passengers and bystanders at risk.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: Beyond phones and texting, what everyday cabin habits appear on the Missouri guide's distraction list?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: The guide's list of distractions includes texting, phone use, eating and drinking, talking to passengers, adjusting audio players, grooming, reading maps, watching videos, browsing the Internet and using navigation.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: Does the Missouri driver guide count ordinary conversation with passengers as a driving distraction?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Talking with passengers appears on the guide's list of distractions, alongside eating, grooming and reading.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: Which three faculties does texting pull off driving simultaneously, making it the deadliest distraction?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: Texting takes your eyes, your hands and your mind off driving at once, which makes it by far the riskiest distraction.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: Which drivers are barred under Missouri law from reading, writing, or sending electronic text messages while driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: Missouri law forbids anyone to read, write or send a text or other electronic message while operating a vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: Which three living companions inside your vehicle can easily turn into dangerous distractions?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: Children, friends and pets can each become a dangerous distraction while you drive.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: What should you do when children in the car need your attention during a drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: If your children need attention, pull over to a safe place instead of handling them while driving.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: What lesson does the guide say to teach young children about your role behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: Teach young children that driving is an important job that needs your concentration when you are behind the wheel.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: Where do arguments and upsetting conversations belong instead of inside a moving car?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: Save arguments and upsetting conversations for a safe place, not for while you are driving.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: In what three ways can a car packed with friends pull a driver's focus off the road?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: A car full of friends can distract you with loud talk, arguments over music, or horseplay.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: How does the Missouri driver guide view letting a pet roam loose inside a moving vehicle?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: A loose pet in a moving vehicle can be very dangerous.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: Which three restraints keep a pet safe in a moving car, and where must a pet never sit?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: Secure a pet in a carrier, portable kennel or pet harness while driving, and never let it sit on your lap.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: Which dashboard or connected-screen tasks can trigger a crash or near-crash?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: Entering a destination, scanning radio stations or changing climate settings can lead to a crash or near-crash, and Internet and email access add more risk.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: What core warning sits behind the guide's heading that turning dials can turn your head?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: Under the heading turning dials can turn your head, the guide warns that working in-vehicle controls pulls your attention from the road.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: Which four cabin adjustments should you lock in before shifting out of park?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: Set the climate controls, mirrors, radio and seat before you start to drive.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: When should you check email, voicemail, and similar digital messages around a trip?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: Check email, voicemail and other devices before you leave or after you arrive, not on the way.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: What automatic phone feature helps stop callers and texters from expecting an answer while you drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: You can set an auto-reply on your phone saying you are driving and will call back later.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: What two safe options do you have if radio, climate, or navigation needs adjusting mid-trip?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: Use normal stops to adjust controls, or ask a passenger to adjust the radio, climate or navigation for you.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: Which six outside-the-window sights become dangerous distractions when drivers stare at them?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: Staring at a crash scene, a vehicle stopped by police, a scenic view, a billboard, street addresses or construction work while driving is a distraction.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: What mindset should replace studying passing roadside scenery when you are behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Stay focused on driving and remain alert so you reach your destination safely, instead of studying the scenery you pass.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: Which vehicle classes and which roadways are covered by Missouri's electronic communication device law?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.expected_back: Missouri law bars drivers of both commercial and noncommercial vehicles from using an electronic communication device on any highway or property open to public traffic, apart from the allowed uses.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: Under what vehicle condition do the prohibited uses in Missouri's electronic device law apply?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: The device bans listed in the law apply while the vehicle is in motion.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: While your vehicle is moving, may you hold a cellphone in your hand or prop it with your shoulder?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: While the vehicle is moving, you may not hold or support a cellphone with any part of your body.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: Which four manual text-message actions are illegal while your vehicle is moving?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: While the vehicle is moving, you may not type, write, send or read text-based messages by hand.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.front: What video-creation, streaming, or calling activities are barred while your vehicle is in motion?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.expected_back: While the vehicle is moving, you may not record, post, send or broadcast video, including video calls and social media posts.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.front: May a driver watch a movie or video clip while the vehicle is moving?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.expected_back: While the vehicle is moving, you may not watch a video or movie.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.front: How must voice calls be started, answered, or ended to stay legal while driving in Missouri?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.expected_back: The law lets you make or take voice calls with voice-operated or hands-free features that turn on or off with a single touch or swipe.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.front: Through which three audio setups may a Missouri driver talk hands-free on a voice call?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.expected_back: You may talk hands-free through a built-in speaker, in-car Bluetooth, or earbuds or a headset.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.front: What feature lets Missouri drivers legally send and receive text-based messages while driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.expected_back: You may send and receive text-based messages through voice-to-text features.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.front: Which map, route, and listening functions remain legal on your phone under Missouri's device law?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.expected_back: You may use phone GPS navigation, view a map for navigation, and play music, podcasts, broadcasts or digital audio.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: If your phone sits in a dash mount untouched, how does the law treat a voice call versus a video call?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: A hands-free voice call is allowed while moving, but a video call is banned even when the phone is not held.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: Contrast the single legal way and the banned way to handle text messages in a moving car?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: Text-based messages are allowed only through voice-to-text; typing or reading them by hand while moving is banned.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: What condition must a rideshare driver meet to use a device for relaying company network trip info?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: A rideshare driver may use a device to relay information through the company's network only if the device is attached or mounted to the vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.front: How did Missouri device-law enforcement shift across the January first, twenty twenty-five milestone?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.expected_back: Before January one, two thousand twenty-five, a violation of the device law may bring a warning; after that date it may bring an infraction.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: Since January first, twenty twenty-five, how can officers cite a violation of Missouri's electronic device law?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: Since January one, two thousand twenty-five, a device law violation may be treated as an infraction rather than only a warning.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.front: What licensing penalty can hit commercial drivers under the device law, and what broader penalties can apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.expected_back: Commercial drivers who violate the device law may be disqualified, and fines and criminal penalties may also apply under state law.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: For which specific group of drivers does the guide name disqualification as a device-law consequence?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: Disqualification is a possible consequence named only for commercial drivers who violate the device law.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: What five pieces of roadway guidance do painted lines and pavement symbols give drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Pavement lines and symbols tell drivers where lanes split, where passing or changing lanes is allowed, which lanes are for turning, where walkers cross, and where to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: How does a dashed pavement stripe differ from a solid stripe when you want to overtake?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: A broken line may be crossed to pass, while a solid line should not be crossed to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Yellow lines divide traffic going in opposite directions, and white lines divide traffic going the same direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What does seeing yellow versus white paint immediately to your left reveal, and what marks the right road edge?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.memory_hook: Left yellow oncoming; right edge white
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: A yellow line on your left means traffic beyond it is coming toward you, while a white line on your left means it is going your way; a solid white line often marks the right edge of the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What markings run down the middle of an undivided four-lane road, and may you cross them to overtake?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: On a four-lane road the center is marked with two solid yellow lines, and you must never cross them to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: How is a two-lane no-passing zone striped, where does it appear, and when must your pass finish?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: A no passing zone on a two-lane road is marked by a solid yellow line and is placed on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, so finish any pass before reaching it.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: When does a center solid yellow stripe bar you from passing, and what rule governs unmarked two-lane roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.memory_hook: Your solid blocks; need clear view
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Do not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line, and on any two-lane road never pass without seeing enough clear road, even if there is no marking.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Why must you never swing onto the road shoulder to get around another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: Do not pass using the shoulder, because drivers do not expect a car there and may pull onto it without checking.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Where on the pavement must your front bumper stop when halted by a sign or red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: When a sign or signal requires a stop, stop before the stop line, or before the crosswalk if one is marked.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: What roadway purpose do marked crosswalk stripes serve?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: Crosswalks mark the area where pedestrians are meant to cross the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: To which walkers must you yield at crosswalks, and why watch closely at intersections without white stripes?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.memory_hook: In or stepping in; unpainted counts
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or about to step into one, and stay alert at intersections without marked crosswalks, because not every crosswalk is painted.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: In a lane marked for both straight and turning movement, when may you turn versus when must you hold?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: In a dual-use lane with turn and straight arrows, you may turn or go straight when both arrows show on the signal, but if only the straight arrow is lit you must wait for the turn arrow before turning.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How is a two-way shared left-turn lane striped, what moves belong in it, and when should you exit it?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: A shared center lane, bordered by a solid yellow and a dashed yellow line on each side, is used by traffic from both directions for left turns, or U-turns where allowed, and you turn out of it as soon as your path is clear.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: What yellow pavement markings identify a dedicated left-turn lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Marked left-turn lanes use solid yellow lines together with thick yellow stripes on the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What is the rule on reversing inside a travel lane when you overshoot an exit or corner?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Never back up in a travel lane; if you miss a turn or exit, keep going to a place where you can safely turn around.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Are you ever allowed to halt inside a travel lane because you are lost, stalling, or dropping off a rider?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Never stop in a travel lane, whether you are lost, broken down or dropping someone off; keep going until you can safely pull off.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Where three or more lanes run your direction, which lane is your home lane and when should you move middle?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: With three or more lanes going your way, stay in the right lane except to pass, but use the center lane if a lot of traffic is entering the right lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Which lane is built for overtaking on multi-lane roads, and what makes right-side passing hazardous?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.memory_hook: Pass far left; right hides cars
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: On multi-lane roads the left-most lane is meant for passing, and passing on the right is risky because the other driver may not see you and may move over.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Alongside signs, lights, and paint, which three groups of people have legal authority to direct traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: Traffic control covers signals, signs and pavement markings, and it can also come from police, highway workers or school crossing guards, whose directions you must follow.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: What must you do when a uniformed officer waves you to stop even though the overhead light is green?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Always obey a traffic officer over any sign or signal, so if an officer signals you to stop at a green light, you stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: How do you respond to a flashing red signal compared with a flashing yellow signal?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Where do you halt for a steady red traffic light, and what is the lone exception to waiting for green?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.memory_hook: Halt before line; right turn exception
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: At a steady red light, stop at the stop line, the crosswalk or before the intersection and wait for green unless you are turning right.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What three conditions must all be met before turning right at a steady red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: After a complete stop you may turn right on red if no pedestrians or traffic are in the way, unless a No Right Turn On Red sign is posted.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What does a solid yellow traffic light warn, and when is driving through it justified?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: Before accelerating on a circular green light, whom must you still allow to clear?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A green light lets you go through, but first yield to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: After coming to a full stop, how does your next step differ at a flashing red signal versus a steady red?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: A flashing red signal works like a stop sign, while a steady red means stop and wait for green except for a permitted right turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What separates your required action at a flashing yellow light from a steady yellow light?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means slow and proceed with caution, while a steady yellow means the light is about to turn red and you should stop if you safely can.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: During which four situations might intersection lights switch to flashing mode in every direction?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Signals may flash in all directions during emergencies, at night, in periods of light traffic and at special events.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How must every approaching driver treat an intersection whose traffic lights are completely dark or broken?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: A traffic signal that is dark or not working is treated as a four-way stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which two signal displays appear during a permissive left-turn phase, and what must you wait for?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.memory_hook: Green ball or flashing arrow yields
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: In a permissive left-turn phase you get a circular green or a flashing yellow arrow and must wait for a big enough gap in oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Which signal lets you turn in a protected left-turn phase, and what signal holds opposing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: In a protected left-turn phase you turn only on a green arrow while oncoming traffic is held by a red light.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: How does a combined protected-permissive left-turn signal cycle work?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: A protected and permissive phase alternates between a green arrow and a circular green or flashing yellow arrow, when you must pick a gap yourself.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What must you do at a steady red arrow, and whom might you still owe right-of-way when it changes?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green or a flashing yellow arrow, and you may still need to yield to pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: Which signal precedes a steady yellow arrow, what three displays can follow it, and how do you react?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow follows a green arrow and warns it will change to a circular green, a flashing yellow arrow or red, so be ready to yield or stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: Under what two conditions does a flashing yellow arrow permit you to complete your turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn in the arrow's direction, but only after a safe gap in oncoming traffic opens and while yielding to pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Even with a steady green arrow pointing your way, what two things must be true before you go?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: A green arrow lets you go the way it points, provided you are in the proper lane and no traffic or pedestrians are in your path.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: What is the key right-of-way difference between a steady green arrow and a flashing yellow arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A green arrow gives a clear path in its direction, while a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after you find a gap and yield.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does your response to a steady red arrow differ from a steady yellow arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: A steady red arrow means wait, but a steady yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and you should get ready to yield or stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Match five classic road sign shapes to their meanings: octagon, triangle, pentagon, pennant, and diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Sign shapes carry meaning: an octagon is stop, a triangle is yield, a pentagon is school, a pennant is a no passing zone and a diamond is a warning.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What categories belong to vertical rectangles, horizontal rectangles, and round or crossbuck shapes?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.memory_hook: Vertical rules, horizontal guides, round rail
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: A vertical rectangle is a regulatory sign, a horizontal rectangle is a guide sign, and a round sign or crossbuck means railroad.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What messages are carried by red, black-and-white, yellow, and fluorescent yellow-green road signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.memory_hook: Red stops, white rules, yellow-green school
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Sign colors carry meaning too: red is for stop, yield or prohibited, white and black for regulatory, yellow for warning and yellow green for school.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: What four kinds of information do orange, green, blue, and brown highway signs provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.memory_hook: Orange work, green guide, blue, brown
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Orange signs are for construction, green for direction and distance, blue for motorist services, and brown for public recreation and cultural interests.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Which two colors mark regulatory signs, and how does yellow-green differ from standard yellow?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Both white and black are listed as regulatory sign colors, while yellow green is reserved for school signs and yellow for general warnings.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How do you keep the pennant sign shape and the five-sided pentagon sign shape straight?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: A pennant shape marks a no passing zone, while a pentagon marks a school sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.front: How are typical regulatory signs colored and shaped, and which five driving rules do they govern?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.memory_hook: White boards govern lanes, turns, speed
sec08-card-sec08-F42.expected_back: Many regulatory signs are white squares or rectangles with black or red letters or symbols covering direction, lane use, turns, speed and parking.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.front: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal red slash over a black symbol send?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.expected_back: A red circle with a red slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed, such as no left turn or no U-turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: Beyond turn prohibitions, which two vehicle-type bans commonly use the red-slash prohibition design?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: No Trucks and No Bicycles are examples of prohibition signs alongside No Left Turn, No Right Turn and No U-Turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: What shape and colors identify standard warning signs, and what driver response do they call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Warning signs are usually yellow diamonds with black letters or symbols and tell you to slow down and be ready to stop for a hazard or special situation ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What upcoming traffic controls do Stop Ahead and Signal Ahead signs announce, and how should you react?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: A Stop Ahead sign means a stop sign is coming on your road, and a Signal Ahead sign means a traffic light is coming; be ready to stop for either.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: How should you adjust your driving at a School Crossing sign and at a Pedestrian Crossing sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.memory_hook: Slow down; watch kids, yield walkers
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: At a School Crossing sign, slow down and watch for children crossing, and at a Pedestrian Crossing sign, slow down and yield to people in the crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: What color transition does the Missouri guide note for School Crossing signs, and over what timeframe?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: The School Crossing sign is being changed to a yellow green color over a transition the guide says will take effect within ten years.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: How does an Added Lane warning sign differ from a Merge warning sign for incoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.memory_hook: Added gets own lane; Merge shares
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: An Added Lane sign means traffic from another road gets its own new lane, so no merge is needed, while a Merge sign means entering vehicles may move into your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: When you pass a Lane Ends Merge Left sign while driving in the right lane, what is your duty?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means two lanes become one, and a driver in the right lane must merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: What common situation do Added Lane and Merge signs both warn about, and what single detail separates them?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.memory_hook: Both warn entry; lane count differs
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: The Added Lane and Merge signs both warn of traffic entering from another road; the difference is whether the entering traffic gets its own lane or moves into yours.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.front: What does a T Intersection Ahead warning sign tell you about the road you are traveling on?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.memory_hook: Your road ends; turn either way
sec08-card-sec08-F44.expected_back: A T Intersection Ahead sign means your road ends and you must turn right or left.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: How does an Intersection warning sign differ from a Side Road Ahead warning sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.memory_hook: Crossroad cuts across; side joins one
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: An Intersection sign warns that another road crosses yours, and a Side Road Ahead sign warns that a road joins from the side the sign shows.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: What two actions does a Roundabout Ahead warning sign prompt before you reach the island?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.memory_hook: Drop to posted speed, obey circle
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: A Roundabout Ahead sign tells you to slow to the posted speed restriction and use the roundabout rules.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: What hazard does a Side Road Railroad Crossing sign alert turning motorists to watch for?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.memory_hook: Rail tracks sit right past turn
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: A Side Road Railroad Crossing sign warns that tracks cross just beside an intersection, so take care crossing them.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: What road geometry and recommended top speed go with a Reverse Turn warning sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.memory_hook: Two opposite turns, thirty or under
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: A reverse turn sign warns of two turns in opposite directions, the second possibly sharper, with a recommended top speed of thirty miles per hour or less.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: How does the recommended speed on a sharp Turn sign differ from the speed meaning of a Curve sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.memory_hook: Turn thirty max; curve below limit
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: A turn sign marks a sharp turn with a recommended maximum of thirty miles per hour or less, while a curve sign marks a curve whose recommended speed is below the posted highway limit.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: Which two bend signs share the thirty-mile-per-hour-or-less speed threshold, unlike a standard Curve sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.memory_hook: Turn and Reverse Turn cap thirty
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Turn signs and reverse turn signs both point to a top recommended speed of thirty miles per hour or less, while a curve sign only says the advised speed is below the highway's posted limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: What does an advisory speed plate beneath a bend sign tell you, especially when rain, snow, or ice hits?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.memory_hook: Advised dry speed; slower when slick
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: An advisory speed plate on a curve or turn sign gives the recommended speed, and you should never go faster than it in rain, snow or ice even if it feels safe in good weather.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: What specific speed guidance does an Exit Speed Advisory sign give freeway drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: An Exit Speed Advisory sign shows the recommended speed for a highway exit ramp.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: What message do large single turn arrows and sequential curve chevrons emphasize along a bend?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: A large arrow placed on the outside of a turn and chevron signs at curves both stress the need to slow down for a sharp change of direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: What top speed does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of farm or work gear indicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels under twenty-five miles per hour, as farm vehicles and construction equipment often do.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: What hazards do a Slippery When Wet sign and a Soft Shoulder sign warn against?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: A Slippery When Wet sign warns of a road that gets unusually slick in wet weather, and a Soft Shoulder sign means do not drive off the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: What road layout changes do Begin Divided Roadway and End Divided Roadway signs announce?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: A Begin Divided Roadway sign warns that a median or barrier will soon split the two directions of traffic, and End Divided Roadway warns that the split is ending.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: Where are roadside object markers placed, and what driving habit do they reinforce?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Object markers warn of something in the road or right at its edge, a reminder not to drift out of your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: What does a yellow Bicycle Share the Road warning sign tell motorists to expect?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: A Bicycle Share the Road sign warns that cyclists may be riding in the same lane as motor traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Which two visibility limits make night driving harder than driving in daylight?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Night driving is harder because headlights show less of the road ahead and to the sides than daylight does, and oncoming glare makes the road harder to see.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: During which daily evening-to-morning window must your headlights stay on in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Headlights must be on from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Outside nighttime hours, what everyday weather trigger legally requires turning on your headlights in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Missouri requires headlights any time the weather calls for using your windshield wipers.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: What are the two independent rules—one by time and one by weather—that mandate headlights in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Headlights are required by the clock from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, and also by the weather whenever the wipers are needed.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which three upkeep steps keep your windows and headlights ready for safe night driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Keep windows and headlights clean, make sure the lights work, and have their aim checked from time to time.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: On open dark roads, when should you switch up to your high-beam headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Use high beams whenever no vehicles are coming toward you.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: About how far ahead do headlights let you see, and how must that cap your nighttime speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Headlights let you see only about three hundred fifty feet ahead, so do not overdrive them; keep a speed at which you can stop or turn within that range.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle versus a vehicle you are following must you switch to low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Dim to low beams within five hundred feet, about one block, of an oncoming vehicle, and within three hundred feet when following another vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How do Missouri's three easy-to-confuse nighttime distances—beam reach, oncoming dim, and following dim—line up?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Three night distances are easy to mix up: headlights reach about three hundred fifty feet, you dim for oncoming traffic at five hundred feet, and you dim when following within three hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Which painted stripe should guide your eyes at night, and what roadside hazards require extra scanning?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: At night, follow the edgeline, or the center line if there is no edgeline, and watch for signs and for people and vehicles stopped beside the road.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: What speed adjustment should you make before entering curves at night if you are cruising at the posted limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Slow down for curves at night if you are already driving at the posted maximum.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: What rule does the Missouri Driver Guide give if you feel drowsy before or during a night drive?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Stay awake and alert at night and do not drive if you feel tired.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Which two visibility systems should you verify work properly before winter weather arrives?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Before winter driving, make sure the windshield wipers and defroster both work.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which surfaces must you clear of snow and ice before driving, even if you are only going a few blocks?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: In winter clear all snow and ice from the windows, headlights and taillights, and never set off, however short the trip, until the windows are clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Even with snow-rated tires or chains installed, what two winter speed rules still apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Snow-rated tires or chains help, but no vehicle can be driven safely on snow or ice at normal speeds, so slow down and do not use cruise control.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: What should you carry ready in your vehicle if it does not run snow-rated tires?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: If your vehicle lacks snow-rated tires, keep chains ready to put on in bad weather.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: How should you press the gas pedal when starting from a stop on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: When starting out on snow or ice, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: If your drive wheels spin when trying to pull out on snow, what two-step method frees the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: If your tires spin when starting on snow, rock gently back and forth to clear a path, then spread salt, sand or cat litter around the wheels if needed.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Why must bystanders stay out of line with spinning tires while freeing a stuck vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Never let anyone stand in line with spinning wheels, because they can throw gravel or ice and hurt someone.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Once rolling on a snowy or icy street, how can you check safely how slick the surface actually is?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Once moving on snow or ice, brake gently to test how slippery the road is and set your speed to match.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: About how many seconds of following distance should you leave behind the vehicle ahead on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: On snow or ice, stopping takes longer, so leave about eight to ten seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Why does Missouri jump the winter following cushion up to eight to ten seconds on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: On snow or ice the safe gap to the vehicle ahead grows to about eight to ten seconds, because stopping takes longer.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: How should you brake on slippery winter roads, and when does pumping versus checking your ABS manual apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Brake gently and smoothly on slippery roads; slamming the brakes can cause a skid, and on very slick surfaces you pump the brakes unless your manual gives anti-lock instructions.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which roadway structures ice over before regular pavement, and can plowed streets still hide ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road, and patches of ice may remain even on cleared roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Why does the Missouri guide warn against using four-wheel drive on ice, and what should you do if caught?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Do not use four-wheel drive on ice, where such vehicles can easily roll over; if you hit ice in four-wheel drive, lift your foot off the accelerator.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Why are roads extra greasy right as rain begins or under wet leaves, and how should you adjust?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: When rain starts, water mixes with road dust and oil into a slick film, wet leaves turn slippery, and stopping takes longer, so slow down and add following distance.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: How does wet pavement affect cornering through highway curves?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: Wet pavement also makes it harder to stay on the road through curves.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Why is using cruise control dangerous on wet pavement?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on wet pavement, because it keeps powering the wheels after traction is lost and can make you lose control.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What happens during hydroplaning, above what speed can it start, and when can contact vanish completely?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Hydroplaning is when tires ride on water instead of the road; it can happen at any speed over thirty-five miles per hour, and in a heavy storm tires can lose all contact at fifty-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How do Missouri's two hydroplaning speed benchmarks—thirty-five and fifty-five miles per hour—differ?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Hydroplaning can begin above thirty-five miles per hour, while full loss of road contact in a severe storm can come at fifty-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: What should you do—and avoid doing—the instant you feel your tires start to hydroplane?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: If you think you are hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and slow down without braking, which could cause a skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: Which three tire and driving habits keep your car from hydroplaning in rainy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Prevent hydroplaning with good, deep-tread tires at proper pressure, slower speeds in rain, and no cruise control.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: What is the job of four-wheel anti-lock brakes during a panic stop, and how does the pedal feel?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Four-wheel anti-lock brakes keep the wheels from locking in emergency braking, and you may feel the pedal pulse under hard braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: What pedal technique should you use with anti-lock brakes in an emergency, and how should you treat noise?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes, keep firm, steady pressure on the pedal while you steer; do not pump the brakes, and do not be alarmed by mechanical noise or slight pulsing.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How does the winter-driving section reconcile brake-pumping advice on glare ice with ABS-equipped cars?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: On very slippery surfaces the winter page says to pump the brakes, but for a vehicle with anti-lock brakes it points you to the owner's manual for special situations.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: Do front-wheel-drive and rear-wheel-drive cars start skid recovery differently, and what are the first two pedal moves?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: A skid is handled the same way in front-wheel and rear-wheel drive vehicles: lift off the accelerator and do not hit the brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: Which direction do you steer during a skid, and what wheel or brake mistakes make the spin worse?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: In a skid, gently steer in the direction the rear wheels are sliding, without braking hard or jerking the wheel, which only makes it worse.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: What four sequential stages are shown in the Missouri guide's right-sliding skid recovery sequence?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: The guide's skid diagram is captioned in four steps: before the skid, rear wheels sliding right, front wheels turned right, and the vehicle straight again.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: How should you adjust speed and headlight beams in fog, and why avoid brights?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: In fog, slow down, be ready to stop, and use low beams, because high beams make it harder to see.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: What must you do when fog thickens so badly that you can no longer see the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: If fog gets so thick that you cannot see, pull off the road, stop, and leave your lights and emergency flashers on.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: What is rule number one in any driving emergency, and why keep the ignition key on while rolling?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: The most important rule in any emergency is not to panic, and with power steering or a locking steering wheel, never turn off the ignition until fully stopped.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: What practical mental advantage does staying calm give you during a sudden roadside crisis?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Staying calm in an emergency helps you remember what to do.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: Which three mechanical actions help slow your car if the brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: If the brake pedal sinks to the floor, pump it fast and hard several times, then apply the parking brake gradually and shift to a low gear while looking for a place to stop.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How does your foot action during total brake failure contrast with an emergency stop using working ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Brake failure is the one emergency here where you pump the pedal fast and hard, which is the opposite of the steady pressure used with working anti-lock brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Once you get a car with failed brakes stopped safely off the road, may you limp it slowly to a repair shop?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: After a brake failure, get the vehicle off the road and call for help instead of driving to a garage.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: Which three sound and steering clues tell you a tire just blew out?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: A blowout may announce itself with a loud bang followed by a repeated thumping, and the steering wheel may jerk.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: How do you control a tire blowout, and when is it finally safe to touch the brake pedal?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly, lift off the accelerator without braking, and let the car slow until it is nearly stopped and off the road before braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: After coasting off-road from a blowout, what lights come on and when should you change the tire yourself?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: After a blowout, turn on the emergency flashers and change the tire only if you can do it without putting yourself in danger.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: How do you recover safely if your right tires drop off the edge of the paved road?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: If your wheels drop off the paved edge, hold the wheel tightly, ease off the gas without braking hard, and steer back once you have slowed, have control and the lane is clear.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: Which way can soft shoulder gravel tug your wheels after dropping off pavement, and how should you brake?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: When wheels run off the paved edge, they may pull to the right, so hold the wheel firmly and use only gentle braking if any is needed.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: What should you do if your steering suddenly stops responding?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: If the steering fails, lift off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow on its own without braking until nearly stopped unless you must, and turn on the flashers.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: What braking rule do tire blowouts and steering failures have in common?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: After a blowout you brake only when nearly stopped, and after a steering failure you also wait to brake until nearly stopped unless you must.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, which switches and backup lamps help you pull off?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: If the headlights fail, try the dimmer or headlight switch, then switch on parking lights, flashers or turn signals and pull off the road with the flashers left on.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: How can you see well enough to pull off safely if your hood flies up or wipers quit in heavy rain?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: If the hood flies up or the wipers fail, roll down the window to see around the blockage, turn on the flashers and pull off the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: What sequence stops your vehicle safely if the accelerator pedal sticks down?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: For a stuck accelerator, shift to neutral, brake, keep watching the road, warn others with the horn and flashers, and steer safely off the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: During a stuck-accelerator emergency, when is it finally safe to shut off the ignition?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: With a stuck accelerator, turn off the ignition only after stopping and no longer needing to steer, since turning off the key locks the steering in many vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: Where must your eyes stay focused while slowing down a car with a stuck accelerator?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: With a stuck accelerator, keep looking for a way out of traffic while you slow down.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How does braking timing for a stuck accelerator contrast with a tire blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: A stuck accelerator calls for shifting to neutral and braking right away, unlike a blowout, where you avoid the brakes at first.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: What three moves should you make—and what swerve must you avoid—when a car comes straight at you in your lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: If a vehicle comes at you head-on in your lane, slow down, pull to the right and sound your horn, but do not swerve into the left lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: Why is dodging into the left lane so deadly when an oncoming car drifts into yours?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: Swerving into the left lane to avoid a head-on vehicle is dangerous because the other driver may move back into that same lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with a train approaching, which direction do you run after getting out?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks with a train coming, unbuckle, get out and away from the tracks, running toward the direction the train is coming from to avoid flying debris.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.front: What happens if you run away in the same direction an approaching train is traveling when it hits your stalled car?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.expected_back: Running in the direction the train is heading after a stall puts you in the path of debris when the train strikes your vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: What sequence should you try if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks with no train visible?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: If you stall on the tracks with no train in sight, roll down the windows to listen, try to restart, and if that fails, shift to neutral and push the vehicle off.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.front: What instability warning and driver recommendation did the NTSB issue for twelve- and fifteen-passenger vans?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.expected_back: The NTSB has found that twelve- and fifteen-passenger vans are inherently unstable when loaded as designed with more than ten passengers, and it recommends special training for their drivers.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.front: Where does the Missouri guide direct drivers of twelve- and fifteen-passenger vans for deeper safety guidance?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.expected_back: The NTSB points drivers of large passenger vans to its website for more on van safety.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Before shifting out of park, whose seat belts and child restraints must you verify, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Buckle your own seat belt before driving and make sure every passenger uses a belt or child restraint, because belts greatly cut the chance of injury or death in a crash.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How must the lap strap and shoulder strap sit on your body, and what positions are unsafe?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Wear the lap belt low and snug across the hips with the shoulder belt across the chest, never under the arm or behind the back, and use both parts of a two-part belt.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What three crash types or control needs explain why air bags never replace wearing a seat belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Wear a belt even with air bags, since air bags do not protect you in side or rear impacts or rollovers and will not keep you behind the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: How can an inflating air bag harm an unbelted rider, and how much chest-to-wheel space does NHTSA advise?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A deploying air bag can seriously hurt or kill someone who is unbelted or badly belted, and NHTSA advises at least ten inches between the center of the breastbone and the steering wheel hub.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Up through what age should children ride in back, and where must a rear-facing infant seat never sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Children twelve and under should always ride properly restrained in a back seat, and a rear-facing infant seat must never go in front of an active passenger air bag.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Under Missouri's general adult seat belt law, which occupants of a passenger vehicle must buckle up?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Missouri law requires the driver and front seat passengers of every passenger vehicle to wear a properly adjusted, fastened seat belt.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: When a graduated intermediate license holder is driving, who inside the vehicle must be restrained?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: When an intermediate license holder is driving, every passenger in the vehicle must be properly restrained.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does Missouri's mandatory belt coverage expand when an intermediate license holder takes the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The general belt law covers the driver and front seat riders, but with an intermediate license holder at the wheel the duty extends to every passenger.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Under Missouri law, does high body weight ever excuse a child younger than four from a child restraint?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A child under four years old must ride in a suitable child restraint system no matter how much the child weighs.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What restraint rule applies to any child weighing less than forty pounds, regardless of birthday?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: A child weighing under forty pounds must ride in a suitable child restraint system no matter how old the child is.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How do the under-four-years rule and the under-forty-pounds rule interact for young Missouri riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: The two youngest restraint tiers work independently: under four years needs a child restraint at any weight, and under forty pounds needs one at any age.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Which exact age, weight, and height ranges place a Missouri child into the mandatory booster-seat tier?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: A child aged four to under eight who weighs from forty to under eighty pounds and is shorter than four feet nine inches must ride in a child restraint system or booster seat.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Reaching which age, weight, or height threshold lets a child graduate to a vehicle safety belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A child who is at least eight, at least eighty pounds, or taller than four feet nine inches must use a vehicle safety belt or a suitable booster seat.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How does the logic of Missouri's booster tier differ from graduating into the vehicle safety-belt tier?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: The booster tier needs all three conditions at once, while the safety belt tier is reached by meeting any one of eight years, eighty pounds or more than four feet nine inches.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Which two types of passenger transport are excluded from Missouri's child-restraint statute?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: The child restraint law covers transport in any motor vehicle other than a school bus or a public carrier for hire.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How should a defensive driver keep their eyes moving, and why monitor oncoming two-lane traffic closely?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Defensive drivers keep their eyes moving ahead, to the sides and behind through the mirrors every few seconds, and watch oncoming traffic, since distracted drivers crossing the center line cause many head-on crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How should you prepare for other motorists' mistakes, and what is your duty even when someone steals right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Expect other drivers to make mistakes, such as not stopping at a stop sign, plan how you would react, and never cause a crash on purpose even when someone fails to yield.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Why must you scan left and right entering an intersection even when cross streets face red lights or stop signs?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.memory_hook: Paint and bulbs cannot stop steel
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Do not count on signals or signs to stop others from crossing your path; look left and right at intersections even when cross traffic faces a red light or stop sign.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Why should you aim your gaze well down the roadway instead of staring right past your hood?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Look well down the road, not just right in front of the hood, to spot places you will need to steer or slow before you reach them.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What body, arm, foot, and hand positions make up proper Missouri driving posture?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.memory_hook: Upright back, bent elbows, both hands
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Good posture means sitting straight and relaxed against the seat, close enough to reach the pedals but with elbows still in front of you, both feet near the controls and both hands on the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Where on the steering wheel clock face does the Missouri guide tell you to place your left and right hands?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Hold the wheel with your left hand between the seven and nine o'clock positions and your right hand between three and five o'clock.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: What practical steering benefit comes from holding the lower left and right clock zones on the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: The seven-to-nine and three-to-five hand positions are comfortable and let you make most turns without letting go of the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Which steering method should you use around corners, what habit is banned, and how do you straighten out?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Steer around corners with the hand-over-hand method rather than palming the wheel with one hand, and straighten the wheel by hand after the turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your car is rolling?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Never turn the ignition key to the lock position while the vehicle is moving, because the steering wheel will lock when you turn it and you will lose control.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What single following mistake causes the frequent rear-end collisions seen on everyday roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Rear-end crashes are very common and are caused by drivers following so closely that they cannot stop when the car ahead stops suddenly.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: How do you apply Missouri's three-second rule to check whether you are following too closely?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Under the three second rule, start counting when the car ahead passes a fixed object, and if you reach the object before you count to three, you are too close.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What two smooth habits help the driver behind you maintain a safe following cushion?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Help the driver behind keep a safe gap by holding a steady speed and signaling early before you slow down.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: How should you respond to a tailgater on a multi-lane road versus on a single-lane stretch?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: If a tailgater follows you and there is a right lane, move into it; if not, wait for clear road and slow down gradually, never braking suddenly.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: When your slower pace stacks cars behind you on a two-lane road, how should you clear the queue?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: If you are slowing others down, pull aside when safe to let them pass, using turnouts on some two-lane roads; other two-lane roads may offer passing lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: What should you do before backing into a parallel parking space when cars are following right behind you?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: If traffic is behind you when you want to parallel park, signal, pull up beside the space and wait for the traffic to pass before you back in.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Where should you pull your car whenever picking up or dropping off riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Pick a safe spot out of traffic to pick up or drop off passengers.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: How should you position your vehicle relative to side-by-side cars, the center line, and your own lane stripes?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Avoid driving alongside other vehicles on multi-lane roads, keep away from oncoming traffic by not crowding the center line, and generally stay in the middle of your lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: What two sudden hazards explain keeping extra side clearance beside a line of parked cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Keep a wider gap from parked cars, because someone may step out of or between them, or one may pull out.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: When oncoming ramp traffic is merging onto your multi-lane highway and the next lane left is open, what helps?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: When traffic is merging onto a multi-lane road and the lane beside you is empty, move over a lane to make room.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: How do you separate two simultaneous hazards like an oncoming car and a bicyclist ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Give pedestrians and cyclists, especially children, extra room, and take hazards one at a time, for example letting an oncoming car pass before you overtake a cyclist.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which two distances add together into total stopping distance, and what three factors stretch it out?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Stopping distance is reaction distance plus braking distance, and speed, fatigue or poor brakes all increase it.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What happens during reaction distance, and how many seconds of reaction time does Missouri's chart assume?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Reaction distance is how far you travel between seeing a danger and braking, and the guide's chart assumes a reaction time of one point five seconds.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What does braking distance measure, and what four ideal conditions does the handbook chart assume?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Braking distance is how far you travel from applying the brakes to a full stop, and the chart assumes good brakes, tires, weather and road.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Which piece of stopping distance happens before your foot hits the brake versus after?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Reaction distance is covered before you touch the brake, while braking distance is covered after; together they make stopping distance.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: What default assumption do nearby drivers make about your car, and why signal before slowing or turning?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Other drivers expect you to keep doing what you are doing, so warn them before you change direction or slow down to give them time to react.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Before which four maneuvers should you signal, even when the street looks completely empty?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.memory_hook: Signal every move, empty streets too
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Signal before changing lanes, turning, merging or parking, and do it every time you change direction even if no one seems to be around.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: At least how far ahead should you signal a turn, and when should you delay flipping the blinker on?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet ahead, but if streets, driveways or entrances lie between you and your turn, wait until you pass them before signaling.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What intermediate features or waiting vehicles create an exception to Missouri's hundred-foot turn-signal rule?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: The signaling rule of at least one hundred feet has an exception: hold the signal until you pass any streets, driveways or entrances before your turn, or a vehicle about to enter between you and the turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: Why must you verify your turn signal has turned off after finishing a lane change or turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: After a turn or lane change make sure the signal has shut off, because a signal left blinking can make others think you will turn again.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: When does a car's turn signal stalk often fail to click off automatically, and how do you fix it?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: A turn signal may not cancel itself after a small turn, so switch it off by hand if it has not clicked off.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: What is the sole legitimate reason to tap your horn, and why skip needless honking?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: The only reason to sound your horn is to warn other drivers, and needless honking can distract others and cause a crash.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: May you ever use your vehicle's horn to vent anger or frustration at slow traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: The horn is never for showing anger or frustration.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: When is driving slower than a posted minimum speed illegal, and which three conditions excuse it?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Driving below a posted minimum speed in normal conditions is illegal, though bad weather, heavy traffic or a bad road can justify going slower.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Even where no minimum speed sign exists, what makes driving too slowly illegal, and how do you clear queues?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: Even with no posted minimum, it is illegal to drive so slowly that you block traffic, and if vehicles line up behind you, pull over and let them pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Compare what justifies dropping below a posted minimum with what makes slow driving illegal on unposted roads?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Going below a posted minimum is excused only by bad weather, heavy traffic or a bad road, while blocking traffic by slow driving is illegal even with no minimum posted.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: What engine, garage, and window habits protect occupants from carbon monoxide poisoning while parked?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: Avoid carbon monoxide by never running the engine in a garage or in a parked car with the windows shut, including running the heater or air conditioner.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: Which two precautions block deadly carbon monoxide fumes while driving in traffic or maintaining your car?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Carbon monoxide from the engine is a deadly gas, so close the vents when following closely behind another vehicle and never drive with a broken muffler or exhaust.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: Why should spotting a single deer, or even roadkill, near fields or streams make you slow down immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Deer rarely travel alone, so if you see one crossing or a struck deer by the road, expect more nearby, especially near fields, streams and gardens.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: In which months and during what daily light windows do most Missouri deer collisions occur?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: Most deer crashes happen in January, May and October through December, and the riskiest times are sunset to midnight and around sunrise.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: How do posted deer signs and fastened seat belts work together in rural wildlife corridors?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: Take extra care where deer crossing signs are posted, and keep everyone belted and children in car seats to reduce injury if a deer crash happens.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: When oncoming lanes are empty at night, how do high-beam headlights help prevent deer strikes?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: At night with no oncoming traffic, use high beams, which light up the eyes of deer near the road and give you more time to react.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: If a deer jumps directly in front of your bumper and impact cannot be avoided, why hold your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: If hitting a deer cannot be avoided, do not swerve, because leaving the road or crossing into oncoming traffic raises the risk of injury.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: What mirror check comes before braking hard for a deer, and what physics danger does nose-dive braking create?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Before slowing hard for a deer, make sure no one is behind you; heavy braking can dip the front end so the deer's body comes through into the passenger area.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: Which three parties or agencies enter the picture after colliding with a deer in Missouri?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: After a deer crash, report it to local law enforcement, get a police report if your insurer needs one, and tell a local Department of Conservation agent where it happened.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Where do you look up your car's recommended tire pressure, and how do you adjust it accurately?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: Read the right tire pressure in the owner's manual or on the driver's door jamb, check it with a gauge, and add or release air until it matches.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: On what routine schedule should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Check tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long trip.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: What three calm steps should you take as soon as police lights flash in your mirror?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: When emergency lights appear behind you, stay calm, signal, and pull off or to the side as soon as it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.front: Once pulled over for a traffic stop, what five actions keep the encounter calm and clear?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.expected_back: Once stopped, turn off the engine and radio, stay inside unless told to get out, keep your hands on the wheel, and do not use phones or search for documents until the officer asks.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.front: What three things should you ask your passengers to do during a roadside police stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.expected_back: Ask passengers at a traffic stop to stay calm, remain in the vehicle and keep their hands where the officer can see them.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.front: After pulling over for an officer at night, what cabin switch should you flip on and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.expected_back: At night an officer may shine a spotlight on your car, so turn on the interior lights once you stop to help the officer see inside.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.front: If there is a firearm or weapon inside your vehicle during a stop, when should you inform the officer?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.expected_back: If there is a weapon in the vehicle, tell the officer when the officer first makes contact.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.front: How should you reach out-of-reach registration papers, and what may you expect from an out-of-uniform officer?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.expected_back: Tell the officer where your documents are before reaching for them if they are out of reach, and expect an officer out of uniform to show credentials, which you may also request.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.front: If an officer asks you to exit your car during a stop, what two safety habits apply?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.memory_hook: Stand clear of traffic, hands out
sec10-card-sec10-R27.expected_back: If asked to step out of the vehicle, stay well away from traffic and keep your hands visible.

sec10-card-sec10-F43.front: What does signing a traffic ticket legally mean, what can refusal cause, and where do you dispute it?
sec10-card-sec10-F43.expected_back: Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, but refusing to sign it may lead to arrest; contest it in court rather than arguing at the roadside.

sec10-card-sec10-R28.front: If you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop, how and where should you follow up?
sec10-card-sec10-R28.expected_back: If you think an officer acted improperly, record what happened and report it promptly to that officer's agency, whose name and the officer's name appear on the ticket or can be requested.

sec10-card-sec10-R29.front: Which three constitutional protections remain yours throughout any traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R29.expected_back: During a traffic stop you keep constitutional rights, including freedom from unreasonable search and seizure, the right to remain silent and the right to an attorney.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What everyday factors can weaken your driving ability, and whose job is it to tell when you shouldn't get behind the wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Alcohol, drugs, even medicine, and being tired can all weaken your driving, and you are the one responsible for knowing when you are not fit to drive.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Before taking your first drink, what should you do with your car keys, and why?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Even a little alcohol may affect your driving, so if you plan to drink, hand the keys to someone who has not been drinking.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: What specific mental and physical effects can alcohol trigger that make safe driving harder?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Alcohol can also cause drowsiness, weaker concentration and attention, poorer coordination and comprehension, and worse decisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: How quickly can just one or two drinks impair your driving or push you past Missouri's legal limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: Even one drink will probably affect your driving, and in many cases two drinks could put you over the legal limit.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: What Blood Alcohol Content percentages make driving illegal in Missouri for standard drivers, commercial drivers, and drivers under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more, with zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Why can't you memorize just a single BAC percentage for every motorist on Missouri roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: The legal BAC limit depends on the driver: zero point zero eight percent for most drivers, zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers, and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: Which substances or combinations can get you charged with DWI in Missouri if they impair your driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: In Missouri you can be charged with DWI for driving impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medicine, over-the-counter medicine, or any mix of them.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: Does Missouri law separate prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs, or soften DWI penalties when drugs cause the impairment?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Missouri law does not separate prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs, and DWI penalties are the same whether alcohol or drugs caused the impairment.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What roadside exercises might an officer ask you to perform if drinking is suspected, and what do they help decide?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: An officer who suspects drinking may ask you to do field tests such as walking heel to toe or balancing on one leg, which help the officer decide whether to arrest you.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Once you are arrested for suspected impaired driving, which three samples can measure your Blood Alcohol Content?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: After an arrest, a chemical test of your breath, blood or urine gives your Blood Alcohol Content, called the BAC level.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: What happens to your Missouri driver license if you refuse an officer's request for a chemical BAC test?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: If you refuse a chemical test of your BAC when stopped by an officer, your license is taken away for one year.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Which two independent legal tracks can penalize an impaired driver in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Missouri can act against an impaired driver in two separate ways, administrative actions and court-convicted actions, and each has its own penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What does the officer do right away if your chemical test hits zero point zero eight percent—or zero point zero two for a minor?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: If your BAC is point zero eight percent or more, or point zero two percent or more for a minor, the officer takes your license and gives you a notice that it will be suspended or revoked after fifteen days.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What temporary driving paper can that arrest notice include, and what two requests does it let you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: That notice may include a fifteen-day driving permit if the officer marks it, and it lets you ask for a hearing or, if eligible, an immediate ninety-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: If you are granted an administrative hearing after a failed BAC test, how long may you keep driving legally?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: If you are granted a hearing, you may keep driving legally until fifteen days after the decision is mailed to you.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How do the two separate fifteen-day clocks on the arrest notice rules differ from each other?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Two different fifteen-day periods appear on the arrest notice page: the license is lost fifteen days after the notice, and with a hearing you may drive until fifteen days after the decision is mailed.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Under Missouri's administrative actions, what license penalty hits on a first offense versus a second offense within five years?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: On the administrative chart, a first offense brings a license suspension, and a second offense within a five-year period brings a one-year license revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: When an administrative action entry in the Missouri guide is marked with an asterisk, what must you install before reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Administrative entries marked with an asterisk require an Ignition Interlock Device to be installed before the license is reinstated.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: After a judge finds you guilty of DWI or illegal BAC, when does your legal driving stop and how do you find out?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: If a judge finds you guilty of DWI or of a BAC of point zero eight percent or more, you can no longer drive legally once the ticket reaches the Department, and you are told by mail when to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: After a court conviction for impaired driving, what determines whether your license is suspended, revoked, or denied, and what hits your record?
