sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: After a court conviction, your license is suspended, revoked or denied depending on your past driving record, and points are added to that record.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What license suspension follows a first court-convicted impaired driving offense, and what restricted option might apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: For a first court-convicted offense the license is suspended for ninety days, and you may qualify for a ninety-day or sixty-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What license loss comes with a second court-convicted offense overall, versus a second offense within five years?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: A second court-convicted offense brings a one-year revocation, while a second offense within five years brings a five-year license denial.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: How long is your license denied after a third—or any subsequent—court-convicted impaired driving offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: A third court-convicted offense, and any later one, brings a ten-year license denial.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Which BAC convictions count toward triggering Missouri's five-year license denial?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Only a BAC conviction dated August twenty-eight, two thousand nine or later can be counted toward a five-year license denial.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: What three major types of punishment can follow a guilty verdict for drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Being found guilty of drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri can bring a fine, a lost license, and even jail.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: If you hurt or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs, what jail, fine, and license penalties can you face?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: If you injure or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs, you may face two to seven years in jail, a five thousand dollars fine, and or or losing your license for five years.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Up to how much jail time and fine money can a first DWI or BAC conviction carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: A first DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to six months in jail and a fine of up to five hundred dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: How does the alcohol-effects section summarize the three parts of DWI punishment?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: The effects page restates the DWI punishment as up to six months in prison, a fine of up to five hundred dollars, and loss of driving privileges.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Up to how much jail time and fine money can a second DWI or BAC conviction bring?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: A second DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to one year in jail and a fine of up to one thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What maximum jail term and fine apply to a third DWI or BAC conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: A third DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to four years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What maximum jail time and fine can hit on a fourth DWI or BAC conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: A fourth DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to seven years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What prison sentence range applies to a fifth DWI or BAC offense in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: A fifth DWI or BAC offense can mean between five and fifteen years in jail.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: At what ages is possessing or purchasing alcohol illegal in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: It is illegal for anyone under twenty-one to possess or buy alcohol in Missouri.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Under Missouri's Abuse and Lose Law, what triggers a ninety-day license loss for a driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Under the Abuse and Lose Law, a driver younger than twenty-one can lose the license for ninety days for any alcohol-related traffic offense, for having or using alcohol or drugs while driving, or for altering or misrepresenting a license.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What happens under Abuse and Lose if a driver under eighteen has or uses alcohol and faces a second offense charge?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: A driver under eighteen who has or uses alcohol and is charged with a second offense can also lose the license for ninety days under Abuse and Lose.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: How long can a driver aged twenty-one or older lose their license for having or using drugs while driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: A driver aged twenty-one or older can lose the license for one year for having or using drugs while driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: What four requirements must you complete to regain your license after that one-year drug-related loss?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: To get the license back after that one-year loss, you pay a forty-five dollars fee, show you completed SATOP or a similar program, keep SR-twenty-two proof of insurance for two years, and retake the full driver exam.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How does the Abuse and Lose license loss length compare between drivers under twenty-one and drivers twenty-one or older with drugs?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Abuse and Lose takes the license for ninety days from a driver under twenty-one, but for a full year from a driver twenty-one or older who has or uses drugs while driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: For someone over fifteen and under twenty-one, which four liquor-related actions let a state court suspend or revoke a license?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: A state court can suspend or revoke the license of someone older than fifteen and under twenty-one for buying or trying to buy liquor, possessing it, being visibly intoxicated, or having a BAC above point zero two percent.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Under Missouri's underage liquor rules, how is drinking alcohol treated in relation to possessing it?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: For a young person, drinking liquor counts as possessing it.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: What are the three escalating license penalties for first, second, and third Minor in Possession offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Minor in Possession penalties climb with each offense: a thirty-day suspension, then a ninety-day suspension, then a one-year revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What must you complete after any Minor in Possession action, and what two extra steps apply after a one-year revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: After a Minor in Possession action you pay a forty-five dollars fee and attend SATOP or a similar program, and after a one-year revocation you also file SR-twenty-two proof for two years and retake the driver exam.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does a first Minor in Possession suspension length compare against an Abuse and Lose license loss?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: A first Minor in Possession offense brings a thirty-day suspension, which is shorter than the ninety-day loss under Abuse and Lose.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: What three core requirements get your license reinstated after an intoxication-related offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: To be reinstated after an intoxication-related offense you pay a forty-five dollars fee, show SATOP or a similar program was completed, and keep SR-twenty-two proof of insurance for two years.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: Where must a driver facing DWI or BAC consequences file proof of insurance, and what form is typically used?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: A driver facing DWI or BAC consequences must file proof of insurance with the Driver License Bureau, most often through an SR-twenty-two insurance filing.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: How long must proof of insurance remain on file, and what happens if coverage lapses early?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Proof of insurance must stay on file for two years; if it lapses, the license is suspended for the rest of that period unless you file again and pay a twenty dollars fee.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Which specific driver is exempt from the two-year proof-of-insurance rule after an alcohol action?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: The one exception to the proof rule is a minor whose first offense is a BAC of point zero two percent or more, who is not required to file it.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: Which three situations require you to use an ignition interlock on every vehicle you drive for at least six months after reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: You must run an ignition interlock device on any vehicle you drive for at least six months after reinstatement if you had more than one intoxication-related contact, a BAC conviction of point one five percent or higher, or caused property damage or injury.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: Which three vehicle systems is an ignition interlock wired into, and when must you blow into it?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: An ignition interlock device is wired to the ignition, horn and headlights and checks breath alcohol, requiring a breath sample before the engine starts and at intervals while driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: How long must a required interlock stay installed, what must the final stretch show, and who covers the cost?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: The interlock must stay in place at least six months from reinstatement with no violations during the final three months, and you pay for its installation and its monthly service.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Can an ignition interlock be required for longer than six months after reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Six months is the least time an interlock must stay installed after reinstatement, but a court may order a device for longer than six months.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Even when licensing rules don't mandate one, can a court order an ignition interlock after a first DWI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: A court may also require an interlock after a first DWI conviction, beyond what the licensing rules require.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: What happens if you fail to maintain a required ignition interlock, and how do you lift that suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: If you fail to keep the interlock, your driving privilege is suspended again until the device is serviced or installed and proof is sent to the Driver License Bureau.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How does Missouri's forty-five-dollar fee differ from the twenty-dollar interlock fee?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: The forty-five dollars fee is the reinstatement fee after an intoxication-related offense, while a separate twenty dollars fee applies when reinstating after the interlock was not maintained.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: What license revocations hit on a first versus second court conviction for failing to install a required interlock?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: A court conviction for failing to install a required interlock revokes your driving privilege for one year, and a second offense takes it away for five years.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Which two alcohol-enforcement violations both carry a one-year loss of driving privilege?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Refusing a chemical test and being convicted of not installing a required interlock both cost one year of driving privilege.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: Can prescription or over-the-counter medicine taken exactly as directed still impair driving, and what two checks should you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can impair driving even when taken as directed, so ask your doctor or pharmacist and read the warning label.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: What common side effect of over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines can compromise safe driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: Cold and allergy medicines bought over the counter can make you drowsy and hurt your driving.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: Why are pep pills, uppers, and diet pills risky for drivers once their brief alertness boost wears off?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: Pep pills, uppers and diet pills may make a driver more alert for a short time but later can cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration and vision problems.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: What is the rule when a medicine bottle warns that it may cause drowsiness or dizziness?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: Do not take any drug whose label warns that it may cause drowsiness or dizziness before you drive.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: What does Missouri say about taking someone else's prescription or combining different medicines?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: Taking a medicine prescribed for someone else is both dangerous and illegal, and you should not mix medicines unless your doctor tells you to.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.front: Why must you never mix alcohol with any medicine before driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.expected_back: Never combine alcohol with any medicine, because many drugs have unexpected side effects when taken with alcohol.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.front: Where does marijuana rank among substances cited in motor vehicle crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.expected_back: Marijuana is the drug cited second most often in car crashes, after alcohol.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.front: Does Missouri's voter-approved medical marijuana law make driving under the influence of cannabis legal or safe?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.expected_back: Missouri voters approved medical marijuana effective in two thousand twenty, yet driving under its influence is never legal or safe.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.front: Which driving skills does marijuana impair, and what two specific on-road problems do studies link to it?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.expected_back: Marijuana can impair thinking, judgment of time and distance, and coordination, and studies link it to more lane weaving and slower reactions.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.front: What did studies find when drivers combined alcohol with marijuana instead of using marijuana alone?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.expected_back: Drivers who used alcohol together with marijuana were even more impaired, with still more lane weaving, than with marijuana alone.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.front: How does the Missouri Driver Guide define a substance use disorder?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.expected_back: A substance use disorder is repeated alcohol or drug use that causes serious problems such as health issues, disability, or failing duties at work, school or home.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.front: What elevated danger do individuals with a substance use disorder face on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.expected_back: People with a substance use disorder are at greater risk of hurting themselves or others in a motor vehicle crash.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.front: What national resource offers help for substance use disorders, and what are its cost, privacy, and hours?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.expected_back: Help for a substance use disorder is available through the free, confidential SAMHSA National Helpline, open around the clock every day of the year.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.front: Why is starting alcohol or drugs at a young age one of the strongest predictors of future addiction?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.expected_back: Early use is one of the strongest predictors of addiction, because a young brain that is still developing can be damaged faster and more severely than an adult brain.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What credential is required to operate a motor vehicle or motor-driven cycle on Missouri public roads, and where is it issued?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Driving a motor vehicle or a motor-driven cycle on Missouri public roads requires a valid driver license, which any Missouri license office can issue.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: At what age does a Missouri resident need a state license to drive, and what rule applies to new residents with out-of-state cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: A Missouri resident who is at least sixteen years old and plans to drive needs a Missouri license, and so does a new resident who wants to drive, even while holding another state's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Within what timeframe must an out-of-state commercial driver who moves to Missouri get a Missouri license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: An out-of-state commercial driver who moved to Missouri within the last thirty days must obtain a Missouri license, as explained in the separate commercial manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which two groups holding a valid license from their home state are exempt from needing a Missouri license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Members of the armed forces and full-time students who hold a valid license from their home state do not need a Missouri license.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Do you need a Missouri driver license to move a farm tractor or implement along a highway for agricultural work?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Moving or operating a farm tractor or farm implement on a highway for agricultural work, even briefly, does not call for a Missouri license.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What three rules apply to carrying, presenting, and sharing your license or permit whenever you drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: You must carry your license or permit whenever you drive, show it when a law enforcement officer asks, and never let another person use it.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: At what age can you get an instruction permit, which GDL stage is it, and how may you drive on it?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The instruction permit, available at age fifteen, is the first step of the Graduated Driver License (GDL) program and lets a young person learn while supervised by a licensed adult.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: When does the required six-month instruction-permit holding period before an intermediate license start counting?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: The six-month permit period needed before an intermediate license only begins once the temporary instruction permit has been issued.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: What special identifier appears on every Missouri permit issued to someone younger than twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Every permit issued to someone younger than twenty-one carries a marking that identifies the holder as a minor.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: At what age does the Class F intermediate license open, and what kind of driving privileges does this second GDL step grant?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: The intermediate license (Class F), available at sixteen, is the second GDL step and gives a young driver restricted privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: At what age does the full Class F license open, and which motor vehicles does this basic operator card cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: The full Class F license, available at eighteen, is the basic operator license and is required for any motor vehicle that does not call for a Class A, B, C or E license.
pills: NOT A B C OR E

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: On Missouri's licensing ladder, which credential opens at age sixteen and which two open at age eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: On the license ladder the intermediate Class F license opens at sixteen, while both the full Class F license and the Class E for-hire license open at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: Once you turn twenty-one with a minor-marked license, what two options do you have for that card?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.memory_hook: Buy replacement or use until expiry
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: The minor marking also appears on licenses issued before twenty-one; once you turn twenty-one you may buy a replacement without it or simply use the old one until it expires.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: What single factor sets your Missouri permit or license fee and how long the card stays valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Permit and license fees and how long the credential lasts depend on the applicant's age on the day of the transaction.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What prices and validity lengths does the fee chart list for an age-fifteen instruction permit versus a student permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: The fee chart lists the instruction permit at age fifteen for ten dollars, valid up to twelve months, and the student permit at fifteen for one dollar for the length of the approved course.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What minimum age, dollar fee, and maximum validity period appear on the chart for an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: The fee chart lists the intermediate license at minimum age sixteen for fourteen dollars, valid up to two years.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: Starting at age eighteen, what two term lengths and prices does the chart list for a full Class F license?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: The fee chart lists the full Class F license at minimum age eighteen for sixteen dollars and fifty cents for up to three years or thirty-three dollars for up to six years.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: When does a Class F license let you ride a motorcycle, and which four checks are required to earn Class F?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: A Class F license does not cover motorcycles unless it shows the M endorsement, and getting one requires passing the Class F written, vision, road sign and driving tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What minimum age and credential let you ride a motorcycle or motortricycle, and which Class M ages follow GDL rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.memory_hook: Class M sixteen, teens follow GDL
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A Class M license, available at sixteen, or a license with the M endorsement is needed to ride a motorcycle or motortricycle on public roads, and GDL rules apply to Class M applicants aged sixteen to eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: What three steps must you complete for a fifteen-and-a-half motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A motorcycle instruction permit at age fifteen and a half (fifteen years and one hundred eighty-two days) requires a completed approved rider training course, passing the Class F and Class M written, vision and road sign tests, and written parent or guardian consent.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which four riding restrictions limit a fifteen-and-a-half-year-old motorcycle instruction permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: The age fifteen and a half motorcycle permit allows daylight riding only, within fifty miles of home, on a motorcycle of two hundred fifty cubic centimeters or less, with no passengers.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Once you turn sixteen, is the rider training course required for a motorcycle permit, and who must take both written tests?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: From age sixteen the rider training course is not required for a motorcycle instruction permit, but an applicant without a valid driver license must still take the Class F and Class M written tests.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Which exact motorcycle permit age bracket makes an approved rider training course mandatory?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Rider training is mandatory only for the motorcycle instruction permit taken at fifteen and a half; an applicant aged sixteen or older can get that permit without the course.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: What fees apply to a motorcycle permit, and how does its maximum length compare with a regular instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The motorcycle permit costs twelve dollars and seventy-five cents or ten dollars depending on the starting age and lasts up to six months (one hundred eighty-two days), half the twelve-month term of the regular instruction permit shown on the same chart.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: Does riding a motorized bicycle require an M endorsement, and what license must the rider hold?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: A motorized bicycle needs no motorcycle endorsement, though its rider must carry a valid operator license or a higher class.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: At what age does Class E open, what exams are required, and which test does a current Class F holder skip?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: The Class E for-hire license, available at eighteen, has a written exam drawn from the whole guide but mostly Chapter fifteen, plus vision and road sign tests; a current Class F holder skips the driving test, and an eighteen-year-old must still meet the under-twenty-one requirements.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which paid passenger-carrying or property-hauling jobs require a Missouri Class E license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Class E applies when you are paid to drive a vehicle carrying fourteen or fewer passengers, or you haul property for pay or as part of your job.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: When does regularly driving someone else's freight vehicle for work call for a Class E license instead of a CDL?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Class E also applies when your job has you regularly drive someone else's freight vehicle rated twenty-six thousand pounds GVWR or less that needs no hazardous-materials placard.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Which ride-share, taxi, and food-delivery drivers are exempt from needing a Class E for-hire license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Class E is not required for eligible ride-share (Transportation Network Company) or taxi drivers using vehicles of twelve thousand pounds gross weight or less, or for prepared-food delivery drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What minimum age applies to a Missouri CDL, and what higher age applies to Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsements?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: A commercial driver license requires age eighteen, and a CDL with a Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsement requires age twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How does the starting age for a Class M motorcycle license compare with base CDL and hazmat or bus endorsement ages?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A Class M motorcycle license can be held from sixteen, but a commercial license waits until eighteen, and its Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsement until twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: When does a Missouri nondriver ID normally expire, and how does age seventy or REAL ID status affect that term?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: A nondriver ID expires on your birthday in the sixth year after you apply, and applicants aged seventy or older get a non-expiring card, though a REAL ID applicant of that age may get a six-year card and immigration document review can shorten the term.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: At what minimum age can someone get a nondriver ID strictly for voting, and how much does it cost?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A nondriver ID card used only for voting can be issued from age seventeen and a half and costs zero dollars on the fee chart.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Can you legally drive using only the Missouri State Highway Patrol examination record before visiting a license office?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: The driver examination record from the Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) is not a permit or license; you bring it and your documents to a license office to be issued the actual credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Which four separate screenings make up the complete examination for a brand-new Missouri driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: A new Missouri license requires the four-part examination: a written test, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: When a new resident transfers a valid out-of-state license, which checks are taken and what happens to old out-of-state cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A new resident transferring an out-of-state license surrenders that license, takes only the vision and road sign tests, and every license, permit or ID from the other state becomes invalid.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does the required screening list differ between a brand-new driver and someone transferring a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: A brand-new applicant takes all four tests, but a newcomer transferring a valid out-of-state license takes just the vision and road sign tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Besides first-time licensing, which three expiration, revocation, or administrative situations require all four exam parts?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: The four-part exam is also required when a Missouri license or an out-of-state license has been expired more than one hundred eighty-four days, after a revocation for too many points or an Administrative Alcohol Revocation, or when the Director of Revenue asks you to take it.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How many days does the Missouri guide equate to six months when deciding whether a lapsed license needs all four exam parts?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: For a lapsed Missouri license the guide treats six months and one hundred eighty-four days as the same window: beyond it, the full four-part exam applies again.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which age span falls under Missouri's GDL program, and what five core identity and residency facts must applicants prove?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Drivers aged fifteen to twenty-one fall under the GDL program and must prove lawful status, identity with full legal name and date of birth, Social Security number, any name change, and Missouri residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Which documents prove U.S. citizen lawful status at a Missouri license office, and which two birth papers are rejected?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A U.S. citizen proves lawful status with a certified birth certificate bearing a vital records seal, a valid U.S. passport, or a certificate of citizenship, naturalization or birth abroad; hospital certificates and birth registration cards are refused.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Which Missouri credential type accepts a vital-records birth certificate copy paired with a military ID or discharge papers, and which refuses it?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A vital-records copy of a birth certificate paired with a military ID card or discharge papers proves lawful status for a standard card but not for a REAL ID-compliant one.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.front: How do acceptable documents for proving a changed last name differ from proving a changed first or middle name?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.expected_back: To prove a new last name you can bring a certified marriage license, divorce decree, court order, adoption papers or an amended birth certificate, but a first- or middle-name change is proven only by a certified court order.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which four documents can prove your required Social Security number on a Missouri license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: State law requires your Social Security number on the application, proven by an original signed unlaminated card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine, or a paystub showing your name and number.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: What document must an applicant without a Social Security number bring, and which foreign student group is exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: Without a Social Security number you bring a status letter from the Social Security Administration, except a nonimmigrant foreign student with an F or J classification who is not authorized to work.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.front: When might a Missouri license clerk let you state your Social Security number aloud instead of handing over paper proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.expected_back: Applicants who already verified their Social Security number on a current Missouri credential may be allowed to state the number aloud instead of showing a document.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.front: What extra review step can apply when someone files a Missouri credential application without a Social Security number?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.expected_back: An application filed without a Social Security number may go to the central office for final approval before the card is printed and mailed.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What four examples of everyday records can prove your Missouri residential address at the counter?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Missouri residency can be shown with items such as two current utility bills, a property tax receipt, a voter ID card, or an official government letter on letterhead dated within the last ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Between government letterhead mail and utility bills used for residency proof, which carries a strict ninety-day limit?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The ninety-day age limit applies to official government letters used as residency proof, while utility bills simply have to be current.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: How many residency documents are needed for a REAL ID versus a standard card, and what if your mailing address differs?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: A REAL ID-compliant card needs two residency documents, a non-REAL ID card needs one, and a separate mailing address needs its own proof.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: May a post office box serve as your Missouri residential address, and where does the state send your finished card?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: A post office box cannot serve as a residential address, and the license is mailed to the address you give.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: How does the Missouri driver guide define a person's residential address?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: The guide defines a residential address as your true, fixed and permanent principal home, the place you intend to come back to even while living somewhere else for now.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: If an applicant under twenty-one lacks address paperwork, how can a parent's document help on standard versus REAL ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: An applicant under twenty-one without an acceptable address document may use one supplied by a parent or legal guardian, but for REAL ID it counts as only one of the two residency proofs.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: Which core documents, along with your old card, can you be asked to present again when renewing a Missouri credential?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Renewing a license, nondriver ID or instruction permit can require showing the lawful status, identity, Social Security, name-change and residency proofs again, plus the previous license.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Who is allowed to skip place-of-birth paperwork when renewing a Missouri permit, license, or nondriver ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: Someone aged sixty-five or older renewing a non-REAL ID non-commercial permit, license or nondriver ID may skip the place-of-birth documents.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Which two driver situations can lead to a restricted Missouri license, and what might removing a restriction require?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: A driver with limited experience or a medical condition affecting safe driving may get a restricted license, and removing a restriction can require a driving test.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: Which three public-safety, court, or medical roles may request adding a restriction onto your Missouri card?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: A law enforcement officer, a judge or a physician may ask the Department to add a restriction to your license.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: What criminal charge and record penalty can hit you for ignoring a restriction printed on your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Ignoring a restriction can bring a charge of driving without a license and, on conviction, points on your record.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What driving limits do Missouri restriction letters A, C, F, G, and I each represent?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: Among the restriction codes, A means corrective lenses, C daylight driving only, F a limit of forty-five miles per hour, G a twenty-five mile radius and I the intermediate license.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: What do restriction letters Q and U indicate on a Missouri driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Restriction code Q signals more than five restrictions, and code U marks an uncoded restriction whose wording appears on the back of the card when space allows.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: How do license endorsements work compared with restrictions, and what two privileges does the guide give as examples?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: Endorsements work opposite to restrictions: they add privileges such as driving a school bus or a motorcycle to a Class F, E or M license.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: Which recent medical episodes within six months before applying can trigger a required physician's statement?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: A physician's statement can be required if you had epileptic seizures, convulsions or blackouts in the six months before applying.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.front: Who can report doubts about a driver's medical fitness to drive, and what state report is used?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.expected_back: Examiners, license clerks, relatives, police officers and the listed health professionals who doubt your medical fitness to drive report it on the Driver Condition Report, Form four thousand three hundred nineteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What trip purpose and passenger-capacity threshold require a Missouri school bus S endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: A school bus (S) endorsement is needed to carry students between home, school and school-sponsored events in any vehicle built for more than ten passengers.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What minimum age and underlying license credentials qualify a driver to earn the school bus endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Only drivers who are at least twenty-one and already carry either a Class E for-hire license or a commercial license bearing the Passenger (P) endorsement can receive the school bus endorsement.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What penalty can hit your school bus endorsement if you fail a drug, alcohol, or chemical check under school bus law?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Failing a drug, alcohol or chemical test given under school bus law can suspend the school bus endorsement for one year.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: At age seventy-five and up, how frequently must a school-bus driver retest behind-the-wheel bus skills?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older must pass school bus skills testing every two years to keep it.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which four screenings must you pass to add the M endorsement onto an existing Missouri driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Beyond school bus and motorcycle, which credential holders are the only drivers eligible for extra endorsements?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: Endorsements beyond school bus and motorcycle are available only to holders of a commercial driver license or commercial learner's permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Where does the Department mail license renewal reminders, and which two learner permits receive no reminder?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: The Department mails a renewal reminder to the mailing address on your record, but none is sent for a temporary instruction permit or a commercial learner's permit.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: Through which two channels can you update your address after moving so renewal notices reach you?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: After moving, you can update the address that renewal reminders go to at a local license office or online.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How many months before expiration can you renew a Missouri license, and which two tests happen at every renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: You may renew up to six months before the license expires, and every renewal includes the vision and road sign tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Does missing a mailed reminder excuse a late renewal, and what ticket risk comes with driving on an expired card?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Renewing on time is your own duty even if no reminder arrives, and driving on a lapsed license can earn a ticket for driving without a valid license.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What option can a Missouri license office grant if you will be out of the state or country for an extended period?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: If you will be away from the state or country for a long period, a license office can grant an early renewal.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What is the longest period a Missouri driver license can remain valid, and may you drive once it expires?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A Missouri driver license can be valid for as long as six years, and once it expires you may not drive.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: When can you take care of both your driver license renewal and vehicle registration renewal in a single visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: When the driver license and vehicle registration renewal dates fall within six months of each other, both renewals may be handled in one visit.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which extra tests return if you let your Missouri license stay expired more than six months before renewing?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Missing the renewal by more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days) after expiration means retaking the written and driving tests on top of the vision and road sign tests.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What exact day count does the Missouri manual use for the six-month lapsed-license cutoff?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: For a license that has lapsed, the guide counts six months as one hundred eighty-four days before the written and driving tests come back.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How long do returning service members whose license expired out of state have to renew without retesting, and can they drive before renewing?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Service members whose license expired while out of state can renew without re-examination for up to six months after an honorable discharge or within ninety days of moving back, whichever comes first, but the expired license still cannot be used to drive.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: Who may renew a Missouri driver license by mail, and what must accompany the mail-in application form?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: Members of the armed forces and their dependents may renew by mail using the Mail-In Driver License Application, Form four thousand three hundred seventeen, with the required documents and fees.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: How do you replace a lost, stolen, or destroyed Missouri license, and what alternative opens if expiration is within six months?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license is replaced with a duplicate, though if it expires within six months you can renew early instead.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Can a non-commercial driver renew during a suspension versus during a revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A non-commercial driver can renew, after the vision and road sign tests, while suspended; during a revocation, renewal is allowed only if the revocation came from refusing a chemical test.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: When does a suspended driver physically get back a license that was renewed during the suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A renewed license is not handed back until the reinstatement requirements are met and the driving privilege is restored.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: What registry does saying yes to the counter donor prompt join, and whose permission governs that decision?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: Answering yes to the donor question at the counter adds you to the Missouri Organ and Tissue Donor Registry, a first-person consent registry whose decision stands unless you change it and needs no family consent.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What does the optional donor symbol on the front of a Missouri card look like, and what is the fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Choosing the optional donor symbol puts a red heart with a green banner on the front of your permit, license or nondriver ID, and neither the symbol nor registry enrollment costs anything.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: What follow-up choice is offered right after joining the donor registry, and how can you add a donor sticker later?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: Applicants who say yes to the donor registry are then asked about the optional donor symbol, and a donor sticker for the back of the card can be requested online later.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: Which two charitable funds must every Missouri license clerk ask if you want to support?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: The clerk must ask whether you want to give money to the organ donor fund or the blindness awareness fund.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Who may request a DHH notation on a Missouri card, when must you ask, and why does it help?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A deaf or hard of hearing applicant may ask for a DHH notation, which must be requested when applying, so emergency and police personnel can quickly recognize the need.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.front: What must a Missouri resident hold to add a boater safety indicator, and what is its first-time fee?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.expected_back: A Missouri resident holding a current Boating Safety Education Card may add a boater safety indicator, which costs one dollar extra the first time it is added.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.front: Where does a permanent disability indicator print on a Missouri card, what paperwork is required, and is it mandatory?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.expected_back: A permanent disability indicator goes on the back of the card only with a Physicians Statement (Form five thousand two hundred ninety-four), costs nothing extra and is never required by law.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.front: How can an eligible former service member get VETERAN printed on the front of a Missouri card, and what does it cost?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.expected_back: A veteran may have VETERAN printed on the front of the card by showing an accepted discharge document, such as a DD Form two hundred fourteen showing honorable or general under honorable conditions, at no extra cost.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.front: Where does an optional medical alert notation for conditions like diabetes, epilepsy, or autism appear, and what does it cost?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.expected_back: A medical alert notation for listed conditions such as diabetes, epilepsy or autism can go on the front of the card with a signed Form five thousand eight hundred thirty-nine, at no extra cost and never by legal requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-R22.front: What does the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act require states to do with personal license and vehicle records?
sec02-card-sec02-R22.expected_back: The federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act requires states to close personal information in motor vehicle and license records unless state law directs otherwise.

sec02-card-sec02-R23.front: What voter-registration service does a Missouri license clerk offer during your counter visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R23.expected_back: At the counter the clerk asks whether you are registered to vote at your current address and can generate updated voter registration for your signature.

sec02-card-sec02-R24.front: Which applicants may register with the Selective Service while applying for a Missouri license or permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R24.expected_back: Male applicants aged eighteen to twenty-six may register with the Selective Service when they apply for a license or permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: What happens when a parent or guardian files a denial form for a driver under eighteen, and how long does it last?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: A parent or guardian of an applicant under eighteen can file Form four thousand eight hundred eleven asking the Director of Revenue to deny a license, which also cancels a license already held; the denial lasts until age eighteen or until the parent asks to clear it.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Which five impairment, crash-scene, or application offenses can get a Missouri license suspended, revoked, or denied?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: A license can be suspended, revoked or denied for driving under the influence, refusing an alcohol or drug test, leaving a crash scene, not filing an accident report, or lying on a license application.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Which insurance, point, court, child-support, fuel-theft, or youth-liquor violations can also cost you your Missouri license?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: A license can also be lost for not keeping insurance, too many points, lending your license, skipping court or unpaid tickets, unpaid child support, skipping a required ignition interlock, stealing fuel, a minor possessing liquor, or failing to yield and causing injury or death.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which fake-ID, Bureau-exam, vehicle-felony, fatal-crash, or insurance-fraud acts are grounds to lose your license?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Altering your license or using someone else's to buy alcohol, ignoring a Driver License Bureau exam request, using a vehicle in a felony or causing a death in a crash, and submitting false proof of insurance are further grounds for losing a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What three sequential stages must every first-time Missouri driver under eighteen complete under GDL law?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Missouri's GDL law makes every first-time driver under eighteen hold an instruction permit and drive with a licensed driver, then drive under restrictions on an intermediate license, before a full license.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: At what age does GDL step one open, which three tests does it require, and how long can the permit last?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: GDL step one, the instruction permit at age fifteen, requires passing the vision, road sign and written tests and is valid up to twelve months depending on document verification.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Which four adult roles are authorized to appear at the license office and sign a teen's permit permission statement?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer from a federal residential job training program must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Who qualifies to ride in the front passenger seat beside a Missouri permit driver younger than sixteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: Under sixteen, a permit holder may drive only with a front-seat companion who is a parent, stepparent, grandparent, legal guardian or qualified instructor, or someone at least twenty-five who has been licensed at least three years and has written parent permission.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Once a Missouri instruction permit holder turns sixteen, who may serve as the required front-seat supervisor?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: From age sixteen a permit holder may drive with a front-seat companion who is at least twenty-one and holds a valid license.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How do the non-family front-seat supervisor rules relax when a permit holder reaches age sixteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Under sixteen, a front-seat companion who is not one of the listed relatives, a guardian or a qualified instructor must be at least twenty-five, licensed three years or more and hold written parent permission, while from sixteen any licensed driver aged twenty-one or older qualifies.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: While driving on an instruction permit, who wears seat belts, what card must you carry, and how do permit renewals work?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Permit drivers and all passengers must wear seat belts, the permit itself must be carried because the exam record is not enough, and the permit can be renewed repeatedly without new written tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: How many total and nighttime behind-the-wheel hours are required during the permit stage, and who gives them?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: The permit period must include forty hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, at least ten of them after dark, given by a parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: If a teen's parent, stepparent, grandparent, or guardian has a physical disability, how can behind-the-wheel instruction be handled?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: If the parent, stepparent, grandparent or guardian is physically disabled, he or she may name up to two people to give the permit holder behind-the-wheel instruction.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: How many months and days must you hold your instruction permit before advancing to an intermediate license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: To move to the intermediate license you must hold the permit for at least six months (one hundred eighty-two days), counted from the day after it was issued.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: What exact day count and start day define the six-month permit period for GDL step two?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The intermediate step counts its six months as one hundred eighty-two days, beginning the day after the permit is issued.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which two conviction-free lookback windows are required to earn a Missouri intermediate license between sixteen and eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: GDL step two, the intermediate license for ages sixteen to eighteen, requires no alcohol-related convictions in the past twelve months and no traffic convictions in the past six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Who confirms your forty hours at the office for an intermediate license, and when must vision, sign, and written results be retaken?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: An adult from the approved list must come to the license office to confirm the forty hours, and the applicant must pass the driving test and retake the vision, road sign and written tests if earlier results are more than one year old.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: During the first six months on an intermediate license, how many non-family passengers under nineteen may ride with you?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: In the first six months an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger under nineteen who is not immediate family.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: After your first six months on an intermediate license, how many non-family passengers under nineteen may you carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: After the first six months the limit becomes no more than three passengers under nineteen who are not immediate family.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Which age and relationship group is counted under both intermediate-license passenger caps?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Both intermediate passenger limits count only riders younger than nineteen who are outside the driver's immediate family.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: During what activity may the intermediate-license passenger limits not apply?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The intermediate passenger limits may not apply while the license holder is doing agricultural work.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Between which overnight hours may an intermediate driver not drive alone, and what four exceptions allow it?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: An intermediate driver may not drive alone from one a.m. to five a.m. unless going to or from a school activity, job or emergency, or riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Which relatives count as immediate family under the Missouri intermediate-license passenger rules?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: For the passenger limits, immediate family means parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, and adopted or foster children living in the driver's household.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Up to how many years is a Missouri intermediate driver license valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: The intermediate license is valid for up to two years, depending on document verification status.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: At age eighteen, what license, clean-record window, and two tests are required to graduate to the full under-twenty-one license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: GDL step three, the full under-twenty-one license at eighteen, requires a valid intermediate license, no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last twelve months, and passing the vision and road sign tests.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: How long is the clean-record check for both traffic and alcohol offenses at step three, and what status blocks upgrading?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: For the full under-twenty-one license, both alcohol-related offenses and traffic convictions are checked over the last twelve months, and the privilege must not be suspended, revoked or denied when you apply.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Up to how many years is the full under-twenty-one Missouri driver license valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: The full under-twenty-one license is valid for up to three years, depending on document verification status.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: How recently expired can a transferable out-of-state license be, and what test record does a first-time applicant bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: A new resident can transfer an out-of-state license that is valid or expired no more than one hundred eighty-four days, and a first-time applicant brings the Driver Examination Record (Form one hundred) showing the tests were passed.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: What paperwork must a driver upgrading a Missouri license bring to the Highway Patrol examination station?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: A driver upgrading a license takes the same document set to the Highway Patrol examination site when sitting the written, vision, road sign or driving tests.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Roughly what share of applicants fail the Missouri written exam on their first attempt according to the guide?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: The guide warns that almost fifty percent of test-takers fail the written exam on the first try, so studying the guide first improves your odds.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Why do car drivers frequently collide with motorcycles they claim they never saw?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Drivers often fail to notice motorcycles, and judging how fast or how far away a motorcycle is can be hard.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: Why shouldn't a motorcyclist assume car drivers will yield right-of-way at an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: At intersections a motorcycle rider should not count on having the right-of-way, because drivers may not see the bike or may think it is moving slower than it is.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: May your car ever share a single lane side-by-side with a motorcycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, because the rider needs the whole lane to stay safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: How much lateral space does a motorcycle deserve when you pass — and what if the lane is narrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane width instead of squeezing by, and wait for a clear stretch if the lane is too narrow to share.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Which four surface or weather hazards force motorcyclists to adjust speed or lane position unexpectedly?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Riders shift speed and lane position for manhole covers, diagonal rail tracks, debris or strong wind, so be ready to react when you follow one.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What protective headgear does the Missouri guide state law requires for motorcycle riders?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Missouri law requires motorcycle riders to wear a helmet.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Which two licensing options authorize riding a motorcycle on Missouri public streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Riding a motorcycle on public streets requires a valid driver license with a motorcycle endorsement, or a motorcycle license.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: Which four visibility and signaling habits help motorcyclists stand out to surrounding drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Motorcycle riders should wear bright clothing, stay out of blind spots, use proper lights and reflectors at night, and signal and scan before slowing, merging or turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Up to how many pounds can a typical tractor-trailer weigh — and past how many feet can a long rig stretch?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: A typical tractor-trailer can weigh as much as eighty thousand pounds, and with a long trailer the whole rig can be longer than ninety feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: Beyond how many feet can multi-trailer rigs stretch on busy intercity highways?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: On busy intercity routes, double and triple trailer rigs can run longer than one hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Which two risky pull-out or lane-change moves right ahead of a large vehicle invite rear-end crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Do not pull onto a road in front of a large vehicle, and avoid moving over in front of one when you are about to turn off the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How can you tell instantly whether a truck or bus driver can see your car?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: If you cannot see a truck or bus driver in that vehicle's rearview mirrors, the driver cannot see you either.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Which three areas around a truck or bus form the No-Zone — and how should you treat them?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: The No-Zone is the set of blind spots beside, behind and in front of a truck or bus where a car disappears from view, so stay out of it unless it is truly necessary.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What two lingering habits beside and behind a large vehicle should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Do not ride alongside a large vehicle for long stretches, and do not tailgate one; keep a safety cushion around it.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What landmark in your inside mirror clears merging back ahead of a truck — and how must you manage speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: After passing a truck, wait until you can see its cab in your rearview mirror before moving back in, then signal, hold your speed and do not slow down ahead of it.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: At which two highway spots should cars vacate the right lane to accommodate heavy trucks?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: On steep grades, keep out of the right lane of a divided or multi-lane road where slow trucks travel, and avoid the right lane near weigh stations so trucks can merge back in.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Why must you leave extra braking room when following a placarded hazardous-materials truck toward railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Vehicles hauling hazardous materials are required to stop at every railroad crossing, so be ready for them to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Why might a semi swing left right before turning right — and what should you check before passing?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A large truck may swing left first to make a right turn, so watch its turn signal before you try to pass it.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, compare an average car's stopping distance with a loaded tractor-trailer's?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour an average car stops in roughly one hundred thirty to one hundred forty feet, while a fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost four hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: How many gears might a loaded semi work through — and how much heavier is its load per engine than a car's?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: A loaded semi speeds up slowly: it may shift through ten gears to reach the limit, and its engine moves thirty to forty times the weight a car engine does.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Instead of racing ahead to cut off a truck before your exit or turn, what calmer choice costs mere seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Rather than cut off a truck, slow down and make your turn or lane change behind it, which costs only a few seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What visual illusion about a tractor-trailer's size causes intersection crashes with cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A tractor-trailer often seems slower than it really is because of its size, which leads to crashes at intersections when car drivers misjudge its distance or speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Even with a steady Walk signal or green light, what must a pedestrian confirm before stepping off the curb?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: A pedestrian facing a Walk signal or green light has the right-of-way but should start across only after making sure drivers see them and stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Which signals bar starting across the street — and what if Don't Walk starts flashing while you are mid-crosswalk?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A pedestrian should not start crossing on a Don't Walk signal or a red or yellow light, but someone already in the street when the Don't Walk begins flashing may finish crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: Where should pedestrians cross in business districts — and who holds right-of-way during a mid-block crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Pedestrians should use an intersection or crosswalk in a business district or between two close signalized intersections, and must yield to all traffic when crossing mid-block.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: On a road with no sidewalk, which side should you walk along?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Where there is no sidewalk, walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: Instead of standing in an active lane to talk with a driver, how should a pedestrian handle the conversation?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: A pedestrian should not stand in a traffic lane talking to a driver, but should wait for the car to park safely and stay on its curb side.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Does a green light excuse hitting or crowding a pedestrian — even one jaywalking against the signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Even on a green light, a driver must yield to every pedestrian in the intersection, and must take care to avoid pedestrians whether or not they are obeying the law.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What rule applies whenever a vehicle ahead stops or slows for a pedestrian?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Never pass a vehicle that has stopped or slowed for a pedestrian.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: When does a lower school-zone speed limit apply — and how must you respond to a school crossing patrol?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Obey the lower school-zone speed limit when its lights flash or children are present, and stop if a school crossing patrol member signals you.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: What must your vehicle do when someone crosses carrying a white cane — plain or red-tipped — or a guide dog?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Always yield to a blind pedestrian; when someone crosses with a guide dog or a white cane, with or without a red tip, vehicles must stop completely.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Which pedestrians inside a marked or unmarked crosswalk earn your yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian in a marked or unmarked crosswalk who is on your side of the road or approaching it.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Where must you avoid stopping at a red light — and what comes before driving across a sidewalk?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Do not block the crosswalk while waiting at a red signal, and yield to pedestrians before driving across a sidewalk or crosswalk.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: How should you set speed along residential streets lined with parked cars?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: On residential streets with parked cars, keep at or under the speed limit, adjusting to how far ahead you can see.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: While looking left for traffic gaps on a right-on-red turn, where else must you scan — and for whom?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: When getting ready to turn right, especially on a red light, watch for pedestrians and cyclists coming up on your right.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Where do most crashes involving bicycles and mopeds occur — and what respect do riders deserve?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Most crashes with bicycles and mopeds happen at intersections, so scan for them and give them the same consideration as any other vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Before turning right onto a main street, why must you look right as well as left?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Before turning right onto a main road, look right as well as left for wrong-way cyclists on the road or the sidewalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: How should you make a right turn when you are following a cyclist approaching the same corner?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: If you need to turn right while following a cyclist, slow down and stay behind the rider until you can turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: When turning left across an oncoming cyclist's path, when must you wait and yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: When turning left, yield to an oncoming cyclist unless you are certain you can finish the turn before the rider reaches the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: How much space should you give when overtaking a bicycle or moped — and what if the lane is tight?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Give a bicycle or moped a full lane width when passing, slowing down if needed, and wait for a clear stretch if the lane is too narrow to share.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: When may motorists cross a striped bicycle lane — and who holds priority inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: A bicycle lane is a striped part of the roadway for bicycles; you may cross it to turn or to enter or leave the road, but you must yield to cyclists in it.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: What check belongs right before swinging a parked car door open toward a travel or bike lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: Look for passing cyclists before you open a car door into a traffic lane or bike lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: How do bicycle and moped rights and duties compare with motorists' — and which way must they ride?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Moped and bicycle riders have the same rights and duties as motorists on public roads and must always ride with traffic, never against it.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: While slower cyclists normally ride far right, which four situations allow taking the middle or left?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: A rider going slower than traffic generally keeps as far right as is safe, but may move toward the middle or left to turn left, avoid hazards, use a lane too narrow to share, or go straight past a right-turn-only lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: Which four roadside traps explain why cyclists leave buffer space away from the extreme right edge?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: The right edge of a road often holds ditches, gutters, sand and gravel shoulders, so riders should leave room between themselves and those hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: Where may a bicyclist ride on a one-way street — and what comes before shifting position?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: On a one-way street a bicyclist may ride as far left as is safe, and riders should check traffic and signal before shifting lanes or position.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: What smart option helps a less experienced cyclist handle heavy traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: In heavy traffic, a less experienced cyclist may find it easier to wait near the curb until a safe gap opens.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.front: For teen and adult bicyclists, how does riding in the street compare with riding on sidewalks?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.expected_back: For teen and adult cyclists, riding in the street with traffic is far safer than riding on the sidewalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Where on the federal interstate highway system may mopeds operate?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Mopeds are not allowed on any part of the federal interstate highway system.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: What credential is required to ride a moped on Missouri public streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: Driving a moped on public streets requires a valid driver license.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: Does Missouri law require helmets on mopeds or bicycles — and why wear a certified one anyway?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: Missouri does not require moped or bicycle riders to wear a helmet, although a safety-certified one can prevent serious head injury or death.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does Missouri treat safety-certified helmets for moped and bicycle riders — law or recommendation?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: For moped and bicycle riders a safety-certified helmet is advice, not a legal requirement, since state law does not demand one.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: How many feet of clearance should cyclists and moped riders keep when passing to the left of cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: Riders passing to the left of a parked or moving vehicle should leave three to four feet of space for a door that swings open or a car that swerves.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Does Missouri require registering or inspecting mopeds and bicycles — and what rule DOES apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: Missouri does not require mopeds or bicycles to be registered or inspected, but it does require certain equipment.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: During what sunset-to-sunrise window must a bicycle run a white front light — visible from how far?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: From half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise a bicycle needs a white front light that drivers can see from five hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What minimum size rear red reflector — or light — does a bike need, visible how far in low beams?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: A rear red reflector must be at least two square inches, or a rear red light may be used instead, and drivers must be able to see it in their low beams from six hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: From how many feet in low beams must reflectors or lights on pedals, cranks, shoes, or ankles show?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Reflectors or lights worn on the rider's shoes or lower legs, or fitted to the pedals or crank arms, must show in low beams at two hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How far in low beams must side reflectors or lights show on a bike — and which mopeds are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Reflective material or lights on each side of the bicycle or rider must show in low beams at three hundred feet, a rule that does not cover mopeds meeting federal NHTSA standards.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Match all four nighttime bicycle visibility distances — front white, rear red, sides, and pedals?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The bicycle lighting distances differ by item: the white front light must be visible from five hundred feet, a rear red light or reflector shows at six hundred feet in low beams, side reflectors or lights at three hundred feet, and pedal or leg reflectors at two hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.front: Between which hours do car-bicycle collisions jump sharply — and what prevents nearly all of them?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.expected_back: Crashes between bicycles and cars climb sharply between sunset and sunrise, and proper lights and reflectors can prevent almost all of them.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: Do you need a driver license or motorcycle license to ride a Missouri-compliant electric bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: Riding an electric bicycle that meets the state definition does not require an operator license or a motorcycle license.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Which three hardware specs — pedals, seating, and motor wattage ceiling — define a Missouri electric bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Under the state definition an electric bicycle has working pedals, a seat or saddle, and an electric motor under seven hundred fifty watts.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: What wheel count, transmission type, cubic-centimeter cap, and horsepower cap define a Missouri motorized bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: A motorized bicycle, such as a moped, has two or three wheels, an automatic transmission and a motor of no more than fifty cubic centimeters producing under three gross brake horsepower.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: What maximum speed on flat ground keeps a device inside Missouri's motorized-bicycle category?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: To count as a motorized bicycle, the device can go no faster than thirty miles per hour on level ground.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: What lights do cars inside an organized funeral procession run, and how closely do they follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: Every vehicle in a funeral procession uses its flashing emergency lights and follows the car ahead as closely as is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: Where do organized funeral processions hold right-of-way — and what two exceptions outrank them?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: An organized funeral procession has the right-of-way at every intersection regardless of traffic signals, except for emergency vehicles or when police direct otherwise.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.front: Which three moves are forbidden for drivers outside a moving funeral procession?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.expected_back: Drivers outside a funeral procession may not cut between its moving vehicles, join it to get the right-of-way, or pass its vehicles except in a lane provided for passing.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.front: When may an outside driver enter an intersection while a funeral procession crosses on red?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.expected_back: A driver not in a funeral procession may enter an intersection the procession is crossing on a red light only without crossing the procession's path.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.front: How does the Missouri guide define road rage and its real-world consequences?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.expected_back: Road rage is an uncontrolled display of anger by a driver, usually in response to another driver, that can damage property or injure people.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.front: Which horn, headlight, spacing, braking, lane, and physical actions count as road-rage behavior?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.expected_back: Examples of road-rage behavior include honking, flashing headlights, tailgating, chasing another car, aggressive gestures, sudden braking, deliberate blocking, cutting off and assault.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.front: Can habitual road-rage reactions be unlearned — and what personal trait does it take?
