sec05-card-sec05-R26.expected_back: Road rage habits can be unlearned, but doing so takes self-discipline from the driver.

sec05-card-sec05-F49.front: Walk through your emotional response, mental notes, and follow-up when targeted by road rage?
sec05-card-sec05-F49.expected_back: Faced with road rage, stay calm and do not respond in kind, note the location and descriptions of the driver and vehicle, and report it to local authorities as soon as you can.

sec05-card-sec05-F51.front: If you spot a suspected drunk driver, whom do you contact immediately and what three details help?
sec05-card-sec05-F51.expected_back: If you think you have seen a drunk driver, tell the police at once and give the plate number, a description of the car and driver, and its location.

sec05-card-sec05-F52.front: What maximum dollar fine and jail term can a Missouri court impose for highway littering?
sec05-card-sec05-F52.expected_back: Littering is illegal, and a court can impose a fine of up to one thousand dollars, up to one year in jail, or both.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.front: Why does flicking a glowing cigarette butt out a car window endanger trailing traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.expected_back: A lit cigarette tossed from a car window can blow into the vehicle behind and cause damage or injury, which is one reason littering is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Once parked, what clearance from travel lanes and visibility from both directions must your car have?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Once parked, your vehicle must not become a hazard, so leave it far enough from any travel lane that it does not get in the way and where drivers coming from either direction can see it.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What type of parking area should you always choose whenever one is available?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Use a designated parking area whenever you can.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: When you have no choice except parking on the roadway itself, how should you position your tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: If you have to park on the roadway itself, get as far from traffic as you can, and pull as close as possible to the curb if there is one.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Even without a No Parking sign, what traffic-flow or safety test rules out a parking spot?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Do not park where your vehicle blocks normal traffic or creates a hazard for other drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What brake step and transmission setting belong every single time you park a manual or automatic car?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Every time you park, set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in park.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: Contrast how you secure the shifter in a manual car versus an automatic — and what step both share?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Leaving the transmission in gear applies to a manual car, while an automatic is left in park, and in both cases the parking brake is set.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What two habits with your ignition key and door locks apply whenever your parked car leaves your sight?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Never leave the keys in a parked vehicle, and lock it any time it will be out of your sight.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Before cracking your door after parking, what must you check — and which side should riders and kids use?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Look for traffic before opening your door, get out on the curb side when possible, and have passengers, especially children, leave on the curb side too.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Whom specifically must you scan for before opening a street-side door — and how fast should it shut?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Before opening a door, watch for cyclists, who often ride along the right edge of the travel lanes next to parked cars, and close the door as soon as you are out.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: When curb-side exit isn't practical, under what condition may you open a street-side door?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Opening a door on the street side is allowed only after you check traffic first, since getting out on the curb side is preferred.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Which two actions are mandatory right before pulling out of any curb stall or parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Before pulling out of any parking space, check traffic and signal.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: On a one-way street without prohibiting signs, which side or sides may you normally park along?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: On a one-way street you may usually park on either the left or the right side.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which curb side and facing direction are illegal when parking on a two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Do not park on the left side of a two-way street or with your vehicle facing against the flow of traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Contrast legal left-side street parking on a one-way street against a two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Street side depends on the street type: a one-way street normally allows parking on either side, while a two-way street forbids parking on the left side.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Besides roadside metal signs, what visual clue right along the pavement edge shows parking limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Look for signs that ban or limit parking, and note that some limits are shown by colored curb markings.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which painted curb color, roadway structure, and fire-rescue fixture forbid parking beside them?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Parking is forbidden next to a curb painted yellow, on a bridge, or in front of a fire hydrant.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Does a yellow-painted curb ban parking even when zero No Parking signs stand nearby?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: Colored curb markings can signal a parking limit even where no sign is posted, and a curb painted yellow means no parking there.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Which four everyday corner, walkway, and property spots are strictly off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Never park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or across the entrance to a driveway.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: What does the blue-and-white International Symbol of Access reserve a parking stall for?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: The International Symbol of Access marks spaces reserved for vehicles driven by or carrying people with disabilities.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Beyond displaying disability plates or a placard, what human presence is required to use a handicapped space?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: A handicapped space may be used only by a vehicle showing a disability placard or plates, and only while a person with a physical disability is in it or is being dropped off or picked up.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Why isn't having valid disability plates on the family car enough by itself to park in a reserved stall?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Showing a disability placard or plates is not enough by itself; the reserved space also needs a person with a physical disability riding in the car or being dropped off or picked up.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: May any driver park inside the painted striped access aisle beside a handicapped space?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Parking in the striped access aisle beside a handicapped space is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: When does using a family member's legitimate disability placard or plates become an offense?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Using someone's disability placard or plates to take a handicapped space is illegal when that person is not riding along at the time.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Which two distinct violations around handicapped stalls draw citations even if a placard exists?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Two separate offenses apply around reserved spaces: parking in the access aisle, and using another person's placard or plates when that person is not being carried.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What minimum and maximum dollar fine hits a conviction for misusing a Missouri handicapped parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: A conviction for misusing a handicapped space brings a fine of at least fifty dollars and no more than three hundred dollars.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Which way does the Missouri guide tell you to turn your front wheels when parking on a hill — and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: When parked on a hill, turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road so that a rolling car moves away from traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What safety goal explains turning your wheels toward the roadside whenever parked on a grade?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: The reason for turning the wheels toward the roadside on a hill is so the car rolls away from traffic if it starts to move.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Before stepping out on a hill, what three mechanical steps cover wheels, engine-and-gear, and brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Before leaving a car parked on a hill, turn the wheels the proper way, shut off the engine with the vehicle in the proper gear, and set the parking or emergency brake.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How do the terms 'emergency brake' and 'parking brake' relate on Missouri's hill-parking checklist?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: The hill checklist on this page uses the words emergency or parking brake for the same brake that must be set on any parked vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: After setting wheels, gear, and brake on a hill, what four closing steps cover keys, mirror, and locks?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: To finish leaving a car parked on a hill, take the keys out, check the rearview mirror for traffic before stepping out, then lock the car and keep the keys with you.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which three key-and-door steps finish hill parking identically to flat-ground parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Parking on hills ends with the same security habit as any other stop: take the key out of the ignition, lock up, and keep the keys with you.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Where and how many feet away should you line up beside the forward car to start parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: To begin parallel parking, stop alongside the car in front of the empty space, about one and a half feet to its left.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Which way do you cut the wheel first when backing into a parallel stall — while watching your front bumper?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Next, turn the wheels sharply right and back slowly into the space, making sure your front end does not block passing or oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Once your nose clears the forward car's rear bumper, what two wheel cuts center you in the stall?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Once your front clears the car ahead, turn the wheels sharply left and keep backing, then turn sharply right and pull forward toward the curb, ending in the middle of the space.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Recite the three sharp steering-wheel directions from start to finish of a standard right-curb parallel park?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: In parallel parking the wheel turns run sharp right, then sharp left, then sharp right again as you pull toward the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Where between the forward and rear parked cars should your vehicle sit when finished parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: During parallel parking the final position is the center of the space, not pressed against the car ahead or behind.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: How many days do you have to visit a license office and title a newly bought car or one brought into Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Whether you buy a vehicle as a Missouri resident or have just moved to Missouri, you have thirty days to go to a license office and title it.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: Does Missouri give a different titling deadline to residents buying a car versus newcomers moving into the state?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: The same thirty-day window applies to titling whether you just bought the vehicle or just became a Missouri resident.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What legal fact does a vehicle title prove, and what happens if you apply past thirty days after buying?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: A title proves that you own the vehicle, and if you do not apply for it within thirty days of buying the vehicle you must pay a penalty fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: Where do you apply for a Missouri vehicle title, and what are the exact title and processing fees?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: You can apply for a title at any license office; the title costs eight dollars and fifty cents and there is also a nine dollars processing fee.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Between Missouri's base title fee and the processing fee charged alongside it, which dollar figure is higher?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: The title itself costs eight dollars and fifty cents while the processing fee charged with it is nine dollars, so the processing fee is the larger of the two.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Beyond the title and processing charges, what taxes must be paid when you title a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: When you title a vehicle you must also pay all the state and local sales taxes that are due.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Which two resources let you look up how much vehicle sales tax you will owe before titling?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Information on sales tax due can be obtained from any license office or from the Department's online sales tax calculator.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: What do you leave the license counter with after applying for a title, and how do you receive the title itself?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: You receive a receipt when you apply, and the Department later mails you the title.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Why does the Missouri guide warn you never to leave your vehicle title inside the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: A title is an important personal document, so do not keep it in your vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Which two pairs of vehicle-buying factors change the exact paperwork required for a Missouri title?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Title requirements differ for new and used vehicles and for vehicles bought inside or outside Missouri.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Which two titling documents does a Missouri dealer hand you when you buy a brand-new vehicle in state?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: For a new vehicle bought in Missouri, the dealer gives you a title application and an assigned Manufacturer's Statement of Origin, or MSO.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What two facts about a vehicle's history does a Manufacturer's Statement of Origin establish?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: The MSO shows that the vehicle is new and has never been registered.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: On a brand-new vehicle, who completes the odometer disclosure and where is it located?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: For a new vehicle, you and the dealer fill in the odometer disclosure on the back of the MSO.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: Where is a brand-new vehicle's odometer reading recorded instead of on a title?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: For a new vehicle, the odometer reading goes on the MSO rather than on a title.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What document must any Missouri used-car seller give you, and what extra form should a Missouri dealer include?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: For a used vehicle bought in Missouri, the seller must give you a properly assigned title, and a dealer seller should also give you a completed title application.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How does the ownership transfer paper for a brand-new vehicle differ from that of a used vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: A new vehicle comes with an MSO from the dealer, while a used vehicle comes with a properly assigned title from the seller.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Which seven buyer, mileage, sale, lien, and signature details belong on a properly assigned Missouri title?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: A properly assigned title lists the buyer's name and address, the odometer reading if needed, the sale price, the sale date, any lienholder, every seller's signature and printed name, and the buyer's printed name and signature if needed.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Which vehicle model years need a title-back mileage disclosure, and at what vehicle age does it stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: An odometer disclosure on the back of the title is required for vehicles of model year two thousand eleven and newer until the vehicle is twenty years old.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: When selling a twenty-eleven-or-newer vehicle under twenty years old, who enters the mileage and where?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: When a vehicle of model year two thousand eleven or newer that is under twenty years old is sold, the seller writes the mileage on the title assignment.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: How do the buyer and seller verify the recorded mileage, and what extra document may occasionally apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Both the buyer and the seller print and sign their names to confirm the mileage, and sometimes a separate odometer statement is needed.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Which two documents do you need to title a brand-new vehicle purchased from an out-of-state dealer?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: For a new vehicle bought out of state, you need the dealer's invoice or a bill of sale plus the assigned MSO from that dealer.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Which title paperwork is needed when bringing home a used vehicle bought outside Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: For a used vehicle bought out of state, you need a properly assigned title from the seller or a reassigned title from the dealer.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: When buying a used car out of state from a dealership rather than a private owner, what kind of title might you receive?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Out of state, a used vehicle may come with a reassigned title from a dealer instead of a title assigned by a private seller.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Which two papers replace a title if you buy a vehicle in a state that does not issue titles?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: If the other state does not require a title, you need a bill of sale and the vehicle's last certificate of registration from that state.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: When the title assigned to you comes from another state, what extra check form is required and who fills it out?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: If the title assigned to you is from another state, a licensed inspection station must complete an identification number and odometer, or ID or OD, verification form.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Under what exact title condition is the ID or OD verification form required, and who alone may complete it?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: The ID or OD verification form is needed only when the title assigned to you was issued by another state, and only a licensed inspection station can complete it.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Where does the Missouri driver guide direct you for rules on titling salvage, dismantling, or rebuilding vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Titling a vehicle bought for salvage, dismantling or rebuilding has separate rules, and the guide points you to the Motor Vehicle Bureau for them.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: Where must Missouri residents register their vehicles, and how long does a newcomer have after moving in?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Missouri residents must register their vehicles in Missouri, and a new resident must do so within thirty days of moving in.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Which exact day starts the thirty-day vehicle registration countdown for someone moving into Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Registration of a new resident's vehicle has its own thirty-day deadline, counted from the day you become a Missouri resident.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What must a new resident do with an existing out-of-state vehicle title when registering in Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: A new resident must turn in the out-of-state title and apply for a Missouri title.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What paperwork must you bring when a lienholder keeps possession of your prior state's title?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: If a lender holds your out-of-state title and cannot release it, you provide a statement from the lender saying it will not surrender the title, plus one of three supporting documents.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: What items do you receive for your vehicle once you complete Missouri registration?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Registering your vehicle gets you Missouri license plates with a year tab on the plate.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: What vehicle factors determine registration fees for Missouri passenger cars versus commercial trucks?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: You can register at any license office; a passenger vehicle's fee depends on its taxable horsepower, a commercial vehicle's on its zone and gross weight, and a processing fee is added.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: When does Missouri let you register a vehicle for two years instead of one year?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: A two-year registration is possible when the year parity matches: an even model year in an even-numbered year or an odd model year in an odd-numbered year; otherwise only one year is offered.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: During an even-numbered calendar year like twenty eighteen, which vehicles qualify for a two-year Missouri registration?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: For example, in an even-numbered year such as two thousand eighteen, a vehicle with an even model year can be registered for two years.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: What optional plate styles can Missouri owners pick beyond standard tags, and how does pricing work?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: You may choose personalized or specialty plates, which can carry an extra personalized plate fee on top of the normal registration fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: Roughly how early should a mailed plate renewal notice arrive, and what if it never shows up?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: A renewal notice should arrive by mail about two months before your registration expires, but you must renew your plates on time even if it never comes.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What simple step helps ensure your plate renewal notice actually reaches your mailbox?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: To be sure your renewal notice reaches you, update your address whenever you move.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: Which four pieces of owner and vehicle info let you report a Missouri address change by email?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: You can report an address change by email with your full name, old and new addresses, your driver license number or the last four digits of your Social Security number, and your plate numbers.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: Which registration and property-tax documents may you need when renewing Missouri license plates?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: To renew you may need the renewal notice, last year's registration receipt or a copy of your title, plus a paid personal property tax receipt or a statement of non-assessment.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Which local government issues your personal property tax receipt, and what time span must it cover?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: The personal property tax receipt comes from the county where you live, or from the city of St. Louis, for the period of your previous registration.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: How do the property-tax receipts required at renewal differ after a one-year registration versus a two-year registration?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: After a one-year registration you show last year's tax receipt, but after a two-year registration you show receipts for both previous years.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: Along with tax and registration papers, what proof of coverage and payment can plate renewal require?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Renewal may also require a current insurance card or other proof of financial responsibility and the correct registration and processing fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: When your vehicle requires inspection at renewal, what certificate must you bring and how recent must it be?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: If an inspection applies to your vehicle, renewal needs a safety and or or emissions inspection certificate from the last sixty days.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: How does the arrival timing of a mailed renewal notice compare with the freshness rule on an inspection certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: The renewal notice comes about two months ahead, but the inspection certificate you bring must be from within the last sixty days.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Why should you read the checklist printed on your own Missouri renewal notice before heading in?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: Not every item on the renewal list applies to every owner, so read the list on your own renewal notice and bring what it asks for.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: How can you tell from your renewal postcard whether your plates qualify to be renewed online?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: You may be able to renew your plates online, and if you qualify a PIN is printed on your renewal notice.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: What form must you file—and within how many days—after selling a motor vehicle or ATV in Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: State law requires you to report selling a motor vehicle or all-terrain vehicle with a Notice of Sale, Form five thousand forty-nine, within thirty days.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.front: Through which two channels can a seller submit Missouri's Notice of Sale form?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.expected_back: The Notice of Sale can be turned in at any license office or mailed to the address printed on the form.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.front: What does Missouri require you to do if your license plates, tabs, or vehicle title get lost or destroyed?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.expected_back: If your plates, tabs or title are lost or destroyed, you are required to apply for a replacement.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: What do replacement titles, individual plates, and tab sets each cost when lost or destroyed, plus what added charge?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Replacing a lost or destroyed title costs eight dollars and fifty cents, plates cost eight dollars and fifty cents per plate, and a set of tabs costs eight dollars and fifty cents, each plus a nine dollars processing fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: How does a notarized theft affidavit change the cost and yearly limit for replacing stolen Missouri plates and tabs?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: With a notarized affidavit that they were stolen, you can replace stolen plates and tabs up to two times a year at no cost apart from a nine dollars processing fee.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.front: Up to how many times per year can stolen Missouri plates and tabs be replaced without the item fee?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.expected_back: The free replacement for stolen plates and tabs is limited to two times per year.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.front: How does the cost of replacing stolen plates and tabs compare with replacing lost or destroyed ones?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.expected_back: Stolen plates and tabs are replaced at no charge beyond the nine dollars processing fee, while lost or destroyed ones cost eight dollars and fifty cents each plus that fee.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: What coverage must every Missouri motor vehicle owner and driver maintain, and what legal name does Missouri give it?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: State law requires every motor vehicle operator and owner to carry some form of liability insurance, which is called Financial Responsibility.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Whose injuries and property damage does your liability insurance policy pay to cover?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Liability insurance covers the policyholder's legal liability when other people are injured or their property is damaged.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: How do most Missouri drivers satisfy Financial Responsibility instead of using cash deposits, bonds, or self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Most drivers get liability insurance from an insurance company or agent rather than through self-insurance, bonds or cash.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: During which two license-office plate transactions must Missouri vehicle owners present proof of insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Vehicle owners must show proof of insurance when they register a vehicle or renew their plates.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: What written pledge do you sign when registering a motor vehicle in Missouri?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: When you register a vehicle, you sign a form saying you have insurance and will keep it on the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Which six paper documents or digital options count as valid proof of insurance in Missouri?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Accepted proof includes a copy of your current insurance ID card, your policy or a binder, a paid receipt showing the policy, a Department self-insurance certificate or bond ID card, or a handheld electronic device.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: In auto insurance paperwork, what is a binder?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: A binder is a temporary insurance policy.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: What happens during a traffic stop if an officer asks for your insurance proof and you cannot produce it?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Keep proof of insurance in your vehicle, because you will be ticketed if an officer asks for it and you cannot show it.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: When may the Department request proof of insurance, and what crash situation guarantees a mandatory request?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: The Department may ask for proof of insurance at any time, and it will require proof if you were in a crash and did not show it then.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What fleet size and financial showing qualify an owner for a Missouri certificate of self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: To be self-insured you must have more than twenty-five vehicles and show that you can and will pay for damage they cause, and the Department then issues a certificate of self-insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Does owning exactly twenty-five vehicles qualify a business or individual for Missouri self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: Self-insurance needs more than twenty-five vehicles, so an owner with exactly twenty-five vehicles does not qualify.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: What dollar amounts must be filed with the Department for a surety bond or CD versus a property-backed bond?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Insuring through a surety bond, certificate of deposit or other negotiable securities means filing seventy-five thousand dollars, or one hundred fifty thousand dollars for a real estate bond, with the Department.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: How much cash must be deposited—and with which state official—to earn a certificate of self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Another option is depositing seventy-five thousand dollars in cash with the State Treasurer, after which the Department issues a certificate of self-insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How does the required dollar filing for a surety bond, CD, or security compare against a real estate bond?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: A regular surety bond, certificate of deposit or security is filed at seventy-five thousand dollars, while a real estate bond must be one hundred fifty thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: What is Missouri's minimum liability coverage per person for bodily injury?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: The minimum liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars per person for bodily injury.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: What is Missouri's minimum total bodily-injury liability coverage for a single crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: The minimum liability coverage is fifty thousand dollars per crash for bodily injury.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: How do Missouri's bodily-injury liability minimums differ between one injured person and an entire crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Bodily injury minimums differ by scope: twenty-five thousand dollars for one person but fifty thousand dollars for all injuries in one crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What minimum property-damage liability coverage must every Missouri policy carry per crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: The minimum liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars per crash for property damage.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Which bodily-injury liability minimum shares the exact same twenty-five-thousand-dollar figure as per-crash property damage?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Property damage coverage has a single minimum of twenty-five thousand dollars per crash, the same figure as the per person bodily injury minimum.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: What mandatory uninsured-motorist coverage amounts must Missouri drivers carry alongside liability?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: You must also carry uninsured motorist coverage of twenty-five thousand dollars per person and fifty thousand dollars per crash for bodily injury.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: How do required uninsured-motorist limits compare with liability limits regarding bodily injury versus property damage?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: Uninsured motorist coverage uses the same twenty-five thousand dollars and fifty thousand dollars bodily injury amounts, and the guide lists no property damage amount for it.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What financial and licensing losses can hit you if you let your Missouri auto insurance lapse?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Letting your insurance lapse can cost a great deal of money after a crash and can lead to losing your driver license and license plates.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: What action does the Department take when it discovers you failed to maintain required insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: If the Department finds out you have not kept insurance, it mails you a notice of suspension, and your license and plates may be taken or suspended.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: What form is most commonly used to file ongoing proof of insurance with Missouri, and who submits it?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Proof of insurance is most often filed as an SR-twenty-two, which your insurance company or agent files for you.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: After a first Missouri insurance suspension, what fee and ongoing filing period are required to get reinstated?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: After one insurance suspension, your license and or or plates stay suspended until you pay a twenty dollars fee and file proof of insurance, which you must keep doing for three years.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: What happens if your insurance drops again before finishing the required three-year proof period?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: If you fail to keep insurance for the required three years, your license and or or plates are suspended again.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: What suspension length, fee, and proof period hit when you collect two insurance suspensions within two years?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Two suspensions within two years of each other bring a ninety-day suspension, a two hundred dollars fee, and three years of proof of insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: What wait time, fee, and proof requirement apply to a third or subsequent Missouri insurance suspension?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Three or more suspensions bring a one-year suspension, a four hundred dollars fee, and three years of proof of insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: How does Missouri's reinstatement fee climb across first, second, and third-or-later insurance suspensions?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: The insurance suspension fees climb from twenty dollars for one suspension to two hundred dollars for two and four hundred dollars for three or more.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: What time window makes two insurance suspensions count as a repeat offense, and how long must proof stay on file afterward?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Two suspensions count as a repeat only when they fall within two years of each other, but proof of insurance must then be kept for three years.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: How long are your license or plates suspended if you cause a crash and leave the resulting damages unpaid?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: A driver who causes an accident and leaves the resulting damages unpaid has the license and or or plates suspended for one year.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: How can a driver suspended for unpaid crash damages get reinstated before the full year ends?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: You can be reinstated within that one year by paying a twenty dollars fee and sending the Driver License Bureau proof that the damages were settled.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: How does a suspension over unpaid crash damages compare with a third no-insurance suspension in length and fees?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.memory_hook: Both one year, twenty versus four-hundred
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: An unpaid-damages suspension and a third insurance suspension both last one year, but early reinstatement from the first costs twenty dollars while the second carries a four hundred dollars fee.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: How much crash protection does responsible, defensive driving give—and can it eliminate crash risk completely?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: Driving responsibly and defensively lowers the chance of a crash, but nothing can prevent crashes entirely.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: How does the Missouri driver guide define a traffic crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: A traffic crash is any time you injure yourself or someone else or damage property while driving your vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: May you drive away after bumping an unattended parked vehicle, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Do not leave even after hitting a parked vehicle, because leaving the scene of a traffic crash is a crime.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: Right after a collision occurs, what must you do first and where should you put your car if drivable?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: After a crash, stop, and move your vehicle off the road if you can, especially if it could cause more crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: How should you care for injured people at a crash scene before paramedics arrive, and whom do you call?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Help anyone who is hurt and keep them comfortable without moving them, then call an ambulance and the police.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: Which three emergency lighting tools help warn oncoming traffic after a nighttime or bad-weather crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: If the crash happens at night or in bad weather, warn other traffic with flares, reflectors or flashlights.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: Which six identity, vehicle, and coverage details must you exchange with everyone involved in a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.memory_hook: Names, addresses, IDs, VINs, plates, policies
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: Exchange names, addresses, driver license numbers, VINs, plate numbers, and insurance companies and policy numbers with everyone involved.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: When are you allowed to leave a police-attended crash scene, and should you call your insurer if not at fault?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: Stay at the scene until a law enforcement officer says you may leave, and contact your insurance company soon even if the crash was not your fault.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: What severe license consequence can follow hitting a road worker or responder inside a marked zone?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: Hitting a highway worker or emergency responder inside a designated construction, work or emergency zone can lead to revocation of your driving privilege.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: What does Missouri's Move It law require when vehicles have a minor crash with zero injuries?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: Missouri law requires vehicles in minor crashes with no injuries to move off the road, onto the shoulder or another nearby spot.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: Contrast what Missouri tells you to move after a minor no-injury crash versus an injury crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: After a minor crash with no injuries you move the vehicle off the road, but you never move an injured person.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: How many minutes of approaching traffic backup does every single minute of a blocked freeway lane create?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: Each minute a stopped vehicle blocks one freeway lane backs up approaching traffic for four minutes.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: What percentage of Missouri traffic fatalities come from secondary crashes that the Move It law targets?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: Secondary crashes cause eighteen percent of fatalities in Missouri, and the Move It law helps cut that risk.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: What four-word slogan promotes Missouri's Move It law on signs around St. Louis and Kansas City?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: The Move It law's campaign phrase is steer it and clear it, and signs with that message are being posted in the St. Louis and Kansas City areas.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: How did the Missouri Department of Transportation mark the tenth anniversary of the Move It law?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: The Missouri Department of Transportation used the law's tenth anniversary to remind drivers to clear minor crashes from the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: Within how many days must a required Missouri motor vehicle accident report be filed?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: When an accident report is required, state law says it must be filed within thirty days.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: Do parking-lot crashes or privately settled crashes still require a Missouri accident report when conditions apply?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: A required report applies even to a parking lot accident or one already settled, if it happened in Missouri less than one year ago.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Which uninsured-driver fact combined with what damage or injury threshold triggers a mandatory Missouri accident report?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: The report is required when someone involved had no liability insurance and there was property damage over five hundred dollars or any injury or death.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.front: Does an injury-free crash with exactly five hundred dollars of property damage trigger a mandatory accident report?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.expected_back: The damage threshold for a required report is property damage greater than five hundred dollars, so damage of exactly five hundred dollars without injury does not meet it.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: Why must both an uninsured party and qualifying damage or injury exist before an accident report is mandatory?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: The uninsured-party condition and the damage-or-injury condition are joined by the word and, so both must be true before a report is required.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: If you file an optional report below the threshold involving an uninsured driver, what action can the Department take?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: Even when a report is not required, you may still file one if an uninsured motorist was involved, though the Department can act only against that motorist for not keeping insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: Where can you obtain Missouri's Motor Vehicle Accident Report form, and which two ways can you submit it?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: You may get a Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Form one thousand one hundred forty, from the Department's website, your insurer or agent, or any license office, and mail or fax it in.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which four screenings make up the full Missouri driver examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: The Missouri driver examination has four parts: a written test on traffic laws and safe-driving rules, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Which three application, expiration, or Revenue-order situations require taking the Missouri driver examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: The examination is required for a new Missouri license, for a Missouri license expired more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days), and whenever the Director of Revenue asks, even if your license is current.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which two types of Missouri license revocations send a driver back through the full examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: A license revoked for too many points or for an Administrative Alcohol action also sends the driver back through the examination.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Which out-of-state drivers only have to pass the vision and road sign tests when switching to Missouri?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: A driver whose license from another state is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days, applying for the same type of Missouri license, takes only the vision and road sign tests.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: What two conditions must an out-of-state license satisfy to qualify for the vision-and-sign shortcut?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: An out-of-state license qualifies for the shortened vision and road sign route only if it is for the same type of license and is valid or expired less than one hundred eighty-four days.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Which agency administers Missouri driver exams, and who can direct you to the closest testing station?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: The Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) gives the driver examination, and either the MSHP or the Department can point you to the nearest testing center.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: What two facts must you prove before testing, and when must you present that identification again?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: You must prove your legal name and age before the exam, and you show that identification again whenever you apply for a license or permit and each time you take the written or driving test.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: Where does the guide point you to find Department and Highway Patrol phone numbers and testing station lists?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: The phone numbers for the Department and the Highway Patrol are printed at the back of the guide, and testing locations are also listed on the Highway Patrol website.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How many questions are on the Class F written test, and what question style is used?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: The Class F written test has twenty-five multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods this guide covers.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: May you consult the manual during the Class F written exam, and is Chapter fifteen commercial material included?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: The written test is not open book, and a Class F applicant is not tested on the commercial vehicle material in Chapter fifteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: How does the Class E for-hire written test differ from Class F, and is it open book?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: A Class E for-hire applicant takes a special written test that adds the Chapter fifteen commercial vehicle material, and it is also not open book.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What testing rule do Class F and Class E written exams share, and what single topic separates them?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Both the Class F and the Class E written tests are closed book; the difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial vehicle chapter.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What two abilities does the Missouri road sign test evaluate?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: The road sign test checks whether you can recognize traffic signs and understand what they mean.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: What criminal level and license loss can result from cheating, lying, or using cameras or two-way devices during an exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: Fraud in any license, permit or nondriver ID examination, such as false statements, cheating, or using a recording, camera or two-way communication device, is a Class A misdemeanor that can cost your driving privilege for up to one year.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which two distinct eyesight checks must every new or renewing Missouri applicant take?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Every new or renewal license or permit applicant takes both an acuity test and a peripheral (side) vision test.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What is Missouri's standard minimum passing visual acuity score?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: The standard minimum acuity is twenty over forty or better using either eye or both eyes.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Does hitting twenty over forty on the acuity chart waive the peripheral vision screen?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: The twenty over forty figure is the standard passing acuity, while a separate peripheral test measures side vision, so passing one screen does not cover the other.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What degree readings pass Missouri's standard peripheral side-vision check using two eyes versus a single eye?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The standard minimum side vision is fifty-five degrees or more in each eye, or eighty-five degrees or more in one eye.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Along with the fifty-five and eighty-five degree passing routes, what combined peripheral floor blocks licensing completely?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Side vision has two passing routes, fifty-five degrees in each eye or eighty-five degrees in a single eye, while seventy degrees combined is the floor below which no license is possible.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What two outcomes can happen to your application if you fall short of Missouri's standard vision numbers?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Missing the vision standards can lead to a denied license or to restrictions placed on the license.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What happens next if you fail the standard vision check at the testing station?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: If you fail the standard vision test, the examiner hands you a vision exam form for an eye specialist or physician, and a new prescription may mean waiting for the glasses or contacts before the written or driving test.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Worse than which acuity score and which combined peripheral score disqualifies you from taking the road test or holding a license?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: If both natural and corrected acuity are worse than twenty over one hundred sixty, or combined side vision is worse than seventy degrees, you cannot take the driving test or hold a Missouri license.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: What does the twenty over one hundred sixty acuity number represent, and when does it block a license?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: The twenty over one hundred sixty acuity cutoff applies only when both natural and corrected vision are worse than it; it is the point at which a license is impossible, not the standard passing level.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which three exam parts must you pass before taking the driving test, and who administers it?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: The driving test comes only after the written, vision and road sign tests are passed, and it is given by an MSHP driver license examiner.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: What does the examiner inspect before starting the road test, and when will the drive be refused?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: The examiner inspects the test vehicle for required equipment and safe condition, and the test is refused if the vehicle is not properly equipped or testing seems dangerous.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Which five plate, sticker, belt, door, and seat items must your road-test vehicle have ready?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: The test vehicle needs current plates, a valid inspection sticker, working seat belts, working doors for the driver and the examiner, and a clean, safe passenger seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Which two braking systems, warning device, and document must your test car carry to pass inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: The test vehicle also needs a working parking brake and foot brake, a working horn, and proof of financial responsibility.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Who is allowed inside the car during the driving test, and what rules govern conversation and traffic laws?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Only you and the examiner ride during the test; skip needless conversation, remember the examiner is there to test rather than teach, and obey every Missouri traffic law.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: How much lead time does the examiner give when calling out a maneuver during the driving test?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: After the examiner gives a direction, you are allowed enough time to check traffic and carry it out.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: How are you graded when asked to operate controls like wipers, turn signals, brakes, or the accelerator?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: When asked to use controls such as the accelerator, brakes, turn signals and wipers, you are graded on finding each one without searching and using it correctly.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Which five steps are graded as you start up and pull away at the beginning of the road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: When you pull away you are graded on starting the car, releasing the parking brake, checking that the way is clear, signaling, and driving smoothly at the right speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What three qualities does the examiner score during starts and stops on the road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Starting and stopping are graded for smoothness and safety, reaction time and control of the car while stopping.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What are the exact length and width dimensions of Missouri's road-test parallel parking space?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: The parallel parking task uses a space twenty-five feet long and seven feet wide.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What maximum curb distance, stall position, and time limit apply during the parallel parking maneuver?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Parallel parking is scored on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, near the middle of the space, and finishing within two minutes.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: Beyond curb distance and the two-minute clock, which four technique steps are scored in parallel parking?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Parallel parking is also scored on your position before backing, not touching the space markers, turning the wheels the right way, and checking traffic and signaling before pulling out.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Which parking maneuver is the only one on the Missouri test with a time limit and a measured stall?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Only parallel parking carries a time limit, two minutes, and only it uses a marked space, twenty-five feet long by seven feet wide.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Where must you look while backing on the driving test, and what three vehicle-control points are graded?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: When backing, you look over your right shoulder through the rear window and must keep a straight line, stay in the proper lane and hold the right speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: At least how many right and left turns are on the driving test, and what six habits are graded?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: You make at least two right turns and two left turns, graded on lane choice, timely signals, turning into the proper lane, traffic checks, speed and control.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What is the minimum count of right turns and left turns required during the Missouri driving skills test?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: For the turning task you make a minimum of two right and two left turns.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Which five curb, gear, wheel, brake, and exit steps are scored when parking on a hill?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Parking on a hill is graded on stopping no more than eighteen inches from the curb, leaving the car in park or the correct gear, turning the front wheels correctly, setting the parking brake, then checking traffic and signaling.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: What identical maximum curb distance applies to both parallel parking and hill parking on the Missouri test?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Parallel parking and hill parking use the same curb-distance limit of no more than eighteen inches.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Which six habits does the examiner grade as you approach and move through intersections?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: At intersections you are graded on obeying signs and lights, approach speed, awareness of traffic, lane position, yielding without blocking traffic, and a full stop at the proper place for stop signs.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: Which two specific stopping and yielding habits are highlighted in the intersection grading section?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: The intersection task includes making a full stop at the proper place at stop signs and yielding without blocking other traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Which five general driving habits does the examiner watch continuously from start to finish?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Throughout the test the examiner also watches your following distance, speed, lane use and lane markings, traffic awareness and yielding.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: What does the examiner continuously score regarding roadside signs and traffic lights across the entire route?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: The examiner also grades whether you notice and obey traffic signs and signals throughout the drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: How does point scoring work on the Missouri driving test, and what point loss fails the exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: The examiner deducts points for driving errors, and losing more than thirty points fails the driving test.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Which five major mistakes cause an immediate failure on the Missouri driving test regardless of points?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: You fail at once for an at-fault crash with another vehicle, hitting a pedestrian, driving so dangerously a crash could have resulted, breaking a traffic law, or refusing to drive as directed.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Can you fail the Missouri driving test even if you have lost thirty points or fewer?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A test can be failed outright without reaching the point limit, for example by breaking a traffic law or refusing an instruction.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: What document do you get upon passing the driving test, and what must you do before driving solo?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: Passing earns a test results form, but that form is not valid for driving; you must first apply for and receive a license at a license office.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: How many driving skills tests are you allowed to take in a single day?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: Only one driving test may be taken per day, and the examiner will suggest practice before a retest.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: What happens if you fail the Missouri driving skills test three times?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: After three failed driving tests, no further test is allowed without written Department authorization, and you must complete extra behind-the-wheel training, send proof, and receive approval to test.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How does the number thirty on a single test differ from the number three across multiple attempts?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: The point limit and the failure count are different numbers: losing more than thirty points fails a single test, while three failed tests trigger the Department authorization and extra training requirement.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: Where are failed driving-test results sent, and what notice follows after repeated failures?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: Results of failed driving tests are sent to the Department of Revenue, which then mails a letter requiring additional behind-the-wheel training.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: Who must provide the extra behind-the-wheel training after three road-test failures, and what clearance is needed before retesting?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: The extra training after three failures must be given by an eligible driver, and you must hold Department approval to test before the next attempt.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What does Missouri law set as every motorist's highest duty on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: A motorist's highest duty is careful, prudent driving, with speed and manner that keep the road safe for pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers as well as yourself.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Does Missouri right-of-way law ever grant any driver the right-of-way, and what crash duty always applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Right-of-way law only says who must yield and never gives any driver the right-of-way, so you must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian or vehicle no matter the circumstances.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: At what kinds of meeting points do right-of-way rules step in, and what do they settle?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Right-of-way rules exist for places where vehicles or pedestrians are likely to meet and no signs or signals control traffic, and they say who goes first and who waits.

sec04-card-sec04-R19.front: Which three levels of government set traffic rules in Missouri, and what local topics can town or county rules cover?
sec04-card-sec04-R19.expected_back: Cities, counties and the state can all set traffic rules, and you must obey each; local rules may set speed limits, one-way streets and stop signs, keep commercial vehicles off certain streets, control parking and turns, require signals, brake lights and horns, or ban sound-producing warning devices.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What added minimum penalties hit drivers caught speeding or passing through a Missouri state highway work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Speeding or passing in a construction or work zone on Missouri state roads can bring a fine of at least two hundred fifty dollars for a first offense and at least three hundred dollars for any later offense, on top of other fines.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How should you approach and pass a pedestrian or bicyclist sharing the roadway?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Pass a pedestrian or cyclist with the same care as a motor vehicle, slowing and waiting for a safe chance just as you would behind any slow traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which left-turn situation or city-street width allows passing another vehicle on the right?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or about to, or on a city street with clear pavement wide enough for two or more lines of vehicles each way.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Beyond left-turners and wide city streets, on which two other road types is passing on the right legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Passing on the right is also allowed on a one-way street, or on a highway outside a city with clear pavement wide enough and marked for four or more lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does the lane requirement for passing on the right differ between a rural highway and a city street?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: On a highway outside a city, passing on the right needs pavement marked for four or more lanes, while on a city street it needs room for two or more lines of vehicles each way.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: Are you ever allowed to leave the main paved roadway and drive onto the shoulder to pass on the right?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Passing on the right may never be done by leaving the paved main roadway and driving on the shoulder.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: Which three roadway settings or traffic situations heighten the danger of passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Intersections, vehicles inside an intersection and two-lane roads all add to the danger of passing.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: When must you stay off the left side of the road approaching a hill crest or curve?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Do not move to the left side of the road when nearing a hill crest or curve where your view is blocked enough that an oncoming vehicle would create a hazard.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Within what distance of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel is driving left of center banned when sightlines are blocked?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Do not drive left of center within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when your view is obstructed.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Within what distance of intersections or railroad crossings—and alongside which pavement stripe—must you stay right of center?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Do not drive left of center within one hundred feet of or at an intersection or railroad grade crossing, or anywhere a solid yellow line is present.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Which two distinct groups of road features share Missouri's one-hundred-foot no-passing rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: The same one hundred-foot distance marks two different no-passing zones on this page: near a bridge, viaduct or tunnel with an obstructed view, and near an intersection or railroad grade crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: When must drivers yield to pedestrians near streets, driveways, or alleys, and when is driving on a sidewalk legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Drivers yield as needed to avoid hitting pedestrians crossing legally, and anyone crossing a sidewalk or entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking lot yields to pedestrians; driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: To which vehicles must a driver turning left at an intersection yield?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A driver turning left yields to oncoming vehicles going straight.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: At a four-way stop, which driver has priority to proceed first?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the driver who reaches the intersection first goes first, after stopping completely.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls out from an alley, driveway, or roadside?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: A driver entering a road from a driveway, alley or the roadside yields to vehicles already on the main road.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: At an open intersection without stop signs or lights—other than a roundabout—who gets priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: At an intersection with no stop sign or signal, other than a roundabout, yield to vehicles coming from your right.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Before entering a roundabout, which two groups must you yield to while waiting for a gap?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Approaching a roundabout, yield to traffic already circulating and to pedestrians in the crosswalks, and wait for a gap before entering.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Compare who goes first at a four-way stop, an uncontrolled intersection, and a roundabout?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: A four-way stop goes by arrival order, an uncontrolled intersection goes to the vehicle on the right, and a roundabout goes to traffic already in the circle.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction using a siren or air horn and red or blue lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Yield to police, fire, ambulance and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with a red or blue flashing light by pulling to the right edge of the road, or as near as possible, from whichever direction they come.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection, and before resuming?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: If you are already in an intersection, drive through it before pulling over, stay stopped until the emergency vehicle passes, follow loudspeaker instructions, and move on only when the way is clear because more may follow.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: On a road of four or more lanes with at least two going your way, how should you pass a stopped red- or red-and-blue-lit emergency vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Nearing a stopped emergency vehicle showing red or red and blue lights on a road with at least four lanes and two or more going your way, move with caution into a lane not next to it if that is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What must you do near a stopped emergency vehicle if changing lanes away from it is unsafe or impossible?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: If changing lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle would be unsafe or impossible, slow down and keep a speed that is safe for conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How do the warning signals requiring you to pull right for a moving emergency vehicle differ from the stopped-vehicle rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: A moving emergency vehicle you must pull over for uses a siren or air horn with red or blue flashing lights, while the stopped-vehicle rule is triggered by red or red and blue lights on a stationary vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: How far ahead of a stop does a school bus start flashing amber lights, and what signals come on once stopped?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A school bus flashes amber warning lights five hundred feet before a designated stop, then shows alternating flashing red lights and its stop arm once stopped.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What school-bus warning action begins five hundred feet before a designated student stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: The five hundred-foot figure is the distance before a stop at which a school bus starts its amber warning lights.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which directions of traffic must halt for a stopped school bus showing red lights and its stop arm on two-lane two-way or one-way streets?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: When the bus's red lights and stop arm are on, oncoming and following traffic must stop before reaching it on a two-lane road with traffic both ways and on a two-lane one-way street.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: In which three roadway or loading-zone situations are you not required to stop for a school bus flashing red?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: You need not stop when traveling the opposite way on a divided highway whose directions are on totally separate roadways, the opposite way on a highway of four or more lanes, or when the bus is in a school loading zone where students do not cross.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Why don't oncoming drivers stop on a highway of four or more lanes, and what matching rule restricts the bus there?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: The four-lane rule for school buses cuts both ways: drivers going the opposite way on a highway of four or more lanes need not stop, and a bus may not load or unload where riders would cross more than two lanes of such a highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Once stopped for an unloading school bus, when may you start moving again?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: After stopping for an unloading school bus, watch for children along the roadside and stay stopped until the bus moves or its driver signals you on, then proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: How many points go onto your Missouri driving record if convicted of failing to stop for a school bus?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: A conviction for failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students carries five points.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What court-ordered suspension lengths apply to first, second, and third school-bus stop violations within five years?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus brings a court-ordered suspension of ninety days or as the court sets for a first offense, ninety days for a second offense within five years, and one hundred eighty days for a third or later offense within five years.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: On which repeat offense within five years does the Missouri school-bus suspension jump from ninety to one hundred eighty days?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: The school bus suspension doubles only at a third or later offense within five years, to one hundred eighty days, while a second offense within five years stays at ninety days.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: Before which three maneuvers must you signal, and what two signaling methods are allowed?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Signal before stopping, turning or changing lanes using hand and arm signals or your turn signals and brake lights, and check often that the vehicle signals work.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: At least how far before a turn must you enter the proper turn lane and start signaling?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Move into the proper turn lane and signal at least one hundred feet before a turn, and look both ways for oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Why does Missouri tell drivers to start signaling at least one hundred feet ahead of a turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: You should signal at least one hundred feet before turning so the drivers around you can get ready.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: When no signs or lane arrows mark a turn, which lane do you start from and which lane do you turn into?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: With no signs or lane markings, turn from the lane nearest the direction you are heading into the lane nearest the one you left, then change lanes afterward if needed.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: What crash risk do you create if you swing wide to the left before making a right turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: Swinging wide to the left before a right turn can lead the driver behind to think you are turning left and pass you on the right.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: While turning left, what corner mistake must you avoid and what space must you leave for opposing left-turners?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: On a left turn, avoid cutting the corner into traffic coming from the left, but leave room for oncoming drivers to turn left in front of you.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Where do you line up and enter when turning left off a one-way road onto two-way traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street, start in the left lane and enter to the right of the yellow dividing line, using the right lane of a four-lane road if it is free.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Where do your left wheels start and where do you enter when turning left from one two-way street onto another?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street, keep your left wheels as close as possible to the yellow line and enter to the right of the center line, using the right lane of a four-lane road if it is free.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: When turning left from a two-way street onto a two-lane one-way street, where do you start and which lane may you enter?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: Turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street, start with your left wheel close to the yellow dividing line and, if the one-way road has two lanes, turn into whichever lane is free of traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: At an intersection with side-by-side dual left-turn lanes, which receiving lane must each turning car enter?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: With two left-turn lanes, a car in the left-side turn lane enters the left lane just right of the yellow line, and a car in the right-side turn lane enters the right lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: In which four specific roadway or intersection settings are U-turns strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Make a U-turn only when safe, never on a curve or near a hill crest where others may not see you, never at a No U-Turn sign, and never at an intersection controlled by a signal or police officer; some towns ban them.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: What is the sole legal use of a center two-way left-turn lane, what distance cap applies, and what side-street move is banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Enter a center two-way left-turn lane only to slow or stop before a left turn from the main road, never travel in it more than five hundred feet, and never use it when entering from a side street.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: What is the maximum distance you may travel inside a shared center two-way left-turn lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: The five hundred-foot figure is also the most you may travel in a center two-way left-turn lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Which direction do vehicles circulate around a roundabout island, and which three road users get priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: At a roundabout you make a slight right turn and travel counterclockwise around the center island, yielding to traffic in the circle, bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalks.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: Which four steps prepare you safely as you approach a multi-lane roundabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Slow down before a roundabout, follow signs and markings to the correct lane in a multi-lane one, look left as you approach, and never make a left turn to enter.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: Once inside a roundabout, what four rules govern island side, lane changes, passing, and stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.memory_hook: Keep right, never pass, keep moving
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: While driving through a roundabout, keep right of the center island, yield the right-of-way to circulating vehicles, never change lanes or try to pass any vehicle, and do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: What speed and signal do you use when leaving a roundabout, and when may you accelerate?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Leave a roundabout at a slow speed with your right turn signal on, and do not speed up until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: How do you handle an approaching emergency vehicle before entering a roundabout versus when already inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Do not enter a roundabout when an emergency vehicle is approaching, and if one comes while you are inside, exit immediately and pull to the right.
