sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: What two crash-reducing design features make roundabouts safer than standard intersections, and what sign guards every entry?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: Roundabouts lower fatal and injury crashes by cutting speeds and removing left turns across opposing traffic, and every entering leg has a yield sign.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: What should you do if you miss your roundabout exit, and how should you drive near large trucks or trailers inside?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: If you miss your exit in a roundabout, keep circling until you reach it, and give trucks and trailers room because they may use more than one lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: What is a roundabout truck apron, which wheels use it, and which everyday vehicles must stay off it?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: A truck apron is the paved inner area of a roundabout for the rear wheels of large trucks, and cars, SUVs and pickup trucks must not use it.

sec04-card-sec04-R18.front: At a Missouri four-lane highway J-turn intersection, what three-step sequence replaces crossing straight across fast traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-R18.expected_back: At a J-turn intersection on a four-lane highway, instead of crossing fast traffic you turn right with traffic, merge to the far left lane, and then turn left in the direction you want to go.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which directions should your eyes sweep on the highway — how long may eyes leave the road — and how do you check a map?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Keep scanning ahead, to the sides and behind, and never look away from the road for more than a few seconds; to study a map, first pull safely off the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which lane is your travel lane on a two-lane highway — and what two checks clear crossing the center line?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: On a highway with one lane each way, drive in the right lane, crossing the center line to pass only when no oncoming vehicle is near and there is no solid yellow line.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, which three reasons justify leaving the right lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, stay right except to pass slower traffic, make room for a merging driver, or set up a legal left turn.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Compare lane discipline on a two-lane undivided highway against a highway with four or more lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: On a two-lane highway the right lane is the travel lane and the center line may be crossed to pass, while on four or more lanes you keep right except for passing, merging room or a left turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Why must you glance frequently at your speedometer right after exiting a fast highway onto local streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Control your speed by checking the speedometer often and watching posted limits, especially after leaving a fast road for much slower local streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How are left lanes, right lanes, and shoulders each treated for passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: The left lane is for passing only, the right lane may be used to pass a vehicle turning left, and the shoulder or unpaved edge must never be used for passing.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which two mirrors and which shoulder check come before pulling left to pass on a four-lane highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Before passing on a four-lane highway, check the left lane with your left and inside mirrors and take a quick look over your left shoulder.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What is a blind spot — and what quick action overcomes it before changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A blind spot is an area your rearview mirrors cannot show, which is why a glance over the shoulder is needed before changing lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Where off another car's rear corners should you avoid cruising — and how do you fix it?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Avoid riding just behind and to either side of another vehicle; speed up or drop back so its driver can see you.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: How briskly should you move through another driver's blind spot while overtaking — and what ceiling still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: When passing, move through the other driver's blind spot as fast as you can without going over the speed limit.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What collision risk grows every extra second you camp inside another vehicle's blind spot?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: The longer you stay in another driver's blind spot while passing, the longer you risk that vehicle moving into yours.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Why shouldn't you linger beside or close behind a truck or bus — and what mirror clue confirms visibility?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Do not linger beside or right behind a truck or bus, whose large blind spots hide you; if the trucker's face is not visible in the side mirror, you are not visible to the trucker.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: After overtaking a tractor-trailer, when may you return right — and what pedal mistake must you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: After passing a truck, wait until its cab appears in your rearview mirror before returning to the lane, keep your speed, and do not slow down in front of it.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Once mirrors and blind spots are clear, how do you execute the pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: If the way is clear, signal the lane change, then pass quickly and smoothly without exceeding the limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Which mirror landmark, shoulder glance, and stalk switch clear returning to the right lane after passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Return to the right lane only once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror, after a look over your right shoulder and a signal.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does your over-the-shoulder glance flip between pulling out to pass and tucking back in?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The shoulder check flips with the direction of the lane change: before moving out to pass you look over the left shoulder, and before moving back in you look over the right one.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What two things must you do whenever another driver starts passing you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: When someone starts to pass you, hold your lane and do not speed up.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: If stream after stream of cars passes you on the right on a multi-lane road, what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: If many drivers are passing you on the right in a multi-lane road, you are likely slower than traffic and should move right when clear unless a left turn is coming up.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What speed mismatch triggers many multi-vehicle highway wrecks — and what habit prevents it?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Crashes involving two or more vehicles often happen when one driver goes faster or slower than the others, so keep pace with traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: How little time does speeding actually shave per hour — and what does every extra pass add?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Speeding saves no more than a few minutes an hour, and each pass you make adds another chance of a collision.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: If you drive slower than normal pace and a queue stacks up behind your bumper, what courtesy applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Driving much slower than traffic is also dangerous; if a line of vehicles builds behind you, pull over when safe and let them by.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: How frequently should your eyes flick to your rearview mirrors during highway cruising?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Check your rearview mirrors every few seconds to track traffic coming up behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Why look far ahead for climbing semis or merging compact cars on highway hills?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Spot slow vehicles early, such as heavy trucks and underpowered cars on steep grades or merging, so you can change lanes or ease off instead of braking suddenly.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Which two vehicle types lose speed on long climbs and need extra runway when merging?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Slow trucks and small underpowered vehicles may lose speed on long or steep climbs and need extra time to get up to speed when they join traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: What spacing rule behind the car ahead does Missouri's highway chapter emphasize — and which chapter details it?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Maintain a safe following distance behind the vehicle ahead, as covered in Chapter eight.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Where must you NEVER stop routinely on a highway — and where belong non-emergency stops?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Never stop in the travel lanes of a highway; use rest stops and service areas instead.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: What two dangers make hard highway panic stops risky — and what eye habit avoids them?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Look far enough ahead to avoid panic stops, because hard braking can cost you control and makes it harder for drivers behind to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: How can easing off the gas or changing lanes early improve your stop when traffic slows ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Slowing or changing lanes early may let you avoid stopping entirely, and any stop you do make will be more gradual and safer.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Where are the ONLY legal places to enter or leave a controlled-access highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: A controlled access highway lets you get on or off only at entrance and exit ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: In how many directions may vehicles travel on highway entrance and exit ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Entrance ramps and exit ramps are both short ramps that carry traffic in one direction only.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: What is your speed goal on an entrance ramp and acceleration lane before merging?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Use the entrance ramp and its acceleration lane to reach the speed of highway traffic, then signal and merge smoothly into a gap.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: When is stopping at the end of an acceleration lane ever acceptable?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Stopping where the acceleration lane ends is only for very heavy traffic that leaves you no choice.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: While through drivers should make room, who legally yields if no highway gap opens for a merging car?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Drivers on the highway should make room for you, but if they do not, you must yield to them rather than force your way in, even if that means stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: When should you get into your exit side lane, where do you slow down, and what sign governs ramp speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Move into the correct lane well before the deceleration lane, then use that lane and the exit ramp to slow down, obeying the ramp's advisory speed sign.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: Contrast where acceleration and deceleration lanes sit — and the job of each one?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: An acceleration lane sits at the end of most entrance ramps and is for speeding up, while a deceleration lane sits at the start of most exit ramps and is for slowing down.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: Which three dangerous moves are forbidden if you overshoot your exit — and what is the right fix?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: If you miss your exit, never stop, back up or turn around on the highway; take the next exit and come back.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: How does an interchange connect two busy highways without stoplights across main lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: An interchange is where two busy highways meet using entrance and exit ramps, and it can be confusing the first time you use it.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: Name the four common interchange layouts pictured in the Missouri Driver Guide?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: The guide pictures four common interchange layouts: cloverleaf, diamond, directional and diverging diamond.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What unusual lane position happens briefly inside a Diverging Diamond Interchange — and what guides you through?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: On a Diverging Diamond Interchange you drive on the left side of the road for a short stretch, and directional signs at every interchange help you find your way.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: What mental state is highway hypnosis, and what sights and sounds bring it on?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, unaware state caused by the sameness of the road and traffic and the steady hum of wind, tires and engine.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: What active eye habit prevents highway hypnosis — and what must you do if sleepiness creeps in?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Prevent highway hypnosis by keeping your eyes moving over traffic and signs, and leave the highway if you start to feel sleepy.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: How does severe drowsiness compare with drunk driving — and what should a very sleepy driver do?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: A drowsy driver decides and reacts more slowly and can be as dangerous as a drunk one, so stop at the nearest rest area or service area and nap if very sleepy.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: What single shared solution does the Missouri guide prescribe for both highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: Highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness share one fix in the guide: get off the highway rather than risk falling asleep at the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: What common mental lapse causes many highway crashes — and what mindset counters it?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: Many crashes happen because drivers do not give enough attention to driving, so stay alert for unexpected events.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: When may you stop on a highway shoulder — and what lights plus two visual distress signals help?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: In an emergency you may stop on the shoulder; turn on your emergency flashers, and raising the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna also helps.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Together with emergency flashers, which two non-electric distress signals does page thirty-nine suggest on the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A white cloth on the antenna and a raised hood are the signals suggested for an emergency stop on the shoulder, together with emergency flashers.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Why is making yourself and your stalled vehicle unmistakable so critical after a highway breakdown?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: After a breakdown, make sure other drivers can see you and your vehicle, since crashes happen when a stalled car is noticed too late.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: When mechanical trouble hits at highway speed, what are your first two priorities?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: With vehicle trouble, get off the road and away from traffic if at all possible, and turn on your emergency flashers.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: If your car dies where leaving the roadway is impossible, which two blind spots must you avoid stopping past?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can clearly see you, not just past a hill crest or around a curve.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: Where do emergency flares go relative to a disabled vehicle — and what message do they send?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Set emergency flares behind a disabled vehicle to warn drivers to change lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: What roadway tire-changing ban applies — and which three exterior parts can hold a white distress cloth?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Never stand in the roadway or change a tire from inside a traffic lane; signal trouble by lifting the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror or door handle.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Modern cars often lack tall whip antennas — which two other exterior parts does page forty-one list for a white cloth?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: The breakdown page adds the side mirror and door handle as places to tie a white cloth, beyond the antenna.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How is a standard stop sign shaped and colored, and what action does it require?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.memory_hook: Red octagon, white letters, full stop
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: A stop sign is an eight-sided red sign with white letters, and it requires a full stop and a wait until crossing traffic and pedestrians have cleared.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How is a yield sign shaped and colored, and how must you handle intersecting traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: A yield sign is a red and white triangle with red letters that means slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or road you are joining.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What visual differences in sides and letter colors separate a stop sign from a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: A stop sign is red with white letters and eight sides, while a yield sign is a triangle in red and white with red letters.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: What separates your legal obligation at a stop sign from your obligation at a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: A stop sign demands a full stop every time, while a yield sign demands slowing and giving way to traffic already in the intersection or on the road you are entering.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Where do you halt when a white stop line sits past the sign post, and where when none exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Stop at the stop line when there is one, even if it is beyond the sign; without a line, stop near the edge of the intersection, look both ways and go when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: In what one-two-three priority order do you pick your exact stopping spot at a stop sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: The stopping point order is the stop line first, then the crosswalk if there is no line, and otherwise just before entering the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What mistake has happened if you face a Wrong Way sign, and how must you fix it?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.memory_hook: Oncoming lane; pull off, turn back
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign means you turned into a lane of oncoming traffic, so pull off, turn around and go back as quickly and safely as you can.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What rule does a Do Not Enter sign enforce at a road opening, and what does One Way indicate?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign at a road opening means you may not drive into that road, and a One Way sign means traffic there moves in a single direction.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How does encountering a Wrong Way sign differ from seeing a Do Not Enter sign at an opening?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.memory_hook: Do Not Enter prevents; Wrong corrects
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign means you are already in an oncoming lane, while a Do Not Enter sign at a road opening warns you not to go in at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Where are lane control signs mounted, and how do they assign movements to individual lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.memory_hook: Side or overhead arrows assign lanes
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Lane control signs, posted beside or above the road, use arrows to show which way each lane may go.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Which path around a median nose or roadway obstruction does a Keep Right sign require?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: A Keep Right sign means traffic must pass only on the right side of a feature or obstruction.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What conditions does a posted speed limit sign assume, and when does Missouri law require going slower?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: A speed limit sign shows the legal maximum under ideal conditions, and the law requires you to slow down when hills, curves, slick roads, short sight lines, pedestrians, cyclists or slow vehicles make that speed unsafe.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What is Missouri's normal minimum speed on an interstate, and what should you do if you cannot hold it?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Interstates also have minimum speeds, and under normal conditions you may not drive slower than forty miles per hour on an interstate; if that is too fast for you, use another route.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Inside a Missouri city, town, or village with no speed sign posted, what legal limit applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Inside a city, town or village the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour whenever no other limit is posted.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Contrast Missouri's unposted municipal speed cap with its normal interstate minimum speed?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: The twenty-five miles per hour default applies inside cities, towns and villages, while forty miles per hour is the floor for normal interstate driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: Which Missouri body can raise or lower speed limits from uniform defaults, and for what two reasons?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: The Missouri Highway and Transportation Commission may set limits above or below the uniform maximums for safety or to keep traffic moving.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What default top speed does the Missouri Driver Guide list for rural expressways?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: The guide's default maximum for rural expressways is sixty-five miles per hour

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Which two road categories share Missouri's sixty-mile-per-hour default maximum in the guide?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: The guide's default maximum is sixty miles per hour both for interstates, freeways and expressways inside urbanized areas and for other roads outside urbanized areas.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What default maximum speed applies on Missouri's supplementary lettered roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Lettered roads have a default maximum speed of fifty-five miles per hour

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Roughly how many miles of interstate cross Missouri, and why do urban stretches often post lower caps?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: The guide says Missouri has more than one thousand three hundred miles of interstate highway, and lower limits are often posted on urban interstates where interchanges and merging traffic are frequent.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Which sign shape and road feature warn you ahead of time that railroad tracks are coming up?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A round advance warning sign, and in some places a pavement marking, tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What traffic rule does a white X-shaped crossbuck enforce, and what does a small plaque underneath tell you?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: The white X-shaped crossbuck at a crossing means the same as a yield sign, so you must yield to trains, and a sign beneath it gives the number of tracks.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do the shape and location of a railroad advance warning sign differ from a crossbuck?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.memory_hook: Round warns early; X sits trackside
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: The railroad advance warning sign is round, which sets it apart from the X-shaped crossbuck placed at the crossing itself.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What two deadly mistakes must you never make when approaching or starting across railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Never race a train to a crossing, and never start across the tracks until there is room for your whole vehicle on the far side.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Why must you avoid shifting gears while your tires are crossing railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Avoid shifting gears while crossing railroad tracks in case the vehicle stalls.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What is your legal duty at a crossing with alternating red flashers or a lowering gate?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Where a crossing has alternately flashing red lights or a lowering gate, you must stop and stay stopped until the train has passed.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does your legal duty at a standalone crossbuck differ from active red lights or lowered gates?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A crossbuck by itself carries a yield duty, while alternately flashing red lights or a lowered gate carry a duty to stop and wait for the train.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: How many feet from the nearest rail must you stop for flashing lights or lowered gates, and what is banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.memory_hook: Stop fifteen to fifty; never dodge
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: When the red lights flash or the gate is down, stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest track, and never drive around the gate.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: After one train clears a multi-track crossing, why watch the lights and adjacent rails before moving?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.memory_hook: Lights stay on; check second train
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Crossing lights may keep flashing after a train clears, and where there are two or more tracks, check for a second train before crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What specific shade identifies Missouri work-zone signs, and who or what directs cars through the zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Work zone signs are fluorescent orange, and flaggers or other devices may guide you through the work area.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: Name four common warning messages posted on orange Missouri work-zone signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.memory_hook: Road Work, Oil, Gravel, Lane Closed
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Common work zone signs include Road Work Ahead, Fresh Oil, Loose Gravel and Right Lane Closed Ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Why should spotting orange work-zone signs immediately put you on high alert?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.memory_hook: Active crews on or beside road
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: Be extremely careful whenever work zone signs appear, because some kind of work is going on on the roadway or beside it.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: What five habits keep everyone safe while driving through any highway work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.memory_hook: Drop distractions, obey signs, watch trucks
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: In any work zone, stay alert for lower speed limits, narrow lanes and workers, avoid distractions, obey the signs and watch for vehicles moving in and out.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What minimum fines hit drivers caught speeding or passing inside a Missouri state-road work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: On Missouri state roads, a driver caught speeding or passing in a work zone faces a minimum fine of two hundred fifty dollars the first time and three hundred dollars for each repeat, plus any other lawful fines.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: How does recognizing Missouri's different work-zone setups help you behind the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Missouri roads have several kinds of work zones, and knowing them helps you predict what you will meet as you drive through.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How should you adjust as you approach a shoulder work zone where crews stay off the main lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.memory_hook: Ease off speed passing shoulder work
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: For a shoulder work zone, where the work is on or past the shoulder, reduce speed as you approach.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What two steps are required when a work zone closes one of the lanes ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: For a lane closure, merge into the marked open lane and slow to the posted work zone speed limit.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: How does what a shoulder work zone asks of drivers differ from a full lane closure?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: A shoulder work zone asks you mainly to slow down, while a lane closure also asks you to merge into an open lane and drop to the work zone speed limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: How does a flagging operation manage traffic on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.memory_hook: One lane shared; flaggers both ends
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: A flagging operation closes one lane of a two-lane, two-way road, with flaggers at each end, so be ready to stop and follow their directions.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What characterizes a mobile work zone, and what hazard should you expect beside the equipment?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: In a mobile work zone, slow or stopped work vehicles move along a travel lane and workers may step out, so expect them near the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: What trailing safety vehicle warns you as you catch up to a mobile work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Approaching a mobile work zone, look for a protective vehicle in the lane with a flashing arrow panel showing which lane to merge into, often signed Slow Vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: When overtaking a mobile work zone, what guides your lane choice and what lies ahead of the shadow truck?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: In a mobile work zone, follow the direction shown on the flashing arrow panel and watch for several slow or stopped work vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Contrast a two-lane flagging operation with a highway mobile work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: A flagging operation is a fixed site on a two-lane road with flaggers at both ends, while a mobile work zone moves along a travel lane behind a protective vehicle with an arrow panel.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: How do green and brown guide signs look, and which destinations do each point toward?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Guide signs are green or brown squares or rectangles with white letters showing direction and distance to cities, airports and state lines or to parks, historic sites and museums.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What colors and shapes identify motorist service signs, and what stops do they mark?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: Service signs are blue squares or rectangles with white letters or symbols marking services such as rest areas and hospitals.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: What background color distinction separates guide signs from motorist service signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Guide signs are green or brown with white lettering, while service signs are blue with white letters or symbols.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: Which official Missouri vehicle-check sign appears alongside guide and service signs in the driver manual?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: The guide pictures an Authorized Safety Inspection Station sign among the guide and service signs.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: What single feature of a numbered highway route marker tells you its road classification?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: The shape of a route sign tells you the road type, whether interstate, United States, state or county.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: What simple two-part habit keeps you from getting lost on unfamiliar highways?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Plan a trip with a highway map and follow the route signs along the way so you do not get lost.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: How do odd-numbered and even-numbered highway routes align with compass directions?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Routes running north and south carry odd numbers, and routes running east and west carry even numbers.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: On a three-digit Missouri interstate like I-270 or I-155, what does an even versus odd first digit mean?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: A three-digit interstate number starting with an even digit, such as I-two hundred seventy or I-four hundred thirty-five, loops around a city, while one starting with an odd digit, such as I-one hundred fifty-five or I-one hundred seventy, is a spur into a city.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: How does the leading digit split three-digit interstate routes between city loops and city spurs?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Three-digit interstate numbers split by first digit: even means a loop around a city, odd means a spur into it.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: Where do interstate exit numbers begin at zero, and in which compass directions do they climb?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: Exit numbers on east-west interstates start at zero in the west and rise heading east, and on north-south interstates they start in the south and rise heading north.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: In which two travel directions do interstate exit numbers count downward?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Driving west on an east-west interstate, exit numbers get smaller, and driving south on a north-south interstate, they also get smaller.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Where sit emergency reference markers, what details do they display, and how closely are they spaced?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: Emergency reference markers along the outside shoulder mark the road edge and show direction and route number, and they are spaced every two-tenths of a mile so one is always in view.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: Before registering or renewing tags on many Missouri vehicles, what check is required unless an exemption applies?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Many vehicles need a safety inspection before they can be registered or have their registration renewed, though some are exempt.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: Who is allowed to run a Missouri safety inspection, and how can drivers recognize an authorized shop?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Any licensed inspection station may perform the safety inspection, and authorized stations display an official sign.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What mailed document helps you confirm whether your upcoming plate renewal requires a safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Your registration renewal notice helps you tell whether your next renewal needs an inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: How many registration years does a single Missouri safety inspection cover, and what event cuts that short?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: One safety inspection covers two registration years, unless the vehicle is sold in between.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: How do even and odd vehicle model years line up with calendar years for Missouri safety inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Even model year vehicles are inspected when their registration expires in an even calendar year, and odd model year vehicles in an odd calendar year.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: What is the maximum dollar fee an authorized Missouri station may charge for a standard inspection versus a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: An official inspection station may charge no more than twelve dollars for an inspection, or up to ten dollars for a motorcycle.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: How does Missouri's safety inspection fee cap differ between standard vehicles and motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: The inspection fee cap is twelve dollars for most vehicles and ten dollars for a motorcycle.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: What proof does a vehicle earn upon passing safety inspection, and how many days does it stay valid?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: A vehicle that passes receives a certificate of inspection as proof, and that certificate is good for sixty days.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: When does a safety inspection certificate provided by a Missouri dealer stay good for ninety days?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: A certificate from a Missouri dealer is good for ninety days when the inspection was done within sixty days before the purchase date.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: How does a standard station's sixty-day certificate window compare with a qualifying Missouri dealer certificate?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: A station's certificate is good for sixty days, but a Missouri dealer's certificate is good for ninety days when the inspection was within sixty days before the sale.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What age and odometer combination exempts a vehicle—even with an out-of-state title—from Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: Vehicles are exempt from safety inspection for the first ten years after their model year while they have under one hundred fifty thousand miles, including vehicles with an out-of-state title.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: Through which calendar year does a twenty seventeen model-year car under one hundred fifty thousand miles skip safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: For example, a two thousand seventeen model year vehicle that stays under one hundred fifty thousand miles is exempt from safety inspection through calendar year two thousand twenty-seven.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Which towed units, specialty tags, condition sales, and wholesale transfers never need a Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: All trailers are exempt from the safety inspection, as are vehicles with historic plates, vehicles sold for junk, salvage or rebuilding, and dealer-to-dealer sales.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: Which MoDOT-registered commercial vehicles and statutory small vehicles also skip Missouri's standard safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Vehicles in intrastate commerce registered with the Missouri Department of Transportation and low speed vehicles as defined by statute are also exempt from safety inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: When does a truck registered at twenty-six thousand pounds or more for under twelve months skip safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Vehicles registered for twenty-six thousand pounds or more for less than twelve months need no inspection if the registration is issued or renewed on or after April one, even though the renewal notice lists one.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: What condition must a vehicle's braking system meet to pass a Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: To pass, a vehicle's brakes must be in good working order.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What minimum number and color of working headlights must a vehicle carry?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: A vehicle must have at least two working white headlights.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: What rear lights and reflector visibility distance are required on a Missouri vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: A vehicle must have at least two working red taillights plus reflectors that other drivers can see from five hundred feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: What standard governs how a vehicle's turn signals and brake lights must function?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Turn signals and brake lights must work as the manufacturer originally installed them.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: Which two steering-system flaws will keep a vehicle from passing safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: The steering must not have too much play or bind.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: Which two tire conditions fail a Missouri vehicle safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: Bald or mismatched tires are not allowed.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: What must be true of a vehicle's horn and windshield wipers during safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: A vehicle needs a working horn that other drivers and pedestrians can hear, and its windshield wipers must work.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: Which three exhaust-system components must be securely attached on a vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: A vehicle must have an attached exhaust pipe, muffler and tailpipe.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: What two conditions must fuel lines, hoses, connections, and tanks meet at inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: The fuel system, including lines, hoses, connections and tanks, must be firmly attached and free of leaks.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: Vehicles manufactured after what date must carry safety glass in every window?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen thirty-six must have safety glass in every window.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What damage and clutter rules govern your windshield's viewing area, and what two exceptions are allowed?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: The windshield's viewing area may not be badly broken, and nothing on it may reduce visibility except legally required stickers and informational signs on the factory-tinted upper strip.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: Passenger cars built after what date must carry how many sets of front seat belts?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: A passenger car made after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four must have two sets of seat belts in the front seat.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: Vehicles built after which year must carry both an inside and an outside rearview mirror?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: A vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must have both an inside and an outside rearview mirror.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: Which vehicles must retain their factory-installed air pollution control devices?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: A non-diesel vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must keep its air pollution control devices as the manufacturer installed them.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: Does the post-nineteen-sixty-seven safety-inspection rule on factory air pollution devices apply to diesel vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: The pollution control requirement for vehicles made after nineteen sixty-seven does not apply to diesel vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Match the three classic equipment cutoffs in chronological order across nineteen thirty-six, nineteen sixty-four, and nineteen sixty-seven?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: Three model-year cutoffs on the equipment list are easy to mix up: safety glass after January one, nineteen thirty-six, front seat belts after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four, and mirrors and pollution controls after nineteen sixty-seven.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: Which trucks are required by Missouri law to have rear mud flaps installed?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Trucks registered for over twenty-four thousand pounds that lack rear fenders must have mud flaps.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: What is the maximum legal height above the ground for a passenger vehicle's bumpers?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: A passenger vehicle's bumpers may not be higher than twenty-two inches above the ground at their highest point.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: How are maximum bumper heights determined for commercial vehicles compared with passenger cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: Commercial vehicle bumper heights are set by gross vehicle weight rating, unlike the fixed limit for passenger vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Beyond safety-inspection checklist items, what three exterior identification or warning items does Missouri law require?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Beyond the inspection equipment, Missouri law also requires additional equipment such as plates, plate lights and signs.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: How must your Missouri license plates be mounted and maintained, and what rule governs decorative plate frames?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: License plates must be firmly fastened, fully visible and clean, and any plate frame must not cover any part of the plate.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: Where do plates mount when issued as a pair, and where does the single plate go on a trailer or motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: If you get two plates, one goes on the front and one on the back; a trailer or motorcycle gets one plate, mounted on the back.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: Where does a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds mount its single plate, and how does the rear get one?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: A truck licensed for more than twelve thousand pounds gets one plate for the front, and a second plate, if requested, goes on the rear.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: While trailers and motorcycles mount their single plate on the back, which vehicle mounts its single plate on the front?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: Most single plates go on the back, as for trailers and motorcycles, but the single plate of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds goes on the front.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: How does a heavy-truck owner above twelve thousand pounds get a rear tag, and where does the first tag stay?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: The owner of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds receives a second plate only by asking for it specifically, and the original plate stays on the front.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: What color lamp must illuminate your rear license plate, and from what distance must the plate be readable?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: A white light must shine on the rear plate so it can be read from fifty feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: When cargo sticks out more than five feet past the rear, what daytime flag and nighttime light are required?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: A load extending more than five feet past the rear must carry a red flag or cloth at least sixteen inches square during the day and a red light from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: What maximum towline gap applies when towing another vehicle, and during what hours must both vehicles show lights?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: When towing another vehicle, the towline must keep the two vehicles within fifteen feet of one another, and both vehicles must display lights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: Which slow vehicles need a reflective emblem between sunset and half-hour pre-sunrise, and where does it mount?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: From sunset to half an hour before sunrise, any vehicle going twenty-five miles per hour or slower must show a clean, reflective slow moving vehicle sign on the rear, near the middle, at least four feet above the road.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Between the slow-moving vehicle emblem, projecting-load lights, and towing lights, which rule starts right at sunset?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: The slow moving vehicle sign starts at sunset, while the projection light and towing lights start half an hour after sunset; all three run until half an hour before sunrise.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: Between which exact calendar dates may Missouri drivers legally use studded snow tires?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Studded snow tires are allowed only from November one to April one.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: Which windows may carry tint or sun-screening, and what light-blockage cap applies to front door glass?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: Tint or sun-screening is allowed on side and rear windows, with the front door windows limited to no more than sixty-five percent light blockage.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: Residents of which Missouri city and four surrounding counties must complete vehicle emissions inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: Drivers living in St. Louis City and in St. Louis, St. Charles, Franklin and Jefferson counties must also get emissions inspections where they apply.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: How frequently do emissions inspections run, and how does their model-year calendar match safety inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: The emissions inspection is a two-year inspection on the same even and odd schedule as the safety inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: Regardless of model year, what ownership event normally triggers a required emissions check unless exempt?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: Vehicles must pass an emissions inspection when sold, whatever their model year, unless an exception applies.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: When do brand-new vehicles and first retail sales skip the at-sale emissions check?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: New vehicles and first retail sales of titled vehicles during the model year and the next year are exempt at sale if the odometer reads under six thousand miles.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.front: How long do brand-new, never-previously-titled vehicles skip emissions unconditionally—and what keeps that waiver active?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.expected_back: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt during the model year and the following year as long as ownership does not change.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: What mileage reading at the first biennial check extends a brand-new untitled vehicle's emissions waiver to four years?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt for the four years after their model year if they have fewer than forty thousand miles at the first required biennial inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: Which older model years are exempt from Missouri emissions testing for gasoline vehicles versus diesel vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: The emissions cutoffs differ by fuel: gasoline vehicles of nineteen ninety-five and older and diesel vehicles of nineteen ninety-six and older are exempt.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Above what manufacturer gross vehicle weight rating is a vehicle exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: Vehicles with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over eight thousand five hundred pounds are exempt from emissions inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.front: Driving fewer than how many miles between biennial checks exempts a vehicle from emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.expected_back: Vehicles driven fewer than twelve thousand miles between biennial inspections are exempt from emissions inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.front: Vehicles powered exclusively by fuels outside which three standard fuels skip Missouri emissions testing?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.expected_back: Vehicles running on fuels other than gasoline, ethanol or diesel are exempt from emissions inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.front: Which six specialty, bus, or two-wheel license plate categories are exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.expected_back: Vehicles with historic, school bus, shuttle bus, motorcycle, motortricycle or street rod plates are exempt from emissions inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.front: In which single county are gasoline-powered low-speed vehicles exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.expected_back: Gasoline-powered low speed vehicles are exempt from emissions inspection in Franklin County only.

sec16-card-sec16-R20.front: How long must an emissions-area vehicle be based and driven outside the zone to qualify as exempt?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.expected_back: A vehicle registered in the emissions area but based and driven outside it for twenty-four consecutive months is exempt.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Does Missouri treat driving as a constitutional right or an earned privilege, and how can you lose it?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and you can lose it by breaking the traffic laws.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What happens to your driving record when you are convicted of a traffic offense committed while your vehicle was moving?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: When you are convicted of a traffic violation that happened while your vehicle was moving, the Department is notified and adds points to your driving record.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: Does merely getting pulled over add points in Missouri, or what exact event puts points on your record?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: Points are tied to convictions: the Department adds them once it is notified that you were convicted of a moving violation.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What is the ultimate consequence of letting too many violation points pile up on your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Collecting too many points can cost you your driving privilege.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Why can a speeding conviction add either two or three points to your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: How many points you get depends on the conviction; a speeding conviction may bring two or three points depending on whether the court was municipal, county or state.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How many points is speeding worth on the Missouri Driver Guide's state-law violation list?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: In the guide's list of state law violations, speeding is worth three points.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Why does one part of the point-system chapter mention two or three points for speeding while the table lists three?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: The guide's example says speeding may bring two or three points depending on the court level, while its list of state law violations shows speeding at three points.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How many points hit your record for a careless and imprudent driving conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Careless and imprudent driving is worth four points.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: How many points do you get for knowingly letting an unlicensed person drive a vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Knowingly letting an unlicensed driver operate a vehicle is worth four points.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Which two violations in the Missouri point table both carry four points?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Careless and imprudent driving and knowingly letting an unlicensed person drive carry the same value, four points each.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: How many points are assessed for failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students is worth five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What point total and license action can result from leaving the scene of a traffic crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a traffic crash can bring twelve points and the revocation of your driving privilege.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How many points does a felony involving a motor vehicle add to your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: A felony involving a motor vehicle is worth twelve points.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How many points are added for obtaining a driver license through misrepresentation?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Getting a driver license through misrepresentation is worth twelve points.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: How many points is driving on a suspended or revoked driver license worth?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Driving with a suspended or revoked driver license is worth twelve points.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Which four state-law violation examples in this chapter each carry twelve points?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Examples of state-law violations carrying twelve points include leaving the scene of a traffic crash, a felony involving a motor vehicle, obtaining a license by misrepresentation, and driving with a suspended or revoked license.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What does the state send you if you accumulate four points within twelve months?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Reaching a total of four points within twelve months gets you a point accumulation advisory from the Department.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: How many points within what number of months get your Missouri driving privilege suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Reaching eight or more points within eighteen months gets your driving privilege suspended.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does hitting four points in twelve months differ from hitting eight points in eighteen months?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Four points in twelve months brings only an advisory letter; a suspension starts at eight or more points in eighteen months.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How long does an eight-points-in-eighteen-months suspension last on the first, second, and third or later time?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: A suspension for eight points in eighteen months lasts thirty days the first time, sixty days the second time, and ninety days the third or any later time.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: Which three point-and-month combinations trigger a one-year revocation of your driving privilege?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Your driving privilege is revoked for one year if you reach twelve or more points in twelve months, eighteen or more in twenty-four months, or twenty-four or more in thirty-six months.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: What simple math pattern connects Missouri's three point-revocation thresholds?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Across the three revocation thresholds, each step adds six points and twelve months: twelve in twelve, eighteen in twenty-four, and twenty-four in thirty-six.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: What key factor changes the requirements to reinstate your license after a point suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Reinstatement requirements after a point suspension or revocation differ depending on whether it was related to alcohol.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: What two items reinstate your license after a point suspension or revocation that was NOT related to alcohol?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: To reinstate after a point suspension or revocation not related to alcohol, you submit SR-twenty-two proof of insurance and pay a twenty dollars reinstatement fee.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: Which chapter of the Missouri Driver Guide covers the full details on filing SR-twenty-two proof of insurance?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Details on filing SR-twenty-two proof of insurance are in the mandatory insurance chapter of the guide.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Where in the guide are the reinstatement items listed when a point suspension or revocation involved intoxication?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Following an intoxication-related point suspension or revocation, reinstatement requires submitting the items listed on page seventy-one of the guide.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: When the state reinstates your driving privilege after a suspension or revocation, what number does your point total drop to?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Once your driving privilege is reinstated, the Department lowers your point total to four.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Does the drop to four points happen at reinstatement itself, or only after a clean year of driving?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: The point total is lowered to four at reinstatement, before any yearly reduction begins.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: How much are your remaining points reduced after one full year of driving with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: After one year of driving with no new points, the remaining points are cut by one-third.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: How much are your remaining points reduced after two consecutive years with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: After two years with no new points, the remaining points are cut by one-half.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: What happens to your point balance after three straight years with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: After three years with no new points, the points drop to zero.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: What is the year-by-year sequence of point reductions across three clean years?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Point reduction goes one-third after the first clean year, one-half after the second, and zero after the third, so the cuts get larger each year.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: When three clean years drop your points to zero, do all past convictions vanish from your driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Even when your points reach zero, certain convictions stay on your driving record permanently.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: Beyond points, what license action can follow a conviction for driving while your privilege is suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: A conviction for driving during a suspension may lead to a one-year revocation of your driving privilege.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: What criminal charge and license penalty can hit if you keep driving during a revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Continuing to drive during a revocation can bring a felony conviction and another one-year revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: What major extra risk separates driving while revoked from driving while suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Driving while suspended may lead to a one-year revocation, but driving while revoked can be a felony with another one-year revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: If you miss a traffic court date, how many days does the court give you to pay fines before reporting you to the bureau?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: When you miss a court date for a traffic violation, the court notifies you and gives you thirty days to pay the fines before it tells the Driver License Bureau.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What happens if you still fail to resolve a missed traffic court date within those thirty days?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: If you still do not comply within those thirty days, the court notifies the Driver License Bureau and your driving privilege is suspended at once.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: Does a failure-to-appear suspension end after a set number of days, or what ends it?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: A suspension for failing to appear lasts until the Bureau receives proof the ticket is paid and a twenty dollars reinstatement fee.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: Why are you still suspended if you pay an overdue traffic fine at the courthouse and immediately drive home?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Paying the ticket alone does not end a failure to appear suspension, because the twenty dollars reinstatement fee is also required.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Which two ways can you submit your paid-ticket proof and reinstatement fee for a failure-to-appear suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: You can send the reinstatement requirements for a failure to appear suspension by mail to the Driver License Bureau or bring them to its central office in Jefferson City.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: When convicted of failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students, how many points hit your record?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: A conviction for failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students carries five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: What suspension comes with a first offense for failing to stop for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: A first school bus offense brings a court-ordered suspension of ninety days, or another period the court sets.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: On a first school-bus stop offense, is the court locked into ordering ninety days?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: For a first school bus offense, the court can set a suspension period other than the standard one.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: Within a five-year window, what suspensions apply to a second and a third or later school-bus offense?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: A second school bus offense within five years brings a ninety-day suspension, and a third or later offense within five years brings one hundred eighty days.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How do first, second, and third school-bus stop suspensions progress when repeats happen within five years?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: For failing to stop for a school bus, a first offense brings a court-ordered suspension of ninety days or another period set by the court, a second offense within five years brings ninety days, and a third or later offense within five years brings one hundred eighty days.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How do Missouri's three school-bus suspension lengths differ from the three eight-point suspension lengths?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: School bus suspensions run ninety, ninety and then one hundred eighty days, unlike the point suspensions of thirty, sixty and ninety days.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: Why does safe driving demand your undivided attention every second behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Reading changing traffic and steering, braking, and scanning smoothly takes nonstop coordination between brain and hands.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: How does the guide define a driving distraction, and which three groups are endangered by it?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Anything hurting safe car control endangers not just you, but also your passengers and nearby bystanders.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: Beyond phones and texting, what everyday cabin habits appear on the Missouri guide's distraction list?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Eating, grooming, passenger chatter, audio dials, paper maps, video, web browsing, and GPS entry all steal focus.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.question_text: Does the Missouri driver guide count ordinary conversation with passengers as a driving distraction?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.teaching_text: Even friendly conversation inside the car sits right beside eating, grooming, and reading on the distraction list.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: Which three faculties does texting pull off driving simultaneously, making it the deadliest distraction?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: Combining visual, manual, and cognitive distraction all at once leaves your car rolling blind down the lane.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: Which drivers are barred under Missouri law from reading, writing, or sending electronic text messages while driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Missouri's electronic messaging ban covers every driver behind the wheel, not just teen or commercial operators.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.question_text: Which three living companions inside your vehicle can easily turn into dangerous distractions?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.teaching_text: Unsettled kids, rowdy friends, and unrestrained animals pull your eyes into the backseat when traffic slows suddenly.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.question_text: What should you do when children in the car need your attention during a drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.teaching_text: Reaching into the backseat while rolling drifts your car across center lines or into stopped traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.question_text: What lesson does the guide say to teach young children about your role behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.teaching_text: Kids behave calmer when taught early that steering safely is an important job needing full concentration.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.question_text: Where do arguments and upsetting conversations belong instead of inside a moving car?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.teaching_text: Anger and emotional stress narrow tunnel vision and spike aggressive pedal inputs when you should be scanning.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.question_text: In what three ways can a car packed with friends pull a driver's focus off the road?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.teaching_text: Rowdy cabin energy, battling over playlists, or roughhousing steals attention right before missed stops or curves.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.question_text: How does the Missouri driver guide view letting a pet roam loose inside a moving vehicle?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.teaching_text: A startled dog or cat can leap under brake pedals or block your view mid-turn.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.question_text: Which three restraints keep a pet safe in a moving car, and where must a pet never sit?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.teaching_text: A pet on your lap blocks steering and airbag deployment, whereas a kennel, carrier, or harness protects everyone.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.question_text: Which dashboard or connected-screen tasks can trigger a crash or near-crash?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.teaching_text: Typing addresses, hunting stations, tweaking climate knobs, or checking web and email pulls eyes off traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.question_text: What core warning sits behind the guide's heading that turning dials can turn your head?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.teaching_text: Looking down for two seconds to adjust a knob at highway speed covers half a football field blind.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.question_text: Which four cabin adjustments should you lock in before shifting out of park?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.teaching_text: Dialing in your seat, mirrors, temperature, and audio while parked keeps both hands free once moving.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.question_text: When should you check email, voicemail, and similar digital messages around a trip?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.teaching_text: Handling inbox and voicemail checks strictly before departure or after parking eliminates mid-trip phone temptation.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.question_text: What automatic phone feature helps stop callers and texters from expecting an answer while you drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.teaching_text: Letting your phone automatically reply that you are driving removes social pressure to glance at notifications.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.question_text: What two safe options do you have if radio, climate, or navigation needs adjusting mid-trip?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.teaching_text: Delegate knob or map changes to your front-seat rider, or handle them during a planned stop.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.question_text: Which six outside-the-window sights become dangerous distractions when drivers stare at them?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.teaching_text: Rubbernecking at wrecks, police stops, scenery, billboards, house numbers, or road crews rear-ends braking cars ahead.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.question_text: What mindset should replace studying passing roadside scenery when you are behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.teaching_text: Save sightseeing for passengers or scenic pullouts so your eyes stay locked on traffic flow.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.question_text: Which vehicle classes and which roadways are covered by Missouri's electronic communication device law?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.teaching_text: Missouri's handheld statute covers everyday car drivers and commercial truckers alike across roadways and properties open for public driving.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.question_text: Under what vehicle condition do the prohibited uses in Missouri's electronic device law apply?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.teaching_text: Notice that exact statutory trigger because the listed handheld and video prohibitions apply whenever wheels are rolling.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.question_text: While your vehicle is moving, may you hold a cellphone in your hand or prop it with your shoulder?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.teaching_text: Pinning a phone against your ear with a shoulder or resting it on your knee violates the law.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.question_text: Which four manual text-message actions are illegal while your vehicle is moving?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.teaching_text: Even glancing down to read an incoming text by hand while rolling counts as an illegal use.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.question_text: What video-creation, streaming, or calling activities are barred while your vehicle is in motion?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.teaching_text: Filming reels, livestreaming, posting clips, or joining video calls while rolling is strictly illegal.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.question_text: May a driver watch a movie or video clip while the vehicle is moving?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.teaching_text: Streaming shows or clips on a mounted phone or dash screen steals visual tracking from live lanes.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.question_text: How must voice calls be started, answered, or ended to stay legal while driving in Missouri?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.teaching_text: Hands-free calling stays legal when voice commands or a single tap or swipe starts and ends calls.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.question_text: Through which three audio setups may a Missouri driver talk hands-free on a voice call?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.teaching_text: Routing calls through cabin Bluetooth, a built-in speaker, or earbuds and headsets keeps both hands on the wheel.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.question_text: What feature lets Missouri drivers legally send and receive text-based messages while driving?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.teaching_text: Letting voice-to-text read and dictate messages keeps your thumbs off the glass and eyes up.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.question_text: Which map, route, and listening functions remain legal on your phone under Missouri's device law?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.teaching_text: Following GPS turn maps and streaming playlists, radio broadcasts, or podcasts stays legal when set up hands-free.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: If your phone sits in a dash mount untouched, how does the law treat a voice call versus a video call?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Mounting your phone never legalizes FaceTime or video chats; video calls stay banned whenever the car moves.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: Contrast the single legal way and the banned way to handle text messages in a moving car?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Spoken dictation passes the law whereas typing or reading texts by hand breaks it.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.question_text: What condition must a rideshare driver meet to use a device for relaying company network trip info?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.teaching_text: Rideshare drivers accepting dispatches must keep their phone secured in a vehicle mount rather than handheld.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.question_text: How did Missouri device-law enforcement shift across the January first, twenty twenty-five milestone?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.teaching_text: Missouri's grace period ended at the start of twenty twenty-five, replacing warnings-only with citable infractions.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.question_text: Since January first, twenty twenty-five, how can officers cite a violation of Missouri's electronic device law?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.teaching_text: Don't expect a free warning anymore because officers can write infractions for moving handheld violations.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.question_text: What licensing penalty can hit commercial drivers under the device law, and what broader penalties can apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.teaching_text: Beyond infraction fines and potential criminal charges in severe crashes, CDL holders risk commercial disqualification.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.question_text: For which specific group of drivers does the guide name disqualification as a device-law consequence?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.teaching_text: Commercial operators are held to strict federal-aligned standards where handheld phone violations can disqualify CDL privileges.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: What five pieces of roadway guidance do painted lines and pavement symbols give drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Reading road paint early keeps you from missing turn pockets, drifting into splits, or rolling onto pedestrian paths.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: How does a dashed pavement stripe differ from a solid stripe when you want to overtake?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Solid stripes mark spots with tight sightlines or conflict zones where pulling out invites a collision.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Mixing up yellow and white stripes on a dark ramp can send your car straight against oncoming headlights.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: What does seeing yellow versus white paint immediately to your left reveal, and what marks the right road edge?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Glancing at the stripe beside your driver door confirms instantly whether you are on a two-way or one-way road.
sec08-card-sec08-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Left yellow oncoming; right edge white

visual_sync.text_span: Left yellow oncoming; right edge white

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What markings run down the middle of an undivided four-lane road, and may you cross them to overtake?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: With two lanes already heading your way, crossing center double yellows puts you into fast oncoming lanes needlessly.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: How is a two-lane no-passing zone striped, where does it appear, and when must your pass finish?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Hills and curves hide oncoming bumpers, so still being left of center when solid paint starts risks a head-on hit.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: When does a center solid yellow stripe bar you from passing, and what rule governs unmarked two-lane roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Unpainted country blacktop still hides dips and curves, so never pull out unless open road stretches clearly ahead.
sec08-card-sec08-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Your solid blocks; need clear view

visual_sync.text_span: Your solid blocks; need clear view

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Why must you never swing onto the road shoulder to get around another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Motorists pulling off for mail, turns, or breakdowns rarely expect a fast car barreling down the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Where on the pavement must your front bumper stop when halted by a sign or red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Rolling across painted bars forces pedestrians out into live cross traffic just to walk around your hood.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: What roadway purpose do marked crosswalk stripes serve?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Channeling foot traffic into predictable lanes lets approaching drivers scan corners before starting turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: To which walkers must you yield at crosswalks, and why watch closely at intersections without white stripes?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Every street corner forms a legal crossing zone whether crews painted white bars across the asphalt or not.
sec08-card-sec08-F08.must_match_memory_hook: In or stepping in; unpainted counts

visual_sync.text_span: In or stepping in; unpainted counts

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: In a lane marked for both straight and turning movement, when may you turn versus when must you hold?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Turning while only the straight green arrow shines cuts directly across protected cross traffic or walkers.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How is a two-way shared left-turn lane striped, what moves belong in it, and when should you exit it?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Cruising down a shared middle lane uses it like a passing strip where opposing left-turners enter head-on.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: What yellow pavement markings identify a dedicated left-turn lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Spotting heavy diagonal yellow bars keeps you from mistaking a turn-only pocket or median gore for a through lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What is the rule on reversing inside a travel lane when you overshoot an exit or corner?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Drivers approaching at full speed never expect reverse lights coming toward them in an active lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Are you ever allowed to halt inside a travel lane because you are lost, stalling, or dropping off a rider?
