sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Even a ten-second curb drop-off or map check inside moving traffic invites a high-speed rear-end crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Where three or more lanes run your direction, which lane is your home lane and when should you move middle?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Shifting into the center lane through busy ramp zones lets merging cars enter smoothly without brake-checking.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Which lane is built for overtaking on multi-lane roads, and what makes right-side passing hazardous?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Right-side passenger blind spots are wider, and slower motorists routinely drift right expecting an open lane.
sec08-card-sec08-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Pass far left; right hides cars

visual_sync.text_span: Pass far left; right hides cars

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Alongside signs, lights, and paint, which three groups of people have legal authority to direct traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Ignoring a crossing guard's paddle or a work flagger carries the same danger and legal trouble as running a red light.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What must you do when a uniformed officer waves you to stop even though the overhead light is green?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Officers at crash scenes, parades, or broken signals see cross hazards automated timers know nothing about.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: How do you respond to a flashing red signal compared with a flashing yellow signal?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Rolling through flashing red like flashing yellow treats a stop-controlled crossroad as an open green.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Where do you halt for a steady red traffic light, and what is the lone exception to waiting for green?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Stopping crisp behind the line or walk keeps cross lanes open while you scan for a legal right turn.
sec08-card-sec08-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Halt before line; right turn exception

visual_sync.text_span: Halt before line; right turn exception

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What three conditions must all be met before turning right at a steady red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Rolling a red right turn without halting first misses walkers stepping off the curb right beside your fender.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What does a solid yellow traffic light warn, and when is driving through it justified?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Flooring the gas to beat yellow risks meeting cross-street starters, while panic-locking inside the box invites rear-ends.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Before accelerating on a circular green light, whom must you still allow to clear?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: A green bulb grants permission, never armor against late left-turners or slower walkers finishing their crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: After coming to a full stop, how does your next step differ at a flashing red signal versus a steady red?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Waiting endlessly for green under a midnight flashing red backs up traffic, while leaving a steady red straight runs it.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: What separates your required action at a flashing yellow light from a steady yellow light?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Confusing a steady yellow cycle change with a continuous caution beacon sends you into the box right on red.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: During which four situations might intersection lights switch to flashing mode in every direction?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Knowing signals switch intentionally off-peak keeps you alert to whether your side flashes yellow or red.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: How must every approaching driver treat an intersection whose traffic lights are completely dark or broken?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Blowing through an unlit arterial intersection during a storm blackout causes devastating T-bone crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Which two signal displays appear during a permissive left-turn phase, and what must you wait for?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Oncoming traffic also holds green during a permissive phase, so turning without a wide gap causes head-on wrecks.
sec08-card-sec08-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Green ball or flashing arrow yields

visual_sync.text_span: Green ball or flashing arrow yields

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Which signal lets you turn in a protected left-turn phase, and what signal holds opposing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Holding opposing straight lanes on red clears cross conflicts, though stray red-runners still warrant a glance.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: How does a combined protected-permissive left-turn signal cycle work?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Once the green arrow drops to a green ball or flashing yellow arrow, oncoming cars start moving straight at you.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What must you do at a steady red arrow, and whom might you still owe right-of-way when it changes?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Turning across a steady red arrow violates dedicated signal timing and cuts into active crosswalk phases.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: Which signal precedes a steady yellow arrow, what three displays can follow it, and how do you react?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Assuming red always comes next misses transitions into flashing yellow or circular green where oncoming traffic launches.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Under what two conditions does a flashing yellow arrow permit you to complete your turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Drivers fixated on gaps in oncoming cars often forget crosswalk walkers have a walk signal parallel to them.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Even with a steady green arrow pointing your way, what two things must be true before you go?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Turning from an adjacent straight lane or crowding stragglers still clearing the box causes avoidable fender-benders.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: What is the key right-of-way difference between a steady green arrow and a flashing yellow arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Misreading a flashing yellow arrow as protected right-of-way turns you straight across fast oncoming cars.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How does your response to a steady red arrow differ from a steady yellow arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Red locks the turn lane completely while yellow warns your protected window is closing right now.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Match five classic road sign shapes to their meanings: octagon, triangle, pentagon, pennant, and diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Recognizing silhouettes through snow, mud, or darkness tells you the rule before you can read a single letter.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What categories belong to vertical rectangles, horizontal rectangles, and round or crossbuck shapes?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Tall white boards state enforceable laws, wide boards point out exits, and circles warn of tracks ahead.
sec08-card-sec08-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Vertical rules, horizontal guides, round rail

visual_sync.text_span: Vertical rules, horizontal guides, round rail

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What messages are carried by red, black-and-white, yellow, and fluorescent yellow-green road signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Spotting bright yellow-green a block away flags school and pedestrian crossings earlier than standard yellow.
sec08-card-sec08-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Red stops, white rules, yellow-green school

visual_sync.text_span: Red stops, white rules, yellow-green school

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: What four kinds of information do orange, green, blue, and brown highway signs provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Color coding lets highway drivers filter urgent work-zone warnings from rest areas, exits, and state parks instantly.
sec08-card-sec08-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Orange work, green guide, blue, brown

visual_sync.text_span: Orange work, green guide, blue, brown

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Which two colors mark regulatory signs, and how does yellow-green differ from standard yellow?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Test distractors swap general yellow hazard warnings with the yellow-green shade reserved for school zones.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How do you keep the pennant sign shape and the five-sided pentagon sign shape straight?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Both start with the letter P, making pennant versus pentagon a classic Missouri written-test swap.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: How are typical regulatory signs colored and shaped, and which five driving rules do they govern?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Unlike yellow advisory warnings, white rectangular signs state legal commands that bring tickets when ignored.
sec08-card-sec08-F42.must_match_memory_hook: White boards govern lanes, turns, speed

visual_sync.text_span: White boards govern lanes, turns, speed

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal red slash over a black symbol send?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: Instant symbol recognition stops illegal left turns or U-turns before you commit your front wheels.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.question_text: Beyond turn prohibitions, which two vehicle-type bans commonly use the red-slash prohibition design?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.teaching_text: Low bridges, narrow parkways, and high-speed expressways restrict heavy rigs or pedal bikes for everyone's safety.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: What shape and colors identify standard warning signs, and what driver response do they call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Diamonds give advance notice of hidden curves, crossings, or merges so you adjust speed before reaching trouble.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What upcoming traffic controls do Stop Ahead and Signal Ahead signs announce, and how should you react?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Curves, hills, and summer foliage often hide red lights or stop signs until braking distance gets tight.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: How should you adjust your driving at a School Crossing sign and at a Pedestrian Crossing sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Children dart unpredictably between parked cars, and crosswalk pedestrians hold legal priority once crossing.
sec08-card-sec08-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down; watch kids, yield walkers

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down; watch kids, yield walkers

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: What color transition does the Missouri guide note for School Crossing signs, and over what timeframe?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: During multi-year sign replacements you will meet both older yellow and newer fluorescent yellow-green school panels.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: How does an Added Lane warning sign differ from a Merge warning sign for incoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Braking or swerving needlessly at an Added Lane ramp disrupts highway flow when newcomers already have fresh pavement.
sec08-card-sec08-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Added gets own lane; Merge shares

visual_sync.text_span: Added gets own lane; Merge shares

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: When you pass a Lane Ends Merge Left sign while driving in the right lane, what is your duty?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Drivers in the ending lane never hold priority over cars already established in the continuous through lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: What common situation do Added Lane and Merge signs both warn about, and what single detail separates them?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Checking whether the arrow joins your stem or runs parallel tells you instantly if cars will cross into your path.
sec08-card-sec08-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Both warn entry; lane count differs

visual_sync.text_span: Both warn entry; lane count differs

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: What does a T Intersection Ahead warning sign tell you about the road you are traveling on?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Missing a T-junction warning at night or in fog risks running straight off the far side of the crossroad.
sec08-card-sec08-F44.must_match_memory_hook: Your road ends; turn either way

visual_sync.text_span: Your road ends; turn either way

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: How does an Intersection warning sign differ from a Side Road Ahead warning sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Knowing whether cross traffic can emerge from both sides or one hidden driveway sharpens your intersection scan.
sec08-card-sec08-R22.must_match_memory_hook: Crossroad cuts across; side joins one

visual_sync.text_span: Crossroad cuts across; side joins one

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: What two actions does a Roundabout Ahead warning sign prompt before you reach the island?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Entering a tight splitter island at open-road speed leaves no time to yield to circulating cars.
sec08-card-sec08-R23.must_match_memory_hook: Drop to posted speed, obey circle

visual_sync.text_span: Drop to posted speed, obey circle

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: What hazard does a Side Road Railroad Crossing sign alert turning motorists to watch for?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Turning onto a side street pushes your hood onto rails almost immediately before you straighten the wheel.
sec08-card-sec08-R24.must_match_memory_hook: Rail tracks sit right past turn

visual_sync.text_span: Rail tracks sit right past turn

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: What road geometry and recommended top speed go with a Reverse Turn warning sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: The second bend can snap back tighter than the first, catching fast drivers off balance mid-transfer.
sec08-card-sec08-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Two opposite turns, thirty or under

visual_sync.text_span: Two opposite turns, thirty or under

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: How does the recommended speed on a sharp Turn sign differ from the speed meaning of a Curve sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Right-angle turn arrows demand thirty or slower, whereas sweeping curve arrows call for easing below highway pace.
sec08-card-sec08-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Turn thirty max; curve below limit

visual_sync.text_span: Turn thirty max; curve below limit

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Which two bend signs share the thirty-mile-per-hour-or-less speed threshold, unlike a standard Curve sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Grouping sharp single turns and S-shaped reverse turns under thirty locks in Missouri's favorite sign-speed distinction.
sec08-card-sec08-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Turn and Reverse Turn cap thirty

visual_sync.text_span: Turn and Reverse Turn cap thirty

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: What does an advisory speed plate beneath a bend sign tell you, especially when rain, snow, or ice hits?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Advisory plaques are calibrated for dry tires, so exceeding them on wet or icy asphalt breaks traction fast.
sec08-card-sec08-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Advised dry speed; slower when slick

visual_sync.text_span: Advised dry speed; slower when slick

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: What specific speed guidance does an Exit Speed Advisory sign give freeway drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Tightly banked cloverleaf ramps can roll top-heavy cars if you carry seventy-mile freeway momentum onto the curve.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: What message do large single turn arrows and sequential curve chevrons emphasize along a bend?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Rows of yellow chevrons outline the outside edge of tightening curves where night drivers otherwise overdrive sightlines.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: What top speed does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of farm or work gear indicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Closing on a tractor at sixty feels like approaching a parked wall, so ease off the gas immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: What hazards do a Slippery When Wet sign and a Soft Shoulder sign warn against?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: Polished pavement loses grip in light rain, while muddy shoulders yank right-side tires toward the ditch.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: What road layout changes do Begin Divided Roadway and End Divided Roadway signs announce?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Missing an End Divided sign leaves drivers forgetting oncoming cars now sit right across a painted line.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: Where are roadside object markers placed, and what driving habit do they reinforce?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Bridge abutments, culverts, and narrow underpass piers sit inches off the fog line waiting for drifting tires.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: What does a yellow Bicycle Share the Road warning sign tell motorists to expect?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Narrow shoulders or bridges leave riders no side space, requiring patience until a safe passing gap opens.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which two visibility limits make night driving harder than driving in daylight?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Headlight beams light far less forward and roadside space than sun does while opposing headlights dazzle your eyes.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: During which daily evening-to-morning window must your headlights stay on in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Twilight hides dark-colored cars well before full night arrives, locking in thirty-minute buffers after sunset and before dawn.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: Outside nighttime hours, what everyday weather trigger legally requires turning on your headlights in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Daytime rain, sleet, or snow spray grays out unpainted cars in mirrors unless full headlights and taillights glow.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: What are the two independent rules—one by time and one by weather—that mandate headlights in Missouri?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Remember both halves together so bright rainy afternoons never trick you into driving dark on automatic light sensors.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Which three upkeep steps keep your windows and headlights ready for safe night driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Road film cuts headlight output dramatically, burned bulbs hide half your car, and crooked aim blinds oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: On open dark roads, when should you switch up to your high-beam headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: High beams stretch your forward reaction window whenever empty oncoming lanes let you use them without blinding others.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: About how far ahead do headlights let you see, and how must that cap your nighttime speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Cruising so fast that stopping eats more than three hundred fifty feet means any dark obstacle ahead gets hit.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle versus a vehicle you are following must you switch to low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Missouri splits its dimming rule—drop brights a block out at five hundred oncoming and three hundred trailing.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How do Missouri's three easy-to-confuse nighttime distances—beam reach, oncoming dim, and following dim—line up?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Keep those three numbers untangled on exam day—beams show three-fifty, oncoming dims at five-hundred, trailing dims at three-hundred.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Which painted stripe should guide your eyes at night, and what roadside hazards require extra scanning?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Looking toward the right edgeline—or center stripe if unmarked—shields your eyes from glare while spotting signs and walkers.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: What speed adjustment should you make before entering curves at night if you are cruising at the posted limit?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Headlights point straight off the outside shoulder as a bend starts, hiding hazards around the curve until late.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: What rule does the Missouri Driver Guide give if you feel drowsy before or during a night drive?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Fighting heavy eyelids in the dark slows reactions just like impairment and risks nodding off at highway speed.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Which two visibility systems should you verify work properly before winter weather arrives?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Streaking blades or a dead defroster leaves your windshield iced over from outside slush and inside breath fog.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Which surfaces must you clear of snow and ice before driving, even if you are only going a few blocks?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Peering through a tiny scraped hole hides cross-traffic and pedestrians, and snow-packed lamps hide your brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Even with snow-rated tires or chains installed, what two winter speed rules still apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Extra tread or chains help you move, never making normal dry-road speeds or cruise control safe on ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What should you carry ready in your vehicle if it does not run snow-rated tires?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Stashing fitting chains in the trunk keeps a sudden Missouri ice or snow squall from stranding all-season tires.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: How should you press the gas pedal when starting from a stop on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Stomping the throttle breaks fragile winter grip immediately and polishes snow under your tires into slick glare ice.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: If your drive wheels spin when trying to pull out on snow, what two-step method frees the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Gentle forward-and-reverse rocking packs a short runway, and salt, sand, or cat litter gives spinning rubber bite.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Why must bystanders stay out of line with spinning tires while freeing a stuck vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: A fast-spinning tread acts like a slingshot, firing chunks of ice or stones straight backward or forward.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Once rolling on a snowy or icy street, how can you check safely how slick the surface actually is?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Feeling how early tires slip under a light test touch lets you dial speed down before real intersections.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: About how many seconds of following distance should you leave behind the vehicle ahead on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Packed snow and glare ice multiply stopping feet dramatically, stretching safe spacing all the way to eight-to-ten seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Why does Missouri jump the winter following cushion up to eight to ten seconds on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: When tire friction drops near zero, only an eight-to-ten-second time buffer gives room to slow without rear-ending.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: How should you brake on slippery winter roads, and when does pumping versus checking your ABS manual apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Hard stabs trigger instant skids—squeeze gently, pumping on ultra-slick ice only when your vehicle lacks anti-lock instructions.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Which roadway structures ice over before regular pavement, and can plowed streets still hide ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from both top and bottom while shady spots hold ice patches on cleared roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Why does the Missouri guide warn against using four-wheel drive on ice, and what should you do if caught?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Four-wheel drive adds zero ice braking grip and risks rollovers—ease smoothly off the accelerator if you hit glare ice.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Why are roads extra greasy right as rain begins or under wet leaves, and how should you adjust?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Fresh raindrops float dripped motor oil and dust into a slick glaze—and wet leaves act just like ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: How does wet pavement affect cornering through highway curves?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Tires fighting side-force around a bend break loose far earlier on wet asphalt unless you trim speed beforehand.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why is using cruise control dangerous on wet pavement?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: If tires lose bite on a puddle, cruise control keeps feeding throttle right when lifting off is vital.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What happens during hydroplaning, above what speed can it start, and when can contact vanish completely?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Tires wedge up onto standing water past thirty-five miles per hour and can surf completely clear of asphalt at fifty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How do Missouri's two hydroplaning speed benchmarks—thirty-five and fifty-five miles per hour—differ?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Exam questions love testing partial water lift starting past thirty-five against total zero-contact surfing in downpours at fifty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What should you do—and avoid doing—the instant you feel your tires start to hydroplane?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Lifting smoothly off the throttle lets speed drop until tread sinks back onto asphalt, whereas touching brakes triggers a spin.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Which three tire and driving habits keep your car from hydroplaning in rainy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Healthy tread grooves and right psi channel water aside while slower manual throttle—never cruise—keeps rubber planted.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: What is the job of four-wheel anti-lock brakes during a panic stop, and how does the pedal feel?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Keeping tires rolling instead of skidding preserves steering control while rapid valve action pulses noticeably beneath your shoe.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: What pedal technique should you use with anti-lock brakes in an emergency, and how should you treat noise?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Pumping defeats ABS computers—press hard and steady right through normal buzzing or pulsing while steering clear.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How does the winter-driving section reconcile brake-pumping advice on glare ice with ABS-equipped cars?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Old-school pumping applies to standard brakes on slick ice, whereas ABS drivers follow their vehicle owner's manual.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: Do front-wheel-drive and rear-wheel-drive cars start skid recovery differently, and what are the first two pedal moves?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Regardless of which axle powers the car, step one is always lifting off the gas without touching the brake.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: Which direction do you steer during a skid, and what wheel or brake mistakes make the spin worse?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: If your tail slides right, smoothly steer right—slamming brakes or yanking the wheel whips the car around.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: What four sequential stages are shown in the Missouri guide's right-sliding skid recovery sequence?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Seeing the tail slide right cues turning the front tires right until the chassis tracks straight ahead again.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: How should you adjust speed and headlight beams in fog, and why avoid brights?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off suspended water droplets back into your eyes like a glowing white wall.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: What must you do when fog thickens so badly that you can no longer see the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Get completely off the travel lane, stop, and leave lights plus emergency flashers running so nobody rear-ends you.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: What is rule number one in any driving emergency, and why keep the ignition key on while rolling?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Turning the key off before stopping kills power-steering assist and can click the steering column lock shut mid-lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What practical mental advantage does staying calm give you during a sudden roadside crisis?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Panic freezes muscle memory, whereas a steady breath lets your brain retrieve the right steering or braking fix.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: Which three mechanical actions help slow your car if the brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Rapid hard pumping may build leftover line pressure while gradual parking-brake tension and downshifting scrub speed toward a safe pull-off.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: How does your foot action during total brake failure contrast with an emergency stop using working ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Dead sinking pedals need fast hard pumps to rebuild pressure, whereas healthy ABS needs one continuous firm press.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Once you get a car with failed brakes stopped safely off the road, may you limp it slowly to a repair shop?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Never gamble on crippled brakes for 'just one more mile'—leave it parked safely and summon a tow.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: Which three sound and steering clues tell you a tire just blew out?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: A sharp pop followed by rhythmic flopping rubber and a sudden tug on the steering wheel signals a blowout.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: How do you control a tire blowout, and when is it finally safe to touch the brake pedal?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Slamming brakes on a shredded tire flips or spins the car—hold straight and coast almost to a crawl off-road first.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: After coasting off-road from a blowout, what lights come on and when should you change the tire yourself?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Hit hazard flashers right away, and never crouch beside fast highway traffic if changing the wheel puts you in danger.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: How do you recover safely if your right tires drop off the edge of the paved road?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Yanking back onto high asphalt at speed slingshots you across oncoming lanes—slow down under control before steering back.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: Which way can soft shoulder gravel tug your wheels after dropping off pavement, and how should you brake?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Loose dirt drags the right tires outward, so brace the wheel firmly and touch brakes lightly if needed.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: What should you do if your steering suddenly stops responding?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Hard braking with disconnected steering can pitch the car sideways—coast down with hazard flashers unless impact looms.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What braking rule do tire blowouts and steering failures have in common?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: In both emergencies, early hard braking destabilizes the vehicle—let momentum bleed off before touching the brake.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, which switches and backup lamps help you pull off?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Click the dimmer or main switch first, then light up parking lamps, blinkers, or four-ways to guide off-road.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: How can you see well enough to pull off safely if your hood flies up or wipers quit in heavy rain?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Looking out the open driver window—or peeking under the raised hood gap—gives enough sightline to reach the shoulder with flashers.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: What sequence stops your vehicle safely if the accelerator pedal sticks down?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Popping the shifter into Neutral cuts engine drive to the wheels instantly so your brakes can haul you onto the shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: During a stuck-accelerator emergency, when is it finally safe to shut off the ignition?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Shutting the engine off while rolling locks the steering wheel on many models right when you need to aim off-road.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: Where must your eyes stay focused while slowing down a car with a stuck accelerator?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Never stare down at the floor mat or shifter—keep eyes up hunting a clean gap out of traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: How does braking timing for a stuck accelerator contrast with a tire blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Once in Neutral, a stuck-pedal car has four healthy tires ready for immediate braking—unlike a blowout coasting down.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: What three moves should you make—and what swerve must you avoid—when a car comes straight at you in your lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Brake hard, blast your horn, and bail right toward the shoulder or ditch—never swerving into the oncoming lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Why is dodging into the left lane so deadly when an oncoming car drifts into yours?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: The instant a distracted or drowsy wrong-way driver looks up, their natural reflex yanks them right back into that lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with a train approaching, which direction do you run after getting out?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Running away from the tracks angled toward the oncoming locomotive keeps you clear of wreckage blasted down-track on impact.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: What happens if you run away in the same direction an approaching train is traveling when it hits your stalled car?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Momentum hurls shattered car parts forward and outward ahead of the locomotive—right through anyone running down-track.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: What sequence should you try if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks with no train visible?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Drop windows first so you can hear distant horns, try restarting once, or shift to Neutral and push clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.question_text: What instability warning and driver recommendation did the NTSB issue for twelve- and fifteen-passenger vans?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.teaching_text: Packing more than ten riders shifts center-of-gravity high and rearward, raising rollover danger unless drivers get special training.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: Where does the Missouri guide direct drivers of twelve- and fifteen-passenger vans for deeper safety guidance?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: The National Transportation Safety Board publishes tire-pressure, loading, and rollover-prevention guides specifically for large van operators.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Before shifting out of park, whose seat belts and child restraints must you verify, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Unbelted riders become human projectiles in a collision, multiplying injury and fatality odds across the cabin.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How must the lap strap and shoulder strap sit on your body, and what positions are unsafe?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Tucking a shoulder strap under your arm or behind your back lets crash force crush ribs and internal organs.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What three crash types or control needs explain why air bags never replace wearing a seat belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Front air bags only cushion head-on hits and cannot hold you in the driver's seat during swerves or flips.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How can an inflating air bag harm an unbelted rider, and how much chest-to-wheel space does NHTSA advise?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Bags punch outward fast enough to seriously injure or kill anyone slumped against the steering wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Up through what age should children ride in back, and where must a rear-facing infant seat never sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: An active passenger air bag slams directly into the back of a rear-facing infant shell with lethal force.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Under Missouri's general adult seat belt law, which occupants of a passenger vehicle must buckle up?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Front-row occupants face the windshield and dash directly, making fastened belts mandatory across Missouri.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: When a graduated intermediate license holder is driving, who inside the vehicle must be restrained?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Teen intermediate drivers carry stricter responsibility requiring every back-seat friend to click in before rolling.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does Missouri's mandatory belt coverage expand when an intermediate license holder takes the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Written exams love contrasting adult front-seat coverage against the all-passenger rule placed on intermediate drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Under Missouri law, does high body weight ever excuse a child younger than four from a child restraint?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Toddlers under four have developing neck bones that need full harness support regardless of scale weight.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What restraint rule applies to any child weighing less than forty pounds, regardless of birthday?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Lightweight older kids can slip out of boosters or lap belts unless a proper harness secures them.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How do the under-four-years rule and the under-forty-pounds rule interact for young Missouri riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Meeting just one threshold locks in a child restraint, whether a heavy three-year-old or petite five-year-old.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Which exact age, weight, and height ranges place a Missouri child into the mandatory booster-seat tier?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Until kids outgrow one of those three measurements, adult lap-shoulder belts cut across soft belly and neck tissue.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Reaching which age, weight, or height threshold lets a child graduate to a vehicle safety belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Hitting eight years, eighty pounds, or over fifty-seven inches positions the vehicle belt safely over hips and collarbone.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How does the logic of Missouri's booster tier differ from graduating into the vehicle safety-belt tier?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Crossing even one milestone among age eight, eighty pounds, or four-foot-nine moves a child into the belt tier.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Which two types of passenger transport are excluded from Missouri's child-restraint statute?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Every private car, pickup, van, and SUV must follow the child-seat tiers, leaving out only buses and public carriers.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: How should a defensive driver keep their eyes moving, and why monitor oncoming two-lane traffic closely?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Distracted oncoming drivers wandering across the center stripe trigger sudden head-on collisions unless spotted early.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How should you prepare for other motorists' mistakes, and what is your duty even when someone steals right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Having right-of-way on paper never justifies colliding when easing off the gas avoids a wreck.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Why must you scan left and right entering an intersection even when cross streets face red lights or stop signs?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Distracted or speeding cross-street drivers blow red lights daily, so a quick left-right check saves your side doors.
sec10-card-sec10-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Paint and bulbs cannot stop steel

visual_sync.text_span: Paint and bulbs cannot stop steel

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Why should you aim your gaze well down the roadway instead of staring right past your hood?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Looking twelve to fifteen seconds downrange reveals brake lights and lane drops while braking can stay gentle.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: What body, arm, foot, and hand positions make up proper Missouri driving posture?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Sitting upright with bent elbows gives full steering leverage without locking your arms or straining toward pedals.
sec10-card-sec10-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Upright back, bent elbows, both hands

visual_sync.text_span: Upright back, bent elbows, both hands

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Where on the steering wheel clock face does the Missouri guide tell you to place your left and right hands?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Lower hand placement keeps forearms clear of the air bag cover while maximizing smooth steering control.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: What practical steering benefit comes from holding the lower left and right clock zones on the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Keeping both hands anchored through gentle bends prevents fumbled grips if a tire hits a pothole.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which steering method should you use around corners, what habit is banned, and how do you straighten out?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: One-hand palming or letting the wheel spin loose through your fingers risks losing grip mid-corner.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your car is rolling?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Engaging the column lock while rolling pins the front tires at one angle and strips away steering.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What single following mistake causes the frequent rear-end collisions seen on everyday roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: When the lead driver slams brakes for debris or traffic, tailgaters run out of asphalt before reacting.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: How do you apply Missouri's three-second rule to check whether you are following too closely?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Reaching the signpost or shadow before finishing three seconds proves your gap is too tight for sudden stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What two smooth habits help the driver behind you maintain a safe following cushion?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Predictable speed and early blinkers give trailing motorists extra seconds to ease off before you brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: How should you respond to a tailgater on a multi-lane road versus on a single-lane stretch?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Brake-checking an impatient bumper rider guarantees a rear-end hit, whereas easing speed encourages an easy pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: When your slower pace stacks cars behind you on a two-lane road, how should you clear the queue?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Pulling safely aside lets faster drivers pass calmly instead of attempting risky blind overtakes.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: What should you do before backing into a parallel parking space when cars are following right behind you?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Throwing the car into reverse with a bumper glued behind yours invites an awkward street-side crunch.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Where should you pull your car whenever picking up or dropping off riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live lane opens passenger doors straight toward moving mirrors and blocks sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: How should you position your vehicle relative to side-by-side cars, the center line, and your own lane stripes?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Cruising centered and staggered out of adjacent blind spots preserves an open swerve path on at least one side.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: What two sudden hazards explain keeping extra side clearance beside a line of parked cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Doors swing wide, kids dart between bumpers, and parked drivers nose out with blocked mirror views.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: When oncoming ramp traffic is merging onto your multi-lane highway and the next lane left is open, what helps?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Sliding left early hands entering cars an empty right lane and eliminates merge friction.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: How do you separate two simultaneous hazards like an oncoming car and a bicyclist ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Slowing to let the oncoming car pass first prevents squeezing between metal on your left and a cyclist right.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which two distances add together into total stopping distance, and what three factors stretch it out?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Tired eyes delay your foot while high speed or worn pads lengthen the skid after you press.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What happens during reaction distance, and how many seconds of reaction time does Missouri's chart assume?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: In one and a half seconds at highway speed, your car rolls over a hundred feet before brakes even touch.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What does braking distance measure, and what four ideal conditions does the handbook chart assume?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Wet asphalt, bald tread, or faded brakes push real-world stops well past the chart's sunny-day numbers.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Which piece of stopping distance happens before your foot hits the brake versus after?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Keeping those two halves distinct prevents mixing up human perception travel with mechanical tire friction.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: What default assumption do nearby drivers make about your car, and why signal before slowing or turning?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Everyone around you plans around your current line and speed until blinkers or brake taps announce a change.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Before which four maneuvers should you signal, even when the street looks completely empty?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Signaling every lane shift, turn, merge, or park warns the hidden cyclist or car you failed to see.
sec10-card-sec10-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Signal every move, empty streets too

visual_sync.text_span: Signal every move, empty streets too

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: At least how far ahead should you signal a turn, and when should you delay flipping the blinker on?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Signaling before an earlier driveway tricks waiting cross-drivers into pulling out right across your bow.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What intermediate features or waiting vehicles create an exception to Missouri's hundred-foot turn-signal rule?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: A car poised to exit an alley between you and your corner will read an early blinker as turning in.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: Why must you verify your turn signal has turned off after finishing a lane change or turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: A forgotten flashing blinker invites side-street drivers to pull straight out expecting you to turn.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: When does a car's turn signal stalk often fail to click off automatically, and how do you fix it?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Gentle lane shifts and slight Y-turns rarely rotate the steering column far enough to trip the cancel cam.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What is the sole legitimate reason to tap your horn, and why skip needless honking?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Startling nearby drivers or cyclists when no collision threat exists can trigger a panic swerve.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: May you ever use your vehicle's horn to vent anger or frustration at slow traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Laying on the horn in frustration escalates road rage without solving a single traffic delay.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: When is driving slower than a posted minimum speed illegal, and which three conditions excuse it?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Clear dry freeways require keeping pace with the minimum, while storms, jams, or rough pavement demand slowing.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: Even where no minimum speed sign exists, what makes driving too slowly illegal, and how do you clear queues?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Crawling far under normal pace stacks impatient cars bumper-to-bumper until you pull aside to let them pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Compare what justifies dropping below a posted minimum with what makes slow driving illegal on unposted roads?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Weather, traffic, or bad pavement excuse slow highway travel, yet obstructing clear roads breaks Missouri law anywhere.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What engine, garage, and window habits protect occupants from carbon monoxide poisoning while parked?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Odorless exhaust seeps into a closed cabin or garage quickly when idling with the heater or AC running.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: Which two precautions block deadly carbon monoxide fumes while driving in traffic or maintaining your car?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Open fresh-air vents suck tailpipe fumes from bumper-to-bumper traffic, and leaky mufflers pipe gas straight cabin-side.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: Why should spotting a single deer, or even roadkill, near fields or streams make you slow down immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Trailing fawns or does bolt across pavement seconds behind the lead animal right as drivers accelerate again.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: In which months and during what daily light windows do most Missouri deer collisions occur?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Mating and seasonal movement peak October through December plus January and May right around dusk and dawn.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: How do posted deer signs and fastened seat belts work together in rural wildlife corridors?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Alert scanning cuts strike odds, while belts and car seats protect riders during hard braking or impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: When oncoming lanes are empty at night, how do high-beam headlights help prevent deer strikes?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Brighter beams catch reflective retinas along ditch lines hundreds of feet before brown fur appears.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: If a deer jumps directly in front of your bumper and impact cannot be avoided, why hold your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel to save a fender sends cars into trees, rollovers, or head-on oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: What mirror check comes before braking hard for a deer, and what physics danger does nose-dive braking create?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Heavy braking pitches the hood downward so a struck deer slides over the grille toward the windshield.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: Which three parties or agencies enter the picture after colliding with a deer in Missouri?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Reporting the strike documents insurance claims and helps Missouri conservation staff track highway wildlife hotspots.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Where do you look up your car's recommended tire pressure, and how do you adjust it accurately?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Tire sidewalls list maximum pressure rather than vehicle spec, so match the door-jamb sticker with a gauge.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: On what routine schedule should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Catching bulges, nails, or uneven wear at home beats fighting a highway blowout at seventy miles per hour.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: What three calm steps should you take as soon as police lights flash in your mirror?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Signaling right away shows the officer you noticed them while you guide the car to safe shoulder space.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.question_text: Once pulled over for a traffic stop, what five actions keep the encounter calm and clear?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.teaching_text: Digging into gloveboxes or pockets before the officer arrives looks suspicious from behind your rear window.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.question_text: What three things should you ask your passengers to do during a roadside police stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.teaching_text: Sudden door openings or hidden hands make traffic stops tense for officers watching multiple occupants.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.question_text: After pulling over for an officer at night, what cabin switch should you flip on and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.teaching_text: Illuminating the interior counteracts spotlight glare and reassures the approaching officer that hands are clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.question_text: If there is a firearm or weapon inside your vehicle during a stop, when should you inform the officer?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.teaching_text: Calmly stating a weapon's presence upfront prevents dangerous surprises when opening a console or glovebox later.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.question_text: How should you reach out-of-reach registration papers, and what may you expect from an out-of-uniform officer?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.teaching_text: Telling the officer where your wallet sits keeps movements predictable, and official credentials verify plainclothes stops.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.question_text: If an officer asks you to exit your car during a stop, what two safety habits apply?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.teaching_text: Standing back off the fog line avoids passing mirrors while visible hands keep communication calm.
sec10-card-sec10-R27.must_match_memory_hook: Stand clear of traffic, hands out

visual_sync.text_span: Stand clear of traffic, hands out

sec10-card-sec10-F43.question_text: What does signing a traffic ticket legally mean, what can refusal cause, and where do you dispute it?
sec10-card-sec10-F43.teaching_text: Your signature merely promises appearance or response, so save legal arguments for the judge instead of the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R28.question_text: If you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop, how and where should you follow up?
sec10-card-sec10-R28.teaching_text: Ticket headers list the agency and officer name so you can file a formal report safely afterward.

sec10-card-sec10-R29.question_text: Which three constitutional protections remain yours throughout any traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R29.teaching_text: Pulling onto a highway shoulder never strips away protection against unreasonable searches, silence, or legal counsel.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What everyday factors can weaken your driving ability, and whose job is it to tell when you shouldn't get behind the wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Fatigue and everyday medicine slow reaction times just like liquor or drugs, and blaming the pill bottle never excuses an unsafe crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Before taking your first drink, what should you do with your car keys, and why?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Judgment slips after even a small amount of alcohol, so giving up your keys before you sip prevents impulsive late-night mistakes.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: What specific mental and physical effects can alcohol trigger that make safe driving harder?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Liquor attacks focus, comprehension, coordination, and alertness all at once, leaving you slow to spot hazards and quick to misjudge them.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: How quickly can just one or two drinks impair your driving or push you past Missouri's legal limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Test takers often guess it takes several rounds to break the law, yet a second drink frequently crosses the statutory threshold.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: What Blood Alcohol Content percentages make driving illegal in Missouri for standard drivers, commercial drivers, and drivers under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Missouri sets stricter ceilings for commercial operators and underage motorists because heavy rigs and inexperienced drivers leave far less margin for error.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Why can't you memorize just a single BAC percentage for every motorist on Missouri roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping adult, commercial, and underage scenarios, so always check who holds the wheel before picking zero point zero eight.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: Which substances or combinations can get you charged with DWI in Missouri if they impair your driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: A doctor's prescription or pharmacy receipt offers zero immunity on the road if the dose leaves you weaving or slow to brake.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: Does Missouri law separate prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs, or soften DWI penalties when drugs cause the impairment?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Whether impairment comes from cold tablets, pain pills, illicit substances, or liquor, Missouri applies the exact same courtroom and licensing punishments.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What roadside exercises might an officer ask you to perform if drinking is suspected, and what do they help decide?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Divided-attention balance checks reveal coordination loss right at the curb, giving the officer probable cause evidence when deciding on an arrest.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Once you are arrested for suspected impaired driving, which three samples can measure your Blood Alcohol Content?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Chemical testing after an arrest produces an exact Blood Alcohol Content reading rather than relying only on roadside observation.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: What happens to your Missouri driver license if you refuse an officer's request for a chemical BAC test?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Saying no to chemical testing triggers an automatic twelve-month revocation on its own, even before any courtroom trial takes place.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Which two independent legal tracks can penalize an impaired driver in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Drivers are often shocked to face separate licensing actions from the state agency alongside criminal punishments ordered by a judge.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What does the officer do right away if your chemical test hits zero point zero eight percent—or zero point zero two for a minor?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Your plastic card is confiscated on the spot and replaced with paperwork warning that suspension or revocation starts in fifteen days.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What temporary driving paper can that arrest notice include, and what two requests does it let you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Checking the officer-marked form carefully matters because your window to request an administrative review or ninety-day restricted privilege starts ticking immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: If you are granted an administrative hearing after a failed BAC test, how long may you keep driving legally?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Granting a review pauses the initial cutoff until the outcome is mailed, giving you fifteen days from that mailing date.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How do the two separate fifteen-day clocks on the arrest notice rules differ from each other?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Watch whether the question asks about the initial arrest paperwork or a granted hearing, since both use a fifteen-day buffer.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Under Missouri's administrative actions, what license penalty hits on a first offense versus a second offense within five years?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Administrative penalties escalate sharply inside a five-year lookback window, jumping from a temporary suspension to a full twelve-month revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: When an administrative action entry in the Missouri guide is marked with an asterisk, what must you install before reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: You cannot regain valid driving status on marked repeat administrative actions until breath-testing hardware is wired into your vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: After a judge finds you guilty of DWI or illegal BAC, when does your legal driving stop and how do you find out?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Once court paperwork arrives at the state agency, an official letter tells you the exact date you must stop driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: After a court conviction for impaired driving, what determines whether your license is suspended, revoked, or denied, and what hits your record?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Clean histories face shorter suspensions while repeat convictions trigger multi-year denials, and every courtroom conviction adds violation points.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What license suspension follows a first court-convicted impaired driving offense, and what restricted option might apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: First-time court offenders lose full privileges for ninety days, though eligible drivers can apply for restricted work-and-essential driving privileges.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What license loss comes with a second court-convicted offense overall, versus a second offense within five years?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Picking up a second conviction inside five years quintuples the time away from full licensing compared with widely spaced offenses.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: How long is your license denied after a third—or any subsequent—court-convicted impaired driving offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Three or more convictions trigger a decade-long license denial to keep chronic impaired offenders off Missouri highways.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Which BAC convictions count toward triggering Missouri's five-year license denial?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Older BAC convictions predating that statutory cutoff date cannot be stacked to impose the five-year denial tier.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: What three major types of punishment can follow a guilty verdict for drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Impaired driving is a criminal offense that hits your wallet, your freedom, and your ability to legally commute.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: If you hurt or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs, what jail, fine, and license penalties can you face?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Causing injury or death while impaired turns a traffic stop into multi-year imprisonment, five-thousand-dollar fines, and five-year license loss.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Up to how much jail time and fine money can a first DWI or BAC conviction carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Even a first-time conviction with zero crash damage exposes you to half a year behind bars plus court fines.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: How does the alcohol-effects section summarize the three parts of DWI punishment?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Both handbook chapters reinforce the exact same baseline numbers while reminding you that driving privileges disappear alongside criminal sentencing.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Up to how much jail time and fine money can a second DWI or BAC conviction bring?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: A second conviction doubles both maximum confinement and maximum fine compared with a first-time impaired driving offense.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What maximum jail term and fine apply to a third DWI or BAC conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: At offense number three, potential incarceration jumps to four years and the financial hit climbs fivefold to five thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: What maximum jail time and fine can hit on a fourth DWI or BAC conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: A fourth conviction keeps the five-thousand-dollar fine ceiling while stretching potential confinement up to seven years.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What prison sentence range applies to a fifth DWI or BAC offense in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Notice there is a mandatory five-year floor rather than an up-to ceiling once someone reaches a fifth offense.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: At what ages is possessing or purchasing alcohol illegal in Missouri?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Holding a closed can or buying liquor before turning twenty-one violates state law even if you never start an engine.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Under Missouri's Abuse and Lose Law, what triggers a ninety-day license loss for a driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Fake or altered IDs cost underage drivers ninety days off the road just like alcohol traffic stops or drugs in the car.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: What happens under Abuse and Lose if a driver under eighteen has or uses alcohol and faces a second offense charge?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Even when alcohol use happens away from the steering wheel, a second underage alcohol charge strips a teen's license for ninety days.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: How long can a driver aged twenty-one or older lose their license for having or using drugs while driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Abuse and Lose is not solely for teens—adults caught with drugs behind the wheel lose driving privileges for twelve months.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: What four requirements must you complete to regain your license after that one-year drug-related loss?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Because a full one-year revocation wipes out your active credential, you must pass the entire driver exam again alongside SATOP and insurance filings.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How does the Abuse and Lose license loss length compare between drivers under twenty-one and drivers twenty-one or older with drugs?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Do not assume underage penalties are always longer—an adult drug-driving violation quadruples the ninety-day underage suspension to a full year.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: For someone over fifteen and under twenty-one, which four liquor-related actions let a state court suspend or revoke a license?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Attempting to buy liquor at a counter can trigger court-ordered license suspension even before a single sip is taken.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Under Missouri's underage liquor rules, how is drinking alcohol treated in relation to possessing it?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Handing off the cup will not beat a Minor in Possession charge because having consumed liquor legally establishes possession.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: What are the three escalating license penalties for first, second, and third Minor in Possession offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Each Minor in Possession strike triples or quadruples your time off the road, ending in a full revocation on strike three.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What must you complete after any Minor in Possession action, and what two extra steps apply after a one-year revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Every MIP requires the forty-five-dollar fee and SATOP, while hitting the third-strike revocation adds two-year SR-twenty-two proof and retesting.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: How does a first Minor in Possession suspension length compare against an Abuse and Lose license loss?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Test questions pair these two youth laws to catch rushers—first-time MIP suspends for thirty days whereas Abuse and Lose takes ninety.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: What three core requirements get your license reinstated after an intoxication-related offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Skipping substance education or letting high-risk insurance lapse blocks your license return even after your suspension calendar finishes.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: Where must a driver facing DWI or BAC consequences file proof of insurance, and what form is typically used?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: A wallet insurance card is not enough—your insurer typically files an SR-twenty-two certificate directly with the state bureau.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: How long must proof of insurance remain on file, and what happens if coverage lapses early?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Canceling or missing a payment during those twenty-four months triggers immediate re-suspension until you refile proof and pay twenty dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Which specific driver is exempt from the two-year proof-of-insurance rule after an alcohol action?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Missouri grants this single insurance-filing exception only to an underage driver on a first zero point zero two percent administrative violation.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: Which three situations require you to use an ignition interlock on every vehicle you drive for at least six months after reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: High breath readings, crash damage, or repeat alcohol contacts mandate breath-locked vehicles for at least half a year.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: Which three vehicle systems is an ignition interlock wired into, and when must you blow into it?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Connecting the horn and headlights alongside the starter alerts nearby traffic if a driver skips or fails a rolling retest.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: How long must a required interlock stay installed, what must the final stretch show, and who covers the cost?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Any failed blow during the last ninety days prevents removal, and installation plus monthly servicing come straight out of your pocket.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Can an ignition interlock be required for longer than six months after reinstatement?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Treat six months as the statutory floor—a sentencing judge has full authority to keep the breath device installed longer.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Even when licensing rules don't mandate one, can a court order an ignition interlock after a first DWI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Judges can attach an interlock requirement to a very first DWI sentence regardless of whether administrative triggers applied.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: What happens if you fail to maintain a required ignition interlock, and how do you lift that suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Skipping monthly calibration puts you right back on suspension until your vendor services the unit and proof reaches the state bureau.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: How does Missouri's forty-five-dollar fee differ from the twenty-dollar interlock fee?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Exam choices swap dollar figures constantly, so pair forty-five dollars with intoxication reinstatement and twenty dollars with interlock lapses.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What license revocations hit on a first versus second court conviction for failing to install a required interlock?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Driving around an interlock order backfires badly, costing a full year on the first conviction and five years on the second.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Which two alcohol-enforcement violations both carry a one-year loss of driving privilege?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Bypassing breath checks—either refusing roadside chemical testing or dodging a required vehicle interlock—carries the exact same twelve-month penalty.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: Can prescription or over-the-counter medicine taken exactly as directed still impair driving, and what two checks should you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Following dosage directions cures symptoms without guaranteeing road alertness, so verify side effects with a professional and inspect the label first.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: What common side effect of over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines can compromise safe driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Antihistamines and decongestants sold without a prescription routinely trigger heavy fatigue that slows braking and steering responses.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: Why are pep pills, uppers, and diet pills risky for drivers once their brief alertness boost wears off?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: Stimulants mask exhaustion temporarily before crashing into jitters, blurred vision, dizziness, and scattered focus while you are still on the highway.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: What is the rule when a medicine bottle warns that it may cause drowsiness or dizziness?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: If a warning sticker mentions sleepiness or lightheadedness, wait until you have zero driving plans before taking a dose.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: What does Missouri say about taking someone else's prescription or combining different medicines?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Borrowed prescriptions are unlawful and uncalibrated for you, while unapproved drug combinations can multiply sedation without warning.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: Why must you never mix alcohol with any medicine before driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: Pairing even one drink with everyday medication can amplify drowsiness or trigger unpredictable reactions far worse than either substance alone.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: Where does marijuana rank among substances cited in motor vehicle crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Behind liquor, cannabis shows up more frequently than any other drug in post-collision investigations.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.question_text: Does Missouri's voter-approved medical marijuana law make driving under the influence of cannabis legal or safe?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.teaching_text: Holding a valid patient card starting in twenty twenty never legalizes impaired driving or shields you from a DWI arrest.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.question_text: Which driving skills does marijuana impair, and what two specific on-road problems do studies link to it?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.teaching_text: Distorted time-and-distance judgment plus dulled coordination cause drivers to drift across lane lines and brake late for hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: What did studies find when drivers combined alcohol with marijuana instead of using marijuana alone?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Stacking liquor onto cannabis compounds impairment instead of canceling out, producing noticeably worse lane drift than cannabis by itself.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: How does the Missouri Driver Guide define a substance use disorder?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: When ongoing drinking or drug use harms health, causes disability, or wrecks school, work, or home responsibilities, it crosses into a disorder.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: What elevated danger do individuals with a substance use disorder face on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Frequent impairment behind the wheel raises the odds of a serious collision that injures both the driver and innocent road users.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: What national resource offers help for substance use disorders, and what are its cost, privacy, and hours?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: Anyone seeking treatment referrals can reach SAMHSA day or night, three hundred sixty-five days a year, without cost or judgment.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.question_text: Why is starting alcohol or drugs at a young age one of the strongest predictors of future addiction?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.teaching_text: Adolescent neural pathways are still wiring up, making teen brains far more vulnerable to rapid, severe addiction damage than adult brains.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What credential is required to operate a motor vehicle or motor-driven cycle on Missouri public roads, and where is it issued?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Operating cars or motor-driven cycles on public streets without an active credential exposes you to unlicensed-driving citations.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: At what age does a Missouri resident need a state license to drive, and what rule applies to new residents with out-of-state cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Once you settle in Missouri and plan to drive, keeping an old out-of-state card will not replace getting a Missouri license.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Within what timeframe must an out-of-state commercial driver who moves to Missouri get a Missouri license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Commercial drivers relocating to Missouri face a strict thirty-day transfer window governed by the commercial manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which two groups holding a valid license from their home state are exempt from needing a Missouri license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Active service members and full-time college students can drive legally here so long as their home-state credential stays valid.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: Do you need a Missouri driver license to move a farm tractor or implement along a highway for agricultural work?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: State law exempts farm tractors and implements moved on highways for agricultural work from standard licensing rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What three rules apply to carrying, presenting, and sharing your license or permit whenever you drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Leaving your card at home or handing it to a friend turns a routine stop into serious legal trouble.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: At what age can you get an instruction permit, which GDL stage is it, and how may you drive on it?
