sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Starting stage one at fifteen lets teen drivers build supervised road habits with a licensed adult beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: When does the required six-month instruction-permit holding period before an intermediate license start counting?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Passing screening checks alone does not start your six-month countdown until the license office issues your temporary permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What special identifier appears on every Missouri permit issued to someone younger than twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Officers and clerks can spot underage status at a glance because every under-twenty-one permit carries a minor marking.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: At what age does the Class F intermediate license open, and what kind of driving privileges does this second GDL step grant?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Step two lets sixteen-year-olds drive solo under passenger and late-night curfews while crash risk is highest.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: At what age does the full Class F license open, and which motor vehicles does this basic operator card cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Once you reach eighteen, full Class F covers everyday vehicles that do not demand commercial or for-hire classes.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: On Missouri's licensing ladder, which credential opens at age sixteen and which two open at age eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Keep sixteen-year-old intermediate Class F distinct from both full Class F and Class E for-hire unlocking at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: Once you turn twenty-one with a minor-marked license, what two options do you have for that card?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: You do not have to rush in on your twenty-first birthday because your existing card stays valid until expiration.
sec01-card-sec01-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Buy replacement or use until expiry

visual_sync.text_span: Buy replacement or use until expiry

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What single factor sets your Missouri permit or license fee and how long the card stays valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Visiting a license office right before versus right after a milestone birthday can change both price and expiration length.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What prices and validity lengths does the fee chart list for an age-fifteen instruction permit versus a student permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Don't mix up the ten-dollar twelve-month standard permit with the one-dollar student permit tied to an approved course.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: What minimum age, dollar fee, and maximum validity period appear on the chart for an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Budget fourteen dollars at age sixteen for an intermediate credential that bridges up to two years toward eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: Starting at age eighteen, what two term lengths and prices does the chart list for a full Class F license?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Doubling from a three-year to a six-year full Class F term doubles the fee from sixteen-fifty to thirty-three dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: When does a Class F license let you ride a motorcycle, and which four checks are required to earn Class F?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Holding a basic car license alone never covers two-wheeled motorcycles unless an M endorsement sits on your card.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What minimum age and credential let you ride a motorcycle or motortricycle, and which Class M ages follow GDL rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Sixteen- to eighteen-year-old riders still fall under graduated licensing protections whether they choose standalone Class M or an endorsement.
sec01-card-sec01-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Class M sixteen, teens follow GDL

visual_sync.text_span: Class M sixteen, teens follow GDL

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: What three steps must you complete for a fifteen-and-a-half motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Starting on two wheels before sixteen demands certified rider training, written parent permission, and passing both F and M exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which four riding restrictions limit a fifteen-and-a-half-year-old motorcycle instruction permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Capping engine size at two hundred fifty cubic centimeters with daylight, radius, and zero-passenger rules protects brand-new teen riders.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Once you turn sixteen, is the rider training course required for a motorcycle permit, and who must take both written tests?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Turning sixteen drops the mandatory rider course, though unlicensed applicants still pass both Class F and Class M written exams.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Which exact motorcycle permit age bracket makes an approved rider training course mandatory?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Watch that half-year distinction closely because applicants sixteen and older can earn the motorcycle permit without taking the course.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: What fees apply to a motorcycle permit, and how does its maximum length compare with a regular instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: A motorcycle permit runs up to one hundred eighty-two days at ten or twelve-seventy-five, half the twelve-month car permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: Does riding a motorized bicycle require an M endorsement, and what license must the rider hold?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Mopeds skip the motorcycle endorsement requirement, yet riding one without at least a basic operator license is still illegal.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: At what age does Class E open, what exams are required, and which test does a current Class F holder skip?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Already holding Class F waives the road test when upgrading to Class E, though Chapter fifteen written material still counts.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which paid passenger-carrying or property-hauling jobs require a Missouri Class E license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Getting paid to shuttle up to fourteen passengers or haul cargo as part of your job requires Class E.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: When does regularly driving someone else's freight vehicle for work call for a Class E license instead of a CDL?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Regularly operating an employer's non-hazmat freight rig at or below twenty-six thousand pounds GVWR lands in Class E.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Which ride-share, taxi, and food-delivery drivers are exempt from needing a Class E for-hire license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Driving prepared meals or eligible ride-share and taxi cars at twelve thousand pounds or less works on standard Class F.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What minimum age applies to a Missouri CDL, and what higher age applies to Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsements?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: You can earn a base commercial credential at eighteen, while hauling hazmat or school buses requires turning twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How does the starting age for a Class M motorcycle license compare with base CDL and hazmat or bus endorsement ages?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Line up that three-step age ladder cleanly from sixteen on motorcycles to eighteen for CDL and twenty-one for endorsements.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: When does a Missouri nondriver ID normally expire, and how does age seventy or REAL ID status affect that term?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Standard nondriver cards expire after six years unless you apply at seventy-plus, though federal or immigration rules can cap terms.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: At what minimum age can someone get a nondriver ID strictly for voting, and how much does it cost?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Issuing free voter identification starting six months before age eighteen ensures eligible teens are ready on Election Day.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Can you legally drive using only the Missouri State Highway Patrol examination record before visiting a license office?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Treat that Highway Patrol score sheet strictly as paperwork to carry with your proofs to a license counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: Which four separate screenings make up the complete examination for a brand-new Missouri driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Every first-time driver proves law knowledge, eyesight, sign recognition, and behind-the-wheel control before earning a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: When a new resident transfers a valid out-of-state license, which checks are taken and what happens to old out-of-state cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Surrendering your prior card invalidates every license, permit, or ID from your former state while skipping written and road testing.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does the required screening list differ between a brand-new driver and someone transferring a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Current out-of-state license holders skip both the written exam and the driving test, taking only vision and road signs.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Besides first-time licensing, which three expiration, revocation, or administrative situations require all four exam parts?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Letting a license lapse past one hundred eighty-four days, losing it to points or alcohol revocation, or Director requests trigger retesting.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How many days does the Missouri guide equate to six months when deciding whether a lapsed license needs all four exam parts?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Renew before day one hundred eighty-five past expiration if you want to avoid repeating written and road exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which age span falls under Missouri's GDL program, and what five core identity and residency facts must applicants prove?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Every fifteen- to twenty-one-year-old GDL applicant brings complete paperwork covering legal presence, birthdate, Social Security, name history, and address.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Which documents prove U.S. citizen lawful status at a Missouri license office, and which two birth papers are rejected?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Souvenir hospital footprints or registration cards get turned away at the counter without a government vital-records seal or passport.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Which Missouri credential type accepts a vital-records birth certificate copy paired with a military ID or discharge papers, and which refuses it?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Pairing military identification with a birth-record copy clears lawful status for a standard card while falling short of federal upgrade rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.question_text: How do acceptable documents for proving a changed last name differ from proving a changed first or middle name?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.teaching_text: Marriage or divorce papers can update a surname, whereas changing a first or middle name strictly requires a certified court order.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: Which four documents can prove your required Social Security number on a Missouri license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Laminating your original Social Security card ruins its validity, so bring an unlaminated signed card, W-two, ten-ninety-nine, or printed paystub.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.question_text: What document must an applicant without a Social Security number bring, and which foreign student group is exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.teaching_text: Non-working F or J visa students skip the Social Security Administration status letter that other unassigned applicants must present.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.question_text: When might a Missouri license clerk let you state your Social Security number aloud instead of handing over paper proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.teaching_text: Once your number is already verified on a current Missouri credential, stating it verbally at renewal can save bringing extra forms.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.question_text: What extra review step can apply when someone files a Missouri credential application without a Social Security number?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.teaching_text: Applications lacking a Social Security number can route through central-office verification before the finished card prints and mails.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What four examples of everyday records can prove your Missouri residential address at the counter?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Bringing recent household records like current utility statements, property tax receipts, voter cards, or ninety-day government letters avoids counter delays.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Between government letterhead mail and utility bills used for residency proof, which carries a strict ninety-day limit?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Check dates on government agency mail carefully so you do not bring a letter older than ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: How many residency documents are needed for a REAL ID versus a standard card, and what if your mailing address differs?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Bring two separate residence proofs for federal-compliant cards plus an extra proof whenever you list a separate mailing address.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: May a post office box serve as your Missouri residential address, and where does the state send your finished card?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Every residential record requires a physical street home rather than a P.O. box, and your credential arrives by mail.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: How does the Missouri driver guide define a person's residential address?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Temporary stays elsewhere do not change your legal residence so long as you intend to return to that permanent home.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: If an applicant under twenty-one lacks address paperwork, how can a parent's document help on standard versus REAL ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: A parent or guardian's address paper satisfies a single-proof card, whereas federal-compliant cards still need a second residency document.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: Which core documents, along with your old card, can you be asked to present again when renewing a Missouri credential?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: Keep your full folder of identity, citizenship, address, surname, and tax-number records ready whenever renewal time arrives.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Who is allowed to skip place-of-birth paperwork when renewing a Missouri permit, license, or nondriver ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Seniors sixty-five and up renewing non-commercial, non-federal cards skip tracking down birth certificates at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: Which two driver situations can lead to a restricted Missouri license, and what might removing a restriction require?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Limited behind-the-wheel experience or health conditions can tailor your driving terms until a road check clears removal.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: Which three public-safety, court, or medical roles may request adding a restriction onto your Missouri card?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Traffic stops, courtroom findings, or medical evaluations can each prompt the state to narrow when or how you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: What criminal charge and record penalty can hit you for ignoring a restriction printed on your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Driving outside your restriction codes is treated like driving without a license and adds conviction points to your file.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: What driving limits do Missouri restriction letters A, C, F, G, and I each represent?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Know those five single-letter codes cold so you never confuse forty-five-mile-per-hour F with twenty-five-mile-radius G.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What do restriction letters Q and U indicate on a Missouri driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Code Q flags more than five active limits while U points to custom restriction text printed on the back.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.question_text: How do license endorsements work compared with restrictions, and what two privileges does the guide give as examples?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.teaching_text: Restrictions narrow how you may drive, whereas endorsements expand Class F, E, or M cards to cover motorcycles or school buses.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: Which recent medical episodes within six months before applying can trigger a required physician's statement?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Sudden loss of consciousness behind the wheel creates catastrophic crash risk, requiring medical clearance after recent episodes.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.question_text: Who can report doubts about a driver's medical fitness to drive, and what state report is used?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.teaching_text: Clerks, examiners, police, health professionals, and concerned relatives can file a Driver Condition Report to prompt medical review.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What trip purpose and passenger-capacity threshold require a Missouri school bus S endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Shuttle vans or buses built for eleven or more riders carrying students to school or school events require the S endorsement.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What minimum age and underlying license credentials qualify a driver to earn the school bus endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Applicants must be twenty-one or older and already carry either Class E for-hire or a CDL with Passenger endorsement.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What penalty can hit your school bus endorsement if you fail a drug, alcohol, or chemical check under school bus law?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Student transport carries zero room for impairment, so failing a school-bus chemical test can sideline that endorsement a year.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: At age seventy-five and up, how frequently must a school-bus driver retest behind-the-wheel bus skills?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Once a bus driver reaches seventy-five, biennial behind-the-wheel skills checks confirm sharp vehicle handling for student safety.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which four screenings must you pass to add the M endorsement onto an existing Missouri driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Even seasoned car drivers must pass motorcycle rules, vision, road signs, and an on-bike or motortricycle skills check.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Beyond school bus and motorcycle, which credential holders are the only drivers eligible for extra endorsements?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Tanker, hazmat, doubles, and passenger codes belong strictly to commercial driver licenses and commercial learner permits.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Where does the Department mail license renewal reminders, and which two learner permits receive no reminder?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Temporary instruction permits and commercial learner permits never trigger reminder postcards, so track your own expiration date.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.question_text: Through which two channels can you update your address after moving so renewal notices reach you?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.teaching_text: Keeping your mailing address current online or at a local branch stops renewal notices from going to old apartments.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: How many months before expiration can you renew a Missouri license, and which two tests happen at every renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Plan on reading the eye chart and identifying road signs every single time you renew, up to six months early.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Does missing a mailed reminder excuse a late renewal, and what ticket risk comes with driving on an expired card?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Missouri offers zero grace period for driving past expiration, even if a reminder card never showed up.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What option can a Missouri license office grant if you will be out of the state or country for an extended period?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Renewing ahead of a long overseas deployment or study term prevents coming home to a lapsed credential.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What is the longest period a Missouri driver license can remain valid, and may you drive once it expires?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: The day printed under expiration ends your legal driving authority immediately until you complete renewal.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.question_text: When can you take care of both your driver license renewal and vehicle registration renewal in a single visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.teaching_text: Matching renewal dates inside a six-month window saves a second trip to the license office.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Which extra tests return if you let your Missouri license stay expired more than six months before renewing?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Waiting past one hundred eighty-four days adds the written knowledge test and full road test onto vision and signs.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: What exact day count does the Missouri manual use for the six-month lapsed-license cutoff?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Memorize that exact four-day cushion past one hundred eighty so tricky calendar math never trips you up.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How long do returning service members whose license expired out of state have to renew without retesting, and can they drive before renewing?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Whichever deadline arrives first waives re-examination, though driving on the expired card before renewing stays illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.question_text: Who may renew a Missouri driver license by mail, and what must accompany the mail-in application form?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.teaching_text: Active-duty personnel and their dependents stationed away can submit the mail-in license form with required documents and fees.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: How do you replace a lost, stolen, or destroyed Missouri license, and what alternative opens if expiration is within six months?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: If your missing card was already within six months of expiring, renewing early saves buying a short-lived duplicate.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Can a non-commercial driver renew during a suspension versus during a revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Renewing during suspension keeps you past the lapse retest cutoff, whereas revocations block renewal except chemical-test refusals.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: When does a suspended driver physically get back a license that was renewed during the suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Completing renewal paperwork stops the expiration clock, yet the card stays withheld until every reinstatement step clears.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: What registry does saying yes to the counter donor prompt join, and whose permission governs that decision?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Enrolling in Missouri's Organ and Tissue Donor Registry records binding first-person consent unless you later change it yourself.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What does the optional donor symbol on the front of a Missouri card look like, and what is the fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Both joining the state donor registry and printing the red-heart green-banner emblem on your card are completely free.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.question_text: What follow-up choice is offered right after joining the donor registry, and how can you add a donor sticker later?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.teaching_text: Even if you skip the printed front heart at the counter, you can order a back-of-card donor sticker online later.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.question_text: Which two charitable funds must every Missouri license clerk ask if you want to support?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.teaching_text: Expect a routine counter prompt inviting voluntary contributions toward organ donation outreach or blindness awareness programs.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Who may request a DHH notation on a Missouri card, when must you ask, and why does it help?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Printing DHH on the credential alerts police and paramedics during roadside emergencies that the holder is deaf or hard of hearing.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.question_text: What must a Missouri resident hold to add a boater safety indicator, and what is its first-time fee?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.teaching_text: Adding that one-dollar indicator onto your driver license saves carrying a separate Boating Safety Education Card on the water.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.question_text: Where does a permanent disability indicator print on a Missouri card, what paperwork is required, and is it mandatory?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.teaching_text: This optional, zero-cost back-of-card indicator requires a signed physician form and is never forced by state law.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.question_text: How can an eligible former service member get VETERAN printed on the front of a Missouri card, and what does it cost?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.teaching_text: Presenting accepted discharge records like an honorable DD two-fourteen prints VETERAN on the front free of charge.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.question_text: Where does an optional medical alert notation for conditions like diabetes, epilepsy, or autism appear, and what does it cost?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.teaching_text: Submitting the signed medical-alert form places a free front-side cue for first responders without any legal mandate.

sec02-card-sec02-R22.question_text: What does the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act require states to do with personal license and vehicle records?
sec02-card-sec02-R22.teaching_text: Federal law shields your home address and identity details in DMV databases unless specific statutory exceptions apply.

sec02-card-sec02-R23.question_text: What voter-registration service does a Missouri license clerk offer during your counter visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R23.teaching_text: Motor-voter rules let you confirm or update your voting address and sign fresh registration paperwork in one stop.

sec02-card-sec02-R24.question_text: Which applicants may register with the Selective Service while applying for a Missouri license or permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R24.teaching_text: Young men in the eighteen-to-twenty-six window can handle federal Selective Service registration right on their license application.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: What happens when a parent or guardian files a denial form for a driver under eighteen, and how long does it last?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: A parent's filing with the Director of Revenue cancels even an active teen license until age eighteen or parental clearance.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Which five impairment, crash-scene, or application offenses can get a Missouri license suspended, revoked, or denied?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Impaired driving, chemical refusal, fleeing crashes, skipping required accident reports, or lying on applications each strip driving rights.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Which insurance, point, court, child-support, fuel-theft, or youth-liquor violations can also cost you your Missouri license?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Even off-road acts like stealing gas, minor liquor possession, lending your card, or skipping child support trigger license loss.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Which fake-ID, Bureau-exam, vehicle-felony, fatal-crash, or insurance-fraud acts are grounds to lose your license?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Altering IDs for alcohol, dodging a Bureau exam order, vehicle felonies, fatal crashes, or fake insurance proof revoke privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: What three sequential stages must every first-time Missouri driver under eighteen complete under GDL law?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Graduated licensing builds skill gradually from supervised driving to restricted solo driving before full privileges unlock.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: At what age does GDL step one open, which three tests does it require, and how long can the permit last?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Passing vision, road signs, and the written test at fifteen starts up to a year of supervised practice.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Which four adult roles are authorized to appear at the license office and sign a teen's permit permission statement?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: An eligible parent, stepparent, legal guardian, or federal residential job-program trainer must sign permission in person at the counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: Who qualifies to ride in the front passenger seat beside a Missouri permit driver younger than sixteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Non-relatives supervising a fifteen-year-old must be twenty-five-plus, licensed at least three years, and carry written parent permission.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: Once a Missouri instruction permit holder turns sixteen, who may serve as the required front-seat supervisor?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Turning sixteen widens your front-seat supervisor pool to any validly licensed adult aged twenty-one or older.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How do the non-family front-seat supervisor rules relax when a permit holder reaches age sixteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Before sixteen, non-family supervisors need age twenty-five, three licensed years, and parent notes; at sixteen, licensed twenty-one-plus suffices.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: While driving on an instruction permit, who wears seat belts, what card must you carry, and how do permit renewals work?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Every occupant must buckle up, the physical permit card must ride with you, and renewals skip retaking written tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: How many total and nighttime behind-the-wheel hours are required during the permit stage, and who gives them?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Logging at least ten after-dark hours inside your forty supervised hours builds crucial low-visibility judgment before solo driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: If a teen's parent, stepparent, grandparent, or guardian has a physical disability, how can behind-the-wheel instruction be handled?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Naming up to two trusted designees ensures teens with physically disabled guardians can still complete their forty practice hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: How many months and days must you hold your instruction permit before advancing to an intermediate license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Missouri counts that six-month practice minimum as one hundred eighty-two full days starting the day after permit issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: What exact day count and start day define the six-month permit period for GDL step two?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Do not count the issue day itself because the one-hundred-eighty-two-day clock begins the next morning.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Which two conviction-free lookback windows are required to earn a Missouri intermediate license between sixteen and eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Any traffic conviction inside six months or alcohol offense inside twelve months delays your upgrade to solo driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Who confirms your forty hours at the office for an intermediate license, and when must vision, sign, and written results be retaken?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: An approved adult verifies your forty hours in person, and earlier exam scores older than one year require retesting.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: During the first six months on an intermediate license, how many non-family passengers under nineteen may ride with you?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Peer distraction spikes teen crash rates, so the first half-year caps non-family riders under nineteen at just one.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: After your first six months on an intermediate license, how many non-family passengers under nineteen may you carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Even after six months of solo experience, carrying four young friends outside your immediate family violates GDL limits.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: Which age and relationship group is counted under both intermediate-license passenger caps?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Passengers nineteen or older and household immediate-family members do not count against your one- or three-friend cap.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: During what activity may the intermediate-license passenger limits not apply?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Missouri carves out an agricultural-work exception when teen intermediate drivers transport young farmhands on the job.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: Between which overnight hours may an intermediate driver not drive alone, and what four exceptions allow it?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Overnight solo driving shuts down during those four pre-dawn hours except for jobs, school events, emergencies, or adult company.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: Which relatives count as immediate family under the Missouri intermediate-license passenger rules?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Cousins or friends do not count as exempt family; only parents, grandparents, siblings, step-siblings, and household adopted or foster kids qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Up to how many years is a Missouri intermediate driver license valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Document verification status sets the exact end date, with two years serving as the maximum intermediate term.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: At age eighteen, what license, clean-record window, and two tests are required to graduate to the full under-twenty-one license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: Keep your intermediate record clean of both traffic and alcohol offenses for twelve straight months to skip another road test.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: How long is the clean-record check for both traffic and alcohol offenses at step three, and what status blocks upgrading?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Unlike step two's split six-and-twelve-month check, step three demands twelve clean months on both and an unsuspended privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Up to how many years is the full under-twenty-one Missouri driver license valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Graduating at eighteen gives up to a three-year credential carrying you to twenty-one, depending on document verification.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: How recently expired can a transferable out-of-state license be, and what test record does a first-time applicant bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Newcomers can swap recently lapsed out-of-state cards inside that six-month window, while brand-new drivers bring passed Patrol paperwork.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: What paperwork must a driver upgrading a Missouri license bring to the Highway Patrol examination station?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Highway Patrol examiners check the exact same identity, status, and residency documents before administering upgrade tests.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Roughly what share of applicants fail the Missouri written exam on their first attempt according to the guide?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Guessing common-sense answers falls short when nearly fifty percent of unprepared walk-ins miss passing on attempt one.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Why do car drivers frequently collide with motorcycles they claim they never saw?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Single headlights and slim silhouettes make judging a bike's closing speed deceptive across intersections.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: Why shouldn't a motorcyclist assume car drivers will yield right-of-way at an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Left-turning cars routinely pull out ahead of bikes that look farther away or slower than reality.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: May your car ever share a single lane side-by-side with a motorcycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Riders weave inside their lane to dodge potholes, oil slicks, and wind gusts safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: How much lateral space does a motorcycle deserve when you pass — and what if the lane is narrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Squeezing past inside the same lane blasts the rider with mirror-close wind turbulence.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Which four surface or weather hazards force motorcyclists to adjust speed or lane position unexpectedly?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Slick steel lids or diagonal rails barely felt inside four tires can dump two wheels instantly.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What protective headgear does the Missouri guide state law requires for motorcycle riders?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Expect written exam questions testing Missouri's statutory helmet requirement for motorcycle riders.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Which two licensing options authorize riding a motorcycle on Missouri public streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: A plain Class F operator license without an M endorsement cannot legally cover street motorcycles.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Which four visibility and signaling habits help motorcyclists stand out to surrounding drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: High-contrast jackets, active night lighting, blind-spot avoidance, and early signals cut car-on-bike surprises.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Up to how many pounds can a typical tractor-trailer weigh — and past how many feet can a long rig stretch?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Twenty times a sedan's mass spanning six car lengths demands extra passing and braking respect.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Beyond how many feet can multi-trailer rigs stretch on busy intercity highways?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Passing tandem or triple trailers takes noticeably longer highway runway than passing single vans.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Which two risky pull-out or lane-change moves right ahead of a large vehicle invite rear-end crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Ducking ahead of forty tons only to hit your brakes for a driveway leaves zero stopping room.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a truck or bus driver can see your car?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Losing sight of the trucker's side mirrors confirms you are tucked inside a blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Which three areas around a truck or bus form the No-Zone — and how should you treat them?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Entire sedans vanish beside trailers, tight behind doors, and right below high cab grilles.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What two lingering habits beside and behind a large vehicle should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Cruising next to trailer tires or hugging rear doors traps your car with nowhere to swerve.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What landmark in your inside mirror clears merging back ahead of a truck — and how must you manage speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Waiting for the whole cab to appear keeps your rear bumper out of the trucker's front No-Zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: At which two highway spots should cars vacate the right lane to accommodate heavy trucks?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Stepping left lets climbing rigs crawl safely and inspected semis merge back onto the highway.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Why must you leave extra braking room when following a placarded hazardous-materials truck toward railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Federal and state rules force hazmat tankers to halt even when crossing gates stay up.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Why might a semi swing left right before turning right — and what should you check before passing?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Sneaking up along the right curb while a trailer setups wide crushes cars against utility poles.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, compare an average car's stopping distance with a loaded tractor-trailer's?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Loaded rigs need nearly three times a sedan's stopping runway — over a football field.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: How many gears might a loaded semi work through — and how much heavier is its load per engine than a car's?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Pulling up to forty times a car's weight through ten shifts means trucks build highway speed gradually.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Instead of racing ahead to cut off a truck before your exit or turn, what calmer choice costs mere seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Trading three seconds behind a trailer beats gambling inside a four-hundred-foot stopping zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: What visual illusion about a tractor-trailer's size causes intersection crashes with cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Large objects appear to creep across your field of view even while barreling along at highway pace.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Even with a steady Walk signal or green light, what must a pedestrian confirm before stepping off the curb?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Painted lines and white Walk symbols cannot physically stop a distracted right-turning SUV.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Which signals bar starting across the street — and what if Don't Walk starts flashing while you are mid-crosswalk?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Flashing orange hands give walkers already in the lane clearance time while holding curb arrivals back.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Where should pedestrians cross in business districts — and who holds right-of-way during a mid-block crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Stepping between parked cars mid-block forfeits crosswalk priority and requires yielding to all vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: On a road with no sidewalk, which side should you walk along?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Facing approaching headlights lets walkers see drifting cars early and step onto grass.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: Instead of standing in an active lane to talk with a driver, how should a pedestrian handle the conversation?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Letting the driver pull to the curb keeps pedestrians out of passing mirrors and traffic lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Does a green light excuse hitting or crowding a pedestrian — even one jaywalking against the signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Drivers carry a constant duty of care to avoid striking pedestrians regardless of who broke signal rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What rule applies whenever a vehicle ahead stops or slows for a pedestrian?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Whip-around passing hides the crossing walker behind the stopped hood until impact.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: When does a lower school-zone speed limit apply — and how must you respond to a school crossing patrol?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Slowing whenever lights flash or children walk — and halting on patrol signals — guards unpredictable young walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: What must your vehicle do when someone crosses carrying a white cane — plain or red-tipped — or a guide dog?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Rolling slowly or honking startles guide dogs and disorients blind pedestrians listening to traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Which pedestrians inside a marked or unmarked crosswalk earn your yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Unmarked corner extensions count identically to painted stripes whenever walkers near your travel lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: Where must you avoid stopping at a red light — and what comes before driving across a sidewalk?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Parking across crosswalk paint forces walkers out into live cross-street bumper lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: How should you set speed along residential streets lined with parked cars?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Children darting from between parked SUVs give scant braking feet if you overdrive your sightline.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: While looking left for traffic gaps on a right-on-red turn, where else must you scan — and for whom?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Staring left at oncoming cars blinds right-turners to joggers or bikes stepping off the right curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Where do most crashes involving bicycles and mopeds occur — and what respect do riders deserve?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Scanning corners actively and granting full vehicle consideration prevents right-hook and left-cross bike wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Before turning right onto a main street, why must you look right as well as left?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Riders pedaling against traffic along sidewalks or curbs arrive silently from your passenger side.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: How should you make a right turn when you are following a cyclist approaching the same corner?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Sprinting past a bike only to hook right across its front wheel causes classic right-hook crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: When turning left across an oncoming cyclist's path, when must you wait and yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Bicycles roll faster than they look — wait unless you can clear the turn well ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How much space should you give when overtaking a bicycle or moped — and what if the lane is tight?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Treat bicycles and mopeds like motorcycles when passing — change lanes completely rather than brushing elbows.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: When may motorists cross a striped bicycle lane — and who holds priority inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Striped bike lanes allow crossing for turns or driveways only after yielding to approaching riders.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: What check belongs right before swinging a parked car door open toward a travel or bike lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Swinging steel doors open suddenly leaves passing cyclists zero room to brake or swerve.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: How do bicycle and moped rights and duties compare with motorists' — and which way must they ride?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Unlike pedestrians walking facing cars, wheeled cyclists and mopeds always roll with traffic flow.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: While slower cyclists normally ride far right, which four situations allow taking the middle or left?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Taking the lane past potholes, narrow pavement, or right-turn pockets keeps cyclists predictable and visible.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: Which four roadside traps explain why cyclists leave buffer space away from the extreme right edge?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Skinny bike tires wash out instantly on gravel lips, sunken grates, or ragged gutter seams.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: Where may a bicyclist ride on a one-way street — and what comes before shifting position?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Left-curb riding on one-way streets simplifies left turns once the rider checks and signals.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: What smart option helps a less experienced cyclist handle heavy traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Waiting calmly near the curb until platoons clear beats weaving nervously through fast cars.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: For teen and adult bicyclists, how does riding in the street compare with riding on sidewalks?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Sidewalk cyclists pop into driveways and crosswalks faster than backing or turning drivers expect.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Where on the federal interstate highway system may mopeds operate?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Thirty-mile-per-hour mopeds are prohibited from every ramp and lane of federal interstates.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: What credential is required to ride a moped on Missouri public streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Even without license plates or motorcycle endorsements, street mopeds still require a valid driver license.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: Does Missouri law require helmets on mopeds or bicycles — and why wear a certified one anyway?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: While state statute skips moped and bicycle helmets, certified shells slash fatal brain trauma.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does Missouri treat safety-certified helmets for moped and bicycle riders — law or recommendation?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Contrast mandatory motorcycle helmets against recommended-only helmets for mopeds and pedal bikes.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: How many feet of clearance should cyclists and moped riders keep when passing to the left of cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Giving parked doors and moving fenders three to four feet clears sudden door swings.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Does Missouri require registering or inspecting mopeds and bicycles — and what rule DOES apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Skipping license tags and inspection stickers never waives mandatory night lights, reflectors, and brakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: During what sunset-to-sunrise window must a bicycle run a white front light — visible from how far?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: From thirty minutes post-sunset to thirty minutes pre-sunrise, oncoming drivers need five-hundred-foot headlamp visibility.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What minimum size rear red reflector — or light — does a bike need, visible how far in low beams?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Overtaking cars approach fast from behind, demanding six-hundred-foot rear red reflection or lamp visibility.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: From how many feet in low beams must reflectors or lights on pedals, cranks, shoes, or ankles show?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Up-and-down pedaling motion catches driver eyes unmistakably at two hundred feet after dark.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How far in low beams must side reflectors or lights show on a bike — and which mopeds are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Three-hundred-foot side reflection alerts cross-street cars, while NHTSA-compliant mopeds carry factory lighting.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Match all four nighttime bicycle visibility distances — front white, rear red, sides, and pedals?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Locking five hundred front, six hundred rear, three hundred side, and two hundred pedal nails any lighting question.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: Between which hours do car-bicycle collisions jump sharply — and what prevents nearly all of them?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Unlit dark-clothed night riding fuels fatal collisions that required lamps and reflectors prevent.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: Do you need a driver license or motorcycle license to ride a Missouri-compliant electric bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Compliant e-bikes follow bicycle licensing rules rather than moped or motorcycle credential rules.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Which three hardware specs — pedals, seating, and motor wattage ceiling — define a Missouri electric bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Motors stay strictly below seven hundred fifty watts paired with operable pedals and a seat.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: What wheel count, transmission type, cubic-centimeter cap, and horsepower cap define a Missouri motorized bicycle?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Exceeding fifty cubic centimeters, three brake horsepower, or manual shifting bumps a bike into motorcycle rules.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: What maximum speed on flat ground keeps a device inside Missouri's motorized-bicycle category?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Any scooter capable of topping thirty miles per hour on flat pavement exits the moped class.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: What lights do cars inside an organized funeral procession run, and how closely do they follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Blinking hazard lights and tight safe spacing signal cross traffic that the column moves together.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: Where do organized funeral processions hold right-of-way — and what two exceptions outrank them?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Even when your cross-light turns green, wait for the entire flashing procession unless sirens or officers intervene.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.question_text: Which three moves are forbidden for drivers outside a moving funeral procession?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.teaching_text: Passing requires a separate passing lane — never slice between cars or tag along to jump reds.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: When may an outside driver enter an intersection while a funeral procession crosses on red?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: A right turn away from the column stays legal only when it never intersects the procession's line.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.question_text: How does the Missouri guide define road rage and its real-world consequences?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.teaching_text: Letting frustration boil into retaliation turns two-ton vehicles into weapons that wreck property and lives.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: Which horn, headlight, spacing, braking, lane, and physical actions count as road-rage behavior?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Flashing high beams, rude gestures, deliberate lane blocking, and chasing escalate minor mistakes into crimes.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: Can habitual road-rage reactions be unlearned — and what personal trait does it take?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: Choosing patience before touching the horn rewires aggressive driving reflexes over time.

sec05-card-sec05-F49.question_text: Walk through your emotional response, mental notes, and follow-up when targeted by road rage?
sec05-card-sec05-F49.teaching_text: Refusing eye-for-an-eye retaliation while noting location, car, and driver details lets police intervene safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F51.question_text: If you spot a suspected drunk driver, whom do you contact immediately and what three details help?
sec05-card-sec05-F51.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers the license plate, car-and-driver description, and milepost helps patrol intercept fast.

sec05-card-sec05-F52.question_text: What maximum dollar fine and jail term can a Missouri court impose for highway littering?
sec05-card-sec05-F52.teaching_text: Tossing trash out a window carries criminal court penalties up to both fine and jail.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: Why does flicking a glowing cigarette butt out a car window endanger trailing traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Highway slipstreams whip burning embers straight through open windows, truck beds, or motorcycle helmets.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Once parked, what clearance from travel lanes and visibility from both directions must your car have?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Tucking well off travel lanes on open sightlines prevents oncoming or overtaking cars from clipping your bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What type of parking area should you always choose whenever one is available?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Marked lots, garages, and stalls keep parked doors and bumpers away from moving traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: When you have no choice except parking on the roadway itself, how should you position your tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Snugging right up beside the curb maximizes passing room along narrow neighborhood streets.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Even without a No Parking sign, what traffic-flow or safety test rules out a parking spot?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Any spot that chokes normal lane flow or forces blind swerves is illegal to take.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What brake step and transmission setting belong every single time you park a manual or automatic car?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Setting the parking brake takes strain off an automatic's parking pawl and locks a stick-shift in gear.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Contrast how you secure the shifter in a manual car versus an automatic — and what step both share?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Neutral lets a stick-shift roll if cables slacken, so leave manuals in gear alongside the brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What two habits with your ignition key and door locks apply whenever your parked car leaves your sight?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Pulling keys every stop and locking whenever out of sight stops opportunistic drive-off thefts.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Before cracking your door after parking, what must you check — and which side should riders and kids use?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Routing children and passengers onto the sidewalk side keeps everyone out of active bumper lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Whom specifically must you scan for before opening a street-side door — and how fast should it shut?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Bicyclists track right beside parked fenders where an unlatched swinging door leaves zero escape room.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: When curb-side exit isn't practical, under what condition may you open a street-side door?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Looking back in your mirror and over your shoulder ensures a clear gap before unlatching.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Which two actions are mandatory right before pulling out of any curb stall or parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Signaling after scanning mirrors and blind spots warns approaching cars that your parked bumper is moving.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: On a one-way street without prohibiting signs, which side or sides may you normally park along?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Because all lanes flow one direction, left-curb parking stays aligned with traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which curb side and facing direction are illegal when parking on a two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Crossing oncoming traffic nose-first to grab a left-side curb spot sets up blind head-on pull-outs.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Contrast legal left-side street parking on a one-way street against a two-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Left-curb parking is legal only when traffic flows one-way rather than two-way.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Besides roadside metal signs, what visual clue right along the pavement edge shows parking limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Cities paint curb edges where signposts are missing or spaced far apart.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Which painted curb color, roadway structure, and fire-rescue fixture forbid parking beside them?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Fire engines need unobstructed hydrant hookups and bridges lack spare breakdown shoulders.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Does a yellow-painted curb ban parking even when zero No Parking signs stand nearby?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Never assume a missing signpost makes a yellow-painted curb legal to use.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which four everyday corner, walkway, and property spots are strictly off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Blocking corners, walks, or driveways traps residents and forces walkers into live lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: What does the blue-and-white International Symbol of Access reserve a parking stall for?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Wider stalls placed closest to building ramps serve drivers and passengers with mobility disabilities.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Beyond displaying disability plates or a placard, what human presence is required to use a handicapped space?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: The person with a physical disability must actually ride along or be picked up or dropped off.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Why isn't having valid disability plates on the family car enough by itself to park in a reserved stall?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Running solo errands in a relative's plated SUV without that person aboard breaks Missouri law.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: May any driver park inside the painted striped access aisle beside a handicapped space?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Side-entry wheelchair vans need every inch of that striped zone to deploy ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: When does using a family member's legitimate disability placard or plates become an offense?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Placards belong to the qualified individual rather than granting household-wide parking perks.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Which two distinct violations around handicapped stalls draw citations even if a placard exists?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Officers ticket both access-aisle parkers and solo drivers borrowing an absent holder's hanger.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What minimum and maximum dollar fine hits a conviction for misusing a Missouri handicapped parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Expect Missouri's fifty-to-three-hundred-dollar fine bracket to appear on permit questions covering accessible stalls.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Which way does the Missouri guide tell you to turn your front wheels when parking on a hill — and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Angling wheels sharply toward the road edge steers any brake failure away from live center lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What safety goal explains turning your wheels toward the roadside whenever parked on a grade?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Gravity pulls an unlatched car off the pavement edge instead of diagonally across oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Before stepping out on a hill, what three mechanical steps cover wheels, engine-and-gear, and brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Combining angled tires, engaged transmission gear, and a set parking brake triples hill-holding security.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How do the terms 'emergency brake' and 'parking brake' relate on Missouri's hill-parking checklist?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Whether called emergency brake or parking brake on exam questions, pull or press that same lever.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: After setting wheels, gear, and brake on a hill, what four closing steps cover keys, mirror, and locks?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Glancing at the rearview mirror before cracking your door catches cars climbing or descending beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Which three key-and-door steps finish hill parking identically to flat-ground parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Never leave keys dangling inside or doors unlocked just because you parked on a residential slope.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Where and how many feet away should you line up beside the forward car to start parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Stopping eighteen inches alongside the front car sets the exact pivot geometry for backing in.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Which way do you cut the wheel first when backing into a parallel stall — while watching your front bumper?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: As you reverse right into the pocket, your front nose swings left toward passing lane traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Once your nose clears the forward car's rear bumper, what two wheel cuts center you in the stall?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Counter-steering sharp left tucks your nose curbward, then pulling forward right centers both bumpers.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Recite the three sharp steering-wheel directions from start to finish of a standard right-curb parallel park?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Right angles in, left straightens the nose behind the lead car, and right centers forward.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Where between the forward and rear parked cars should your vehicle sit when finished parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Leaving balanced room fore and aft lets both neighboring drivers pull out without bumping you.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: How many days do you have to visit a license office and title a newly bought car or one brought into Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Mark your calendar the day you buy or move because waiting past day thirty triggers late title penalties.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Does Missouri give a different titling deadline to residents buying a car versus newcomers moving into the state?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Missouri uses one uniform thirty-day titling clock whether you bought locally or relocated from another state.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What legal fact does a vehicle title prove, and what happens if you apply past thirty days after buying?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Your title is your legal ownership certificate, and missing the thirty-day purchase deadline adds an avoidable penalty fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: Where do you apply for a Missouri vehicle title, and what are the exact title and processing fees?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Every license office charges both the eight-dollar-fifty title charge and a separate nine-dollar processing charge.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: Between Missouri's base title fee and the processing fee charged alongside it, which dollar figure is higher?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Watch that subtle fifty-cent swap because the nine-dollar processing charge actually exceeds the eight-fifty title fee.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Beyond the title and processing charges, what taxes must be paid when you title a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Budget for combined state and local sales taxes before heading to the license counter so titling finishes smoothly.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Which two resources let you look up how much vehicle sales tax you will owe before titling?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Checking the Department's online sales-tax calculator or calling a local branch prevents sticker shock at the counter.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What do you leave the license counter with after applying for a title, and how do you receive the title itself?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Hold onto your counter application receipt while the Department prints and mails your official ownership title.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Why does the Missouri guide warn you never to leave your vehicle title inside the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Storing an ownership title in your glovebox hands a car thief the exact document needed to forge a sale.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Which two pairs of vehicle-buying factors change the exact paperwork required for a Missouri title?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Check whether your car is brand-new or pre-owned and bought inside or outside Missouri before gathering forms.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Which two titling documents does a Missouri dealer hand you when you buy a brand-new vehicle in state?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Make sure you leave the dealership with both the title application and the assigned Manufacturer's Statement of Origin.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What two facts about a vehicle's history does a Manufacturer's Statement of Origin establish?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: An MSO serves as a vehicle's birth certificate before any state has ever issued its first title or plates.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: On a brand-new vehicle, who completes the odometer disclosure and where is it located?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Both you and the selling dealer complete the mileage disclosure printed on the reverse side of the MSO.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: Where is a brand-new vehicle's odometer reading recorded instead of on a title?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Because a brand-new car has no prior title yet, its starting mileage belongs strictly on the MSO.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: What document must any Missouri used-car seller give you, and what extra form should a Missouri dealer include?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Never hand over cash for a used car in Missouri without receiving a properly assigned title from the seller.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How does the ownership transfer paper for a brand-new vehicle differ from that of a used vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Dealers transfer brand-new cars with an MSO, whereas every used sale transfers ownership on an assigned title.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Which seven buyer, mileage, sale, lien, and signature details belong on a properly assigned Missouri title?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Missing a sale price, date, lienholder entry, or required signature sends you back to track down the seller.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Which vehicle model years need a title-back mileage disclosure, and at what vehicle age does it stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Vehicles from model year twenty eleven onward carry mandatory title mileage disclosures until reaching twenty years old.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: When selling a twenty-eleven-or-newer vehicle under twenty years old, who enters the mileage and where?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: The seller records exact dashboard mileage inside the title assignment block before both parties confirm it.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: How do the buyer and seller verify the recorded mileage, and what extra document may occasionally apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Having both buyer and seller print and sign their names locks in the disclosed mileage against tampering disputes.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: Which two documents do you need to title a brand-new vehicle purchased from an out-of-state dealer?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Pair the out-of-state dealer's invoice or bill of sale with the assigned MSO so Missouri can calculate tax and title.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: Which title paperwork is needed when bringing home a used vehicle bought outside Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Bring either the private seller's properly assigned title or the out-of-state dealership's reassigned title to the counter.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: When buying a used car out of state from a dealership rather than a private owner, what kind of title might you receive?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Out-of-state dealers often transfer ownership using a dealer reassignment rather than a direct private-seller assignment.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Which two papers replace a title if you buy a vehicle in a state that does not issue titles?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Combining a signed bill of sale with that state's most recent registration certificate proves legal ownership chain.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: When the title assigned to you comes from another state, what extra check form is required and who fills it out?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Stop by a licensed Missouri inspection station first so an inspector verifies your vehicle ID number and odometer.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Under what exact title condition is the ID or OD verification form required, and who alone may complete it?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Missouri titles skip the ID or OD form, and when another state's title requires it, only licensed stations qualify.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: Where does the Missouri driver guide direct you for rules on titling salvage, dismantling, or rebuilding vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Salvage and rebuilt cars follow specialized inspection and branding rules handled directly through the Motor Vehicle Bureau.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: Where must Missouri residents register their vehicles, and how long does a newcomer have after moving in?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Newcomers get thirty days after establishing Missouri residency to switch their vehicle registration over to Missouri plates.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Which exact day starts the thirty-day vehicle registration countdown for someone moving into Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Start your thirty-day countdown as soon as Missouri residency begins rather than waiting until old plates expire.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: What must a new resident do with an existing out-of-state vehicle title when registering in Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: You cannot hold active titles from two states at once, so turn in the prior title when applying.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What paperwork must you bring when a lienholder keeps possession of your prior state's title?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Pairing your lender's non-surrender letter with one of the three accepted backup papers lets Missouri register your car.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: What items do you receive for your vehicle once you complete Missouri registration?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Affixing your Missouri plates and current expiration year tab shows officers your registration is active.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: What vehicle factors determine registration fees for Missouri passenger cars versus commercial trucks?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Passenger plate fees scale by taxable horsepower while commercial fees follow operating zone and gross weight plus processing.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: When does Missouri let you register a vehicle for two years instead of one year?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Two-year plates unlock only when your vehicle's model year parity matches the calendar year; mismatches get one year.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: During an even-numbered calendar year like twenty eighteen, which vehicles qualify for a two-year Missouri registration?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: An even calendar year pairs with even model-year cars for two-year tags while odd models take one year.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: What optional plate styles can Missouri owners pick beyond standard tags, and how does pricing work?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Personalized or specialty designs carry an additional plate fee stacked on top of your regular registration charge.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: Roughly how early should a mailed plate renewal notice arrive, and what if it never shows up?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Mail delays never excuse expired tags, so renew before your tab month ends whether a postcard arrived or not.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: What simple step helps ensure your plate renewal notice actually reaches your mailbox?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Filing a prompt address change keeps registration reminders from going to your old street.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: Which four pieces of owner and vehicle info let you report a Missouri address change by email?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Include your full name, old and new addresses, license number or last four SSN digits, and plate numbers.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: Which registration and property-tax documents may you need when renewing Missouri license plates?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Bring your renewal card, prior receipt, or title copy alongside a paid personal property tax receipt or non-assessment statement.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: Which local government issues your personal property tax receipt, and what time span must it cover?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Your county collector—or the City of St. Louis—issues the receipt covering the span of your previous registration.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: How do the property-tax receipts required at renewal differ after a one-year registration versus a two-year registration?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Renewing after a two-year tag means proving paid personal property taxes across both prior years, not just last year.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Along with tax and registration papers, what proof of coverage and payment can plate renewal require?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Keep an active insurance card or financial-responsibility proof ready with your registration and processing fees.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: When your vehicle requires inspection at renewal, what certificate must you bring and how recent must it be?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Getting inspected too early backfires if your safety or emissions slip ages past sixty days before you renew.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: How does the arrival timing of a mailed renewal notice compare with the freshness rule on an inspection certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Your postcard arrives roughly two months early, matching the strict sixty-day freshness window for completing inspections.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Why should you read the checklist printed on your own Missouri renewal notice before heading in?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Exemptions vary by model year, mileage, and county, so your personal renewal card lists only what applies to you.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: How can you tell from your renewal postcard whether your plates qualify to be renewed online?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Finding a printed PIN on your mailed renewal notice means you can renew tags online and skip counter lines.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: What form must you file—and within how many days—after selling a motor vehicle or ATV in Missouri?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Reporting the sale within thirty days protects you if the buyer racks up tickets or crashes before retitling.
