sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Through which two channels can a seller submit Missouri's Notice of Sale form?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Drop the completed Notice of Sale at any local license branch or mail it to the form's printed address.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: What does Missouri require you to do if your license plates, tabs, or vehicle title get lost or destroyed?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Driving with missing plates or expired-looking missing tabs invites traffic stops until you apply for replacements.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: What do replacement titles, individual plates, and tab sets each cost when lost or destroyed, plus what added charge?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Lost or destroyed titles, single plates, and tab sets each run eight dollars fifty cents plus nine dollars processing.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: How does a notarized theft affidavit change the cost and yearly limit for replacing stolen Missouri plates and tabs?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: With a notarized stolen-plate affidavit, Missouri waives the eight-fifty item charge up to twice a year, charging only processing.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: Up to how many times per year can stolen Missouri plates and tabs be replaced without the item fee?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Missouri caps no-charge stolen plate and tab replacements at two replacements inside any twelve-month year.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: How does the cost of replacing stolen plates and tabs compare with replacing lost or destroyed ones?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Both situations charge nine dollars processing, whereas lost or destroyed items add eight-fifty per plate or tab set.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: What coverage must every Missouri motor vehicle owner and driver maintain, and what legal name does Missouri give it?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Both vehicle owners and anyone behind the wheel must maintain Financial Responsibility before operating on Missouri streets.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Whose injuries and property damage does your liability insurance policy pay to cover?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Liability coverage protects other people you hurt or property you wreck rather than paying to fix your own bumper.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: How do most Missouri drivers satisfy Financial Responsibility instead of using cash deposits, bonds, or self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Buying a standard auto liability policy from an insurer or agent is far simpler than tying up thousands in bonds.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: During which two license-office plate transactions must Missouri vehicle owners present proof of insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Clerks verify active coverage both when you first put Missouri plates on a car and whenever you renew them.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What written pledge do you sign when registering a motor vehicle in Missouri?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Dropping your policy right after getting tags violates the signed pledge promising continuous coverage on that vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Which six paper documents or digital options count as valid proof of insurance in Missouri?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Missouri accepts current ID cards, policies, binders, paid policy receipts, state self-insurance or bond cards, and mobile screens.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: In auto insurance paperwork, what is a binder?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Agents issue a temporary binder right after purchase so you have valid roadside proof before permanent cards arrive.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What happens during a traffic stop if an officer asks for your insurance proof and you cannot produce it?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Even having an active policy at home still lands you a citation if no proof is inside the car.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: When may the Department request proof of insurance, and what crash situation guarantees a mandatory request?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Expect random sampling anytime and a mandatory verification demand whenever a crash report shows no coverage presented.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What fleet size and financial showing qualify an owner for a Missouri certificate of self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Large fleet owners with at least twenty-six vehicles who prove financial capacity receive a Department self-insurance certificate.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Does owning exactly twenty-five vehicles qualify a business or individual for Missouri self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Watch the words more than twenty-five closely because owning twenty-five flat misses the threshold by one vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: What dollar amounts must be filed with the Department for a surety bond or CD versus a property-backed bond?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Negotiable securities, CDs, and surety bonds require seventy-five thousand dollars, while real estate bonds double to one-fifty.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: How much cash must be deposited—and with which state official—to earn a certificate of self-insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Placing that seventy-five-thousand-dollar cash reserve with Missouri's State Treasurer backs future claims and unlocks self-insurance certification.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: How does the required dollar filing for a surety bond, CD, or security compare against a real estate bond?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Property-backed bonds demand one hundred fifty thousand dollars, twice the seventy-five-thousand-dollar floor for surety bonds or CDs.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: What is Missouri's minimum liability coverage per person for bodily injury?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Every Missouri liability policy must cover at least twenty-five thousand dollars when one person is hurt.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: What is Missouri's minimum total bodily-injury liability coverage for a single crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: When multiple people are hurt in one collision, total bodily-injury coverage must reach at least fifty thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: How do Missouri's bodily-injury liability minimums differ between one injured person and an entire crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Keep twenty-five thousand tied to any one injured victim and fifty thousand tied to everyone injured together.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What minimum property-damage liability coverage must every Missouri policy carry per crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Repairing totaled cars, guardrails, or fences quickly adds up, setting twenty-five thousand dollars as Missouri's floor.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Which bodily-injury liability minimum shares the exact same twenty-five-thousand-dollar figure as per-crash property damage?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Missouri's twenty-five, fifty, twenty-five split bookends fifty thousand total injury with matching twenty-five-thousand-dollar outer numbers.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: What mandatory uninsured-motorist coverage amounts must Missouri drivers carry alongside liability?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Uninsured-motorist coverage protects you and your passengers if an illegally uninsured driver injures you.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: How do required uninsured-motorist limits compare with liability limits regarding bodily injury versus property damage?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Mandatory uninsured-motorist protection mirrors twenty-five and fifty thousand for bodily injuries without listing any property-damage minimum.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What financial and licensing losses can hit you if you let your Missouri auto insurance lapse?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Driving uncovered exposes your personal savings to huge crash claims and risks losing both license and plates.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: What action does the Department take when it discovers you failed to maintain required insurance?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Once state verification catches an uninsured gap, a mailed suspension notice puts both driving privileges and plates at risk.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What form is most commonly used to file ongoing proof of insurance with Missouri, and who submits it?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Your insurance carrier or agent transmits the SR twenty-two directly to verify active state-minimum liability coverage.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: After a first Missouri insurance suspension, what fee and ongoing filing period are required to get reinstated?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Reinstating a first lapse requires zero mandatory wait days once you pay twenty dollars, though three-year monitoring begins.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: What happens if your insurance drops again before finishing the required three-year proof period?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Any coverage break inside your three-year SR twenty-two monitoring window triggers a brand-new suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: What suspension length, fee, and proof period hit when you collect two insurance suspensions within two years?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: A second uninsured hit inside two years locks privileges for ninety days and jumps the fee tenfold.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: What wait time, fee, and proof requirement apply to a third or subsequent Missouri insurance suspension?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Reaching three insurance suspensions sidelines you a full year and doubles the reinstatement fee again to four hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: How does Missouri's reinstatement fee climb across first, second, and third-or-later insurance suspensions?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Memorize that steep jump from twenty dollars on offense one to two hundred and then four hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: What time window makes two insurance suspensions count as a repeat offense, and how long must proof stay on file afterward?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Do not swap those numbers because two years measures repeat spacing while three years sets your SR twenty-two monitoring term.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How long are your license or plates suspended if you cause a crash and leave the resulting damages unpaid?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Causing collision losses and walking away from the bill suspends your driving privileges and plates for twelve months.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: How can a driver suspended for unpaid crash damages get reinstated before the full year ends?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Sending settlement proof to the Driver License Bureau with a twenty-dollar fee lifts that one-year suspension early.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: How does a suspension over unpaid crash damages compare with a third no-insurance suspension in length and fees?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Both carry a one-year term, yet settling unpaid damages reinstates early for twenty dollars versus four hundred on third-lapse.
sec15-card-sec15-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Both one year, twenty versus four-hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Both one year, twenty versus four-hundred

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: How much crash protection does responsible, defensive driving give—and can it eliminate crash risk completely?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Smart defensive habits slash your odds of colliding, yet mandatory insurance exists because no driver controls every surprise.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: How does the Missouri driver guide define a traffic crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Even solo curb impacts that hurt you or dent someone's mailbox count legally as a traffic crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: May you drive away after bumping an unattended parked vehicle, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Driving off after scraping a parked car turns an ordinary fender-bender into a criminal hit-and-run offense.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: Right after a collision occurs, what must you do first and where should you put your car if drivable?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Leaving a drivable car sitting in live lanes invites high-speed secondary pileups from approaching traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: How should you care for injured people at a crash scene before paramedics arrive, and whom do you call?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Moving an injured victim can worsen spinal trauma, so keep them comfortable in place and call police and ambulance.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: Which three emergency lighting tools help warn oncoming traffic after a nighttime or bad-weather crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Darkness and rain hide disabled cars until oncoming drivers are too close to brake without roadside warning lights.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: Which six identity, vehicle, and coverage details must you exchange with everyone involved in a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Capture license numbers, VINs, tag numbers, and insurer plus policy numbers on scene before anyone drives off.
sec15-card-sec15-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Names, addresses, IDs, VINs, plates, policies

visual_sync.text_span: Names, addresses, IDs, VINs, plates, policies

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: When are you allowed to leave a police-attended crash scene, and should you call your insurer if not at fault?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Remain until law enforcement clears you to leave, and alert your carrier promptly regardless of who caused impact.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: What severe license consequence can follow hitting a road worker or responder inside a marked zone?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Hitting road crews or first responders inside marked work or emergency zones can revoke your driving privilege outright.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: What does Missouri's Move It law require when vehicles have a minor crash with zero injuries?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Pulling onto the shoulder or a nearby safe spot immediately keeps minor bumper taps from triggering highway pileups.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: Contrast what Missouri tells you to move after a minor no-injury crash versus an injury crash?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Clear undamaged rolling metal out of live traffic fast, while leaving hurt people still until medics arrive.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: How many minutes of approaching traffic backup does every single minute of a blocked freeway lane create?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Five minutes parked in a live interstate lane arguing over a scratch creates twenty minutes of stopped congestion.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What percentage of Missouri traffic fatalities come from secondary crashes that the Move It law targets?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Nearly one in five Missouri road deaths happens when fast traffic slams into backups behind an earlier wreck.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: What four-word slogan promotes Missouri's Move It law on signs around St. Louis and Kansas City?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Metro highway signs remind drivers in St. Louis and Kansas City to steer drivable fender-benders off travel lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: How did the Missouri Department of Transportation mark the tenth anniversary of the Move It law?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: MoDOT used that ten-year milestone to reinforce clearing minor non-injury collisions off active roadways.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: Within how many days must a required Missouri motor vehicle accident report be filed?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Waiting past thirty days when a state crash report applies risks an administrative suspension of your license.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: Do parking-lot crashes or privately settled crashes still require a Missouri accident report when conditions apply?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Private cash handshakes or shopping-center lots never waive reporting if the Missouri crash occurred under a year ago.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Which uninsured-driver fact combined with what damage or injury threshold triggers a mandatory Missouri accident report?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Mandatory filing kicks in whenever an uninsured party is involved alongside any injury, death, or damage exceeding five hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: Does an injury-free crash with exactly five hundred dollars of property damage trigger a mandatory accident report?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Damage must be greater than five hundred dollars without injury, so five hundred flat falls just below mandatory reporting.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: Why must both an uninsured party and qualifying damage or injury exist before an accident report is mandatory?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Fully insured drivers skip filing state Form eleven-forty even after big crashes because both conditions must hold.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: If you file an optional report below the threshold involving an uninsured driver, what action can the Department take?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: The state can still penalize the other driver for lacking mandatory coverage even when damage stayed small.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: Where can you obtain Missouri's Motor Vehicle Accident Report form, and which two ways can you submit it?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Grab the form online, from your insurance agent, or at any license branch, then mail or fax it.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which four screenings make up the full Missouri driver examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Missouri evaluates rule knowledge, eyesight, sign literacy, and behind-the-wheel skill before issuing a brand-new driver license.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Which three application, expiration, or Revenue-order situations require taking the Missouri driver examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Even holding an unexpired card will not exempt you if the Director of Revenue orders a recheck.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which two types of Missouri license revocations send a driver back through the full examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Losing your privilege to point accumulation or an Administrative Alcohol action means proving every exam part from scratch.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Which out-of-state drivers only have to pass the vision and road sign tests when switching to Missouri?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Applying for the matching Missouri class with a valid or recently expired out-of-state card waives written and driving parts.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: What two conditions must an out-of-state license satisfy to qualify for the vision-and-sign shortcut?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Upgrading license classes or holding a card expired one hundred eighty-four days or longer forfeits that two-part shortcut.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Which agency administers Missouri driver exams, and who can direct you to the closest testing station?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Remember that license offices issue cards while the Missouri State Highway Patrol administers the examinations themselves.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: What two facts must you prove before testing, and when must you present that identification again?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Bring your ID to every single written exam, road exam, and counter application visit rather than just day one.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: Where does the guide point you to find Department and Highway Patrol phone numbers and testing station lists?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Checking the back of the manual or the Highway Patrol website confirms current testing hours and locations before traveling.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: How many questions are on the Class F written test, and what question style is used?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Every question pulls straight from the traffic statutes and safe-driving habits covered inside the Missouri driver guide.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: May you consult the manual during the Class F written exam, and is Chapter fifteen commercial material included?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Basic operator applicants test strictly from memory and skip the commercial-vehicle rules reserved for for-hire drivers.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How does the Class E for-hire written test differ from Class F, and is it open book?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: For-hire drivers face a closed-book special written exam that adds Chapter fifteen commercial-vehicle safety rules.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What testing rule do Class F and Class E written exams share, and what single topic separates them?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Neither written exam allows notes or manuals, and only Class E pulls questions from the commercial vehicle chapter.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What two abilities does the Missouri road sign test evaluate?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Spotting a sign's visual design and knowing the rule behind it keeps you safe even when text blurs.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: What criminal level and license loss can result from cheating, lying, or using cameras or two-way devices during an exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Pulling out recording gear, two-way electronics, or dishonest statements turns an exam room into a criminal misdemeanor case.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which two distinct eyesight checks must every new or renewing Missouri applicant take?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Clear straight-ahead reading and wide peripheral awareness both matter for spotting hazards entering from side lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What is Missouri's standard minimum passing visual acuity score?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Meeting twenty over forty with either eye or both eyes clears standard visual sharpness at the screening machine.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Does hitting twenty over forty on the acuity chart waive the peripheral vision screen?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Sharp straight-ahead eyesight cannot substitute for peripheral field testing because each check measures a separate safety skill.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What degree readings pass Missouri's standard peripheral side-vision check using two eyes versus a single eye?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Drivers with sight in only one eye need a wider eighty-five-degree field to compensate on the road.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Along with the fifty-five and eighty-five degree passing routes, what combined peripheral floor blocks licensing completely?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Falling short of seventy combined peripheral degrees leaves too wide a blind zone for any Missouri license.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What two outcomes can happen to your application if you fall short of Missouri's standard vision numbers?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Corrective lenses, daylight-only hours, or speed caps can bridge mild deficits, while severe loss leads to denial.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What happens next if you fail the standard vision check at the testing station?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: The examiner issues a specialist vision form, and getting a fresh prescription can pause testing until your lenses arrive.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Worse than which acuity score and which combined peripheral score disqualifies you from taking the road test or holding a license?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Vision worse than twenty over one hundred sixty even with lenses, or below seventy combined degrees, bars driving completely.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: What does the twenty over one hundred sixty acuity number represent, and when does it block a license?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Don't confuse twenty over forty standard passing with twenty over one hundred sixty, where neither natural nor corrected vision qualifies.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Which three exam parts must you pass before taking the driving test, and who administers it?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: You only get behind the wheel with a Highway Patrol examiner after clearing written, vision, and road sign screens.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What does the examiner inspect before starting the road test, and when will the drive be refused?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Showing up in a car with broken safety equipment or hazardous defects ends your appointment at the curb.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Which five plate, sticker, belt, door, and seat items must your road-test vehicle have ready?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Expired tags, stuck passenger doors, missing seat belts, or a cluttered passenger seat will cancel your skills exam.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Which two braking systems, warning device, and document must your test car carry to pass inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Verify your foot brake, parking brake, horn, and insurance card at home so a quick fix never costs test day.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Who is allowed inside the car during the driving test, and what rules govern conversation and traffic laws?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Friends and parents stay outside while the examiner scores rather than coaches your adherence to Missouri traffic law.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: How much lead time does the examiner give when calling out a maneuver during the driving test?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Examiners never try to trick you into sudden swerves; every instruction leaves time to check mirrors and lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: How are you graded when asked to operate controls like wipers, turn signals, brakes, or the accelerator?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Practice the switch layout in the car you bring so you never fumble for wipers or signals.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Which five steps are graded as you start up and pull away at the beginning of the road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Forgetting to release the parking brake or skipping a mirror check and turn signal costs points before reaching traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: What three qualities does the examiner score during starts and stops on the road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Jerky starts or late, nose-diving braking signals poor pedal modulation and late hazard recognition.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What are the exact length and width dimensions of Missouri's road-test parallel parking space?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Practicing inside a twenty-five-by-seven-foot box in an empty lot builds muscle memory for exam cones.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: What maximum curb distance, stall position, and time limit apply during the parallel parking maneuver?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Center your car within eighteen inches of the curb inside the two-minute clock to clear the numbers cleanly.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Beyond curb distance and the two-minute clock, which four technique steps are scored in parallel parking?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Line up cleanly before reversing, avoid bumping boundary markers, steer accurately, and check plus signal when exiting.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Which parking maneuver is the only one on the Missouri test with a time limit and a measured stall?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Hill parking has no stopwatch or twenty-five-by-seven stall; those constraints belong solely to parallel parking.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Where must you look while backing on the driving test, and what three vehicle-control points are graded?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Staring only at mirrors or backup screens loses points; turn over your right shoulder and hold a straight, steady path.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: At least how many right and left turns are on the driving test, and what six habits are graded?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Examiners score starting lane, early signals, traffic scans, speed, control, and finishing inside the proper receiving lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What is the minimum count of right turns and left turns required during the Missouri driving skills test?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Expect at least four total scored turns split evenly so the examiner observes both right-hand and left-hand execution.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: Which five curb, gear, wheel, brake, and exit steps are scored when parking on a hill?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Stop within eighteen inches, shift into park or gear, angle front tires properly, set the brake, and signal out.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: What identical maximum curb distance applies to both parallel parking and hill parking on the Missouri test?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Leaving more than a foot and a half between your tires and the curb costs points on both maneuvers.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Which six habits does the examiner grade as you approach and move through intersections?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Approach smoothly in the right lane, scan cross traffic, stop at the proper mark, and yield without blocking lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: Which two specific stopping and yielding habits are highlighted in the intersection grading section?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Stopping past the line or poking your nose out to block cross traffic drops points fast.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Which five general driving habits does the examiner watch continuously from start to finish?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Even between specific maneuvers, tailgating, drifting over lane lines, or missing yield cues steadily chips away points.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: What does the examiner continuously score regarding roadside signs and traffic lights across the entire route?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Overlooking a posted regulatory sign or signal phase anywhere along the route counts against your observation score.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: How does point scoring work on the Missouri driving test, and what point loss fails the exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: You can lose up to thirty deducted points and still pass, whereas thirty-one or more ends in failure.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: Which five major mistakes cause an immediate failure on the Missouri driving test regardless of points?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: An at-fault collision, striking a walker, near-crash recklessness, breaking any traffic law, or refusing instructions fails instantly.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Can you fail the Missouri driving test even if you have lost thirty points or fewer?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: A clean point sheet will not save a drive if you roll a stop sign or refuse an instruction.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: What document do you get upon passing the driving test, and what must you do before driving solo?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Do not drive off solo holding only the passed test form; visit a license office first to get licensed.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: How many driving skills tests are you allowed to take in a single day?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: If a drive goes sideways, take the examiner's practice feedback home and return another day sharper.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: What happens if you fail the Missouri driving skills test three times?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Testing freezes after failure three until you log additional behind-the-wheel training, submit proof, and receive written Department authorization.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How does the number thirty on a single test differ from the number three across multiple attempts?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Losing more than thirty points fails one road exam, while failing three road exams triggers mandatory extra training.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Where are failed driving-test results sent, and what notice follows after repeated failures?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Examiners transmit failed scores to the Department of Revenue, which mails out the formal letter ordering extra behind-the-wheel practice.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: Who must provide the extra behind-the-wheel training after three road-test failures, and what clearance is needed before retesting?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Only practice supervised by an eligible driver counts, and you must hold Department approval in hand before attempt four.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What does Missouri law set as every motorist's highest duty on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Missouri holds drivers to a high standard of care that protects walkers, cyclists, other motorists, and passengers alike.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Does Missouri right-of-way law ever grant any driver the right-of-way, and what crash duty always applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Even when another driver should have yielded, you must still do everything possible to avoid hitting anyone.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: At what kinds of meeting points do right-of-way rules step in, and what do they settle?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Whenever paths cross without signs or traffic lights, right-of-way statutes prevent standoffs by deciding order.

sec04-card-sec04-R19.question_text: Which three levels of government set traffic rules in Missouri, and what local topics can town or county rules cover?
sec04-card-sec04-R19.teaching_text: Watch posted local signs closely because towns and counties regulate speed, one-way flow, truck routes, parking, and noise.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What added minimum penalties hit drivers caught speeding or passing through a Missouri state highway work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Those two-hundred-fifty and three-hundred-dollar work-zone minimums stack right on top of standard ticket fines.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How should you approach and pass a pedestrian or bicyclist sharing the roadway?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Give walkers and cyclists the same patience and safe passing gap you would give any slower motor vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Which left-turn situation or city-street width allows passing another vehicle on the right?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: You may pass on the right around a left-turning car or along city pavement wide enough for two lanes each way.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: Beyond left-turners and wide city streets, on which two other road types is passing on the right legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Outside city limits, right-side passing requires clear pavement marked for at least four total lanes, or a one-way road.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does the lane requirement for passing on the right differ between a rural highway and a city street?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Rural highways require marked four-lane pavement, whereas city streets only need unobstructed room for two lines each direction.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: Are you ever allowed to leave the main paved roadway and drive onto the shoulder to pass on the right?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Shoulders hide gravel, debris, and stopped cars, so swinging off the main pavement to pass is illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: Which three roadway settings or traffic situations heighten the danger of passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Cross-street pullouts and oncoming traffic on two-lane pavement erase escape room if a pass takes too long.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: When must you stay off the left side of the road approaching a hill crest or curve?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Hidden oncoming traffic over a blind rise or bend closes head-on at combined highway speeds with nowhere to dodge.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Within what distance of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel is driving left of center banned when sightlines are blocked?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Narrow bridge decks and dark tunnel portals eliminate shoulder escape space inside that final hundred-foot approach.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Within what distance of intersections or railroad crossings—and alongside which pavement stripe—must you stay right of center?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Passing near tracks, cross streets, or solid yellow stripes puts you head-on against turning cars or trains.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: Which two distinct groups of road features share Missouri's one-hundred-foot no-passing rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Lock one hundred feet to both obstructed bridges, viaducts, and tunnels and every intersection or railroad crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: When must drivers yield to pedestrians near streets, driveways, or alleys, and when is driving on a sidewalk legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Pedestrians own sidewalks and legal crossings, and cars may never roll along a sidewalk except to cross a driveway.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: To which vehicles must a driver turning left at an intersection yield?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Misjudging the speed of oncoming through traffic while turning left across their path is a leading intersection crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: At a four-way stop, which driver has priority to proceed first?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Come to a complete halt at the line first, then move out in the order vehicles reached the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls out from an alley, driveway, or roadside?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Drivers already moving at street speed hold priority over anyone pulling out from parked edges or private drives.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: At an open intersection without stop signs or lights—other than a roundabout—who gets priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Check left first for immediate crossers, then yield to any car approaching simultaneously from your right.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Before entering a roundabout, which two groups must you yield to while waiting for a gap?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Scan the entry crosswalk first and then look left so you never cut off traffic already inside the circle.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Compare who goes first at a four-way stop, an uncontrolled intersection, and a roundabout?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Keeping arrival order, right-side priority, and circulating priority distinct prevents hesitation or T-bone mistakes across junction types.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction using a siren or air horn and red or blue lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Clear the center lanes immediately toward the right curb regardless of whether responders approach from behind or ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection, and before resuming?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Stopping mid-intersection blocks the responder's turn radius, and pulling back out too fast risks hitting a second rig.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: On a road of four or more lanes with at least two going your way, how should you pass a stopped red- or red-and-blue-lit emergency vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Leaving an empty buffer lane shields officers, firefighters, and paramedics working inches from highway traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What must you do near a stopped emergency vehicle if changing lanes away from it is unsafe or impossible?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Never force a sideswipe into heavy traffic; ease off the throttle and pass slowly with full control.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: How do the warning signals requiring you to pull right for a moving emergency vehicle differ from the stopped-vehicle rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Moving responders pair sirens or air horns with red or blue lights, while stationary move-over protection triggers on lights alone.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: How far ahead of a stop does a school bus start flashing amber lights, and what signals come on once stopped?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Five hundred feet of yellow warning gives following and oncoming cars plenty of space to brake smoothly before red.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: What school-bus warning action begins five hundred feet before a designated student stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Treat flashing yellow bus lamps five hundred feet out as your cue to prepare to stop rather than speed past.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Which directions of traffic must halt for a stopped school bus showing red lights and its stop arm on two-lane two-way or one-way streets?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Students cross both lanes on two-lane streets, so every approaching and following vehicle must stop short of the bus.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: In which three roadway or loading-zone situations are you not required to stop for a school bus flashing red?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers keep moving across separate divided roadways or four-plus-lane highways, and inside no-crossing school loading zones.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: Why don't oncoming drivers stop on a highway of four or more lanes, and what matching rule restricts the bus there?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Opposite lanes keep flowing on four-plus-lane highways because buses are barred from crossing students across more than two lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Once stopped for an unloading school bus, when may you start moving again?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Hold stationary and watch roadside curbs until either the bus rolls forward or the bus driver motions you through.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: How many points go onto your Missouri driving record if convicted of failing to stop for a school bus?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Passing a loading or unloading school bus slams your record with five points plus mandatory court license suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: What court-ordered suspension lengths apply to first, second, and third school-bus stop violations within five years?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: First and five-year second convictions bring ninety-day suspensions, escalating to one hundred eighty days on a third offense.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: On which repeat offense within five years does the Missouri school-bus suspension jump from ninety to one hundred eighty days?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Don't fall for the test trap assuming offense two doubles; the jump to one hundred eighty days hits offense three.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: Before which three maneuvers must you signal, and what two signaling methods are allowed?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Keep your turn blinkers and brake bulbs inspected, and use standard hand-and-arm signals whenever needed.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: At least how far before a turn must you enter the proper turn lane and start signaling?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Getting into your turn lane and blinking one hundred feet early prevents last-second cutoffs and rear-end crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: Why does Missouri tell drivers to start signaling at least one hundred feet ahead of a turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Flicking your lever mid-turn surprises following traffic and pedestrians who needed advance notice to adjust.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: When no signs or lane arrows mark a turn, which lane do you start from and which lane do you turn into?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Finish the turn inside the nearest matching lane first, then signal a separate lane change afterward if needed.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: What crash risk do you create if you swing wide to the left before making a right turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Swinging left tricks following drivers into thinking you are turning left, tempting them straight into your right-turn path.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: While turning left, what corner mistake must you avoid and what space must you leave for opposing left-turners?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Stay out of cross-street approach lanes on your left while leaving room for oncoming left-turners to turn in front.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: Where do you line up and enter when turning left off a one-way road onto two-way traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Turn from the extreme left curb lane across into the lane right of the yellow center stripe, moving right if clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: Where do your left wheels start and where do you enter when turning left from one two-way street onto another?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Keeping left wheels close to the center yellow line sets a clean arc onto the right half of the cross street.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: When turning left from a two-way street onto a two-lane one-way street, where do you start and which lane may you enter?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Start right beside your yellow center line and turn cleanly into whichever lane of the two-lane one-way road is open.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: At an intersection with side-by-side dual left-turn lanes, which receiving lane must each turning car enter?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Drifting across the dotted guide arc mid-turn sideswipes the car turning right alongside you.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: In which four specific roadway or intersection settings are U-turns strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Never whip a U-turn near blind curves or crests, posted bans, traffic signals, police-directed junctions, or towns prohibiting them.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: What is the sole legal use of a center two-way left-turn lane, what distance cap applies, and what side-street move is banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Never cruise past five hundred feet or merge into a shared center lane from a side street as an acceleration strip.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: What is the maximum distance you may travel inside a shared center two-way left-turn lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Treating the shared center lane like a passing lane past five hundred feet invites a head-on crash with opposing turners.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: Which direction do vehicles circulate around a roundabout island, and which three road users get priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Steer slightly right on entry to flow counterclockwise after yielding to pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles already circulating.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: Which four steps prepare you safely as you approach a multi-lane roundabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Pick your signed lane before the yield line, glance left for circulating gaps, and never turn left into the island.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: Once inside a roundabout, what four rules govern island side, lane changes, passing, and stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Switching lanes, trying to pass, or stopping mid-circle—unless avoiding a crash—causes chain-reaction collisions.
sec04-card-sec04-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Keep right, never pass, keep moving

visual_sync.text_span: Keep right, never pass, keep moving

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: What speed and signal do you use when leaving a roundabout, and when may you accelerate?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Hold a slow exit pace until you clear the pedestrian crosswalk because walkers cross right across exit legs.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: How do you handle an approaching emergency vehicle before entering a roundabout versus when already inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Stopping inside a curved single-lane ring traps fire engines behind you, so clear your exit first and pull right.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.question_text: What two crash-reducing design features make roundabouts safer than standard intersections, and what sign guards every entry?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.teaching_text: Eliminating high-speed left turns across oncoming traffic and posting yield signs at every leg slashes fatal angle crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.question_text: What should you do if you miss your roundabout exit, and how should you drive near large trucks or trailers inside?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.teaching_text: Never brake or swerve across lanes for a missed exit; loop around calmly and never crowd wide-tracking trailers.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.question_text: What is a roundabout truck apron, which wheels use it, and which everyday vehicles must stay off it?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.teaching_text: The raised inner collar lets long trailer rear wheels track around tight islands while cars, SUVs, and pickups stay off.

sec04-card-sec04-R18.question_text: At a Missouri four-lane highway J-turn intersection, what three-step sequence replaces crossing straight across fast traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-R18.teaching_text: Merging right with traffic flow and using the median left turn removes deadly broadside crossings across divided highway lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which directions should your eyes sweep on the highway — how long may eyes leave the road — and how do you check a map?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Looking down for even four seconds at sixty-five miles per hour covers a football field blind.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which lane is your travel lane on a two-lane highway — and what two checks clear crossing the center line?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Never cross into the oncoming lane when headlights approach or a solid yellow stripe borders you.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, which three reasons justify leaving the right lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane blocks faster traffic unless overtaking, opening merge space, or turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Compare lane discipline on a two-lane undivided highway against a highway with four or more lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Two-lane passing borrows oncoming asphalt briefly, whereas four-lane roads reserve inner lanes for passing, merges, or lefts.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Why must you glance frequently at your speedometer right after exiting a fast highway onto local streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Velocitation tricks highway-adapted ears and eyes into thinking forty-five feels like twenty-five on town streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How are left lanes, right lanes, and shoulders each treated for passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Passing on the right is limited to cars turning left, and shoulders are strictly off-limits.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which two mirrors and which shoulder check come before pulling left to pass on a four-lane highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Mirrors show fast-closing traffic far back, while the left-shoulder glance catches cars alongside your quarter panel.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What is a blind spot — and what quick action overcomes it before changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Even well-set mirrors leave side pockets that only a brief head turn clears.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Where off another car's rear corners should you avoid cruising — and how do you fix it?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Hovering diagonally off someone's rear fender hides your hood right where lane-changers drift.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: How briskly should you move through another driver's blind spot while overtaking — and what ceiling still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Accelerating smoothly clears that hidden blind zone promptly without exceeding the posted speed limit.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What collision risk grows every extra second you camp inside another vehicle's blind spot?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Drivers who glance only at mirrors assume empty space and drift straight into lingering cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Why shouldn't you linger beside or close behind a truck or bus — and what mirror clue confirms visibility?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: If the driver's face isn't visible in that big side mirror, your entire car is invisible.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: After overtaking a tractor-trailer, when may you return right — and what pedal mistake must you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Letting off the gas right in front of an eighty-thousand-pound rig steals its braking buffer.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Once mirrors and blind spots are clear, how do you execute the pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Early turn signals and smooth steering keep high-speed lane shifts predictable without speeding.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Which mirror landmark, shoulder glance, and stalk switch clear returning to the right lane after passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Seeing the overtaken car in your inside mirror plus checking right prevents clipping their front bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does your over-the-shoulder glance flip between pulling out to pass and tucking back in?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Always turn your chin toward the lane you are about to enter — left out, right back.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What two things must you do whenever another driver starts passing you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Accelerating alongside an overtaking car traps them in oncoming traffic or tight merge gaps.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: If stream after stream of cars passes you on the right on a multi-lane road, what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Getting passed on the right signals you are dragging below lane pace unless preparing a left turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What speed mismatch triggers many multi-vehicle highway wrecks — and what habit prevents it?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Both weaving speeders and crawling roadblocks create closing-speed shocks that spark chain-reaction hits.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: How little time does speeding actually shave per hour — and what does every extra pass add?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Trading collision exposure on pass after pass to arrive three minutes sooner fails basic highway math.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: If you drive slower than normal pace and a queue stacks up behind your bumper, what courtesy applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Clearing a frustrated line of trailing cars prevents risky blind-curve overtaking behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How frequently should your eyes flick to your rearview mirrors during highway cruising?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Brief mirror sweeps every few seconds spot fast-closing motorcycles or tailgaters before you need to brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Why look far ahead for climbing semis or merging compact cars on highway hills?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Reading slow movers from a quarter mile back lets you step left smoothly instead of slamming brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Which two vehicle types lose speed on long climbs and need extra runway when merging?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Loaded rigs and small-engine cars bleed momentum uphill and accelerate gently off entrance ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What spacing rule behind the car ahead does Missouri's highway chapter emphasize — and which chapter details it?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Leaving generous following cushions at highway speed buys reaction seconds when brake lights flash ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Where must you NEVER stop routinely on a highway — and where belong non-emergency stops?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Stopping inside live high-speed highway travel lanes invites catastrophic rear-end collisions from trailing cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: What two dangers make hard highway panic stops risky — and what eye habit avoids them?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Locking up at highway speed risks losing control while catching trailing drivers off guard.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How can easing off the gas or changing lanes early improve your stop when traffic slows ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Shedding speed gradually often lets congestion clear ahead before your wheels ever halt.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Where are the ONLY legal places to enter or leave a controlled-access highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Eliminating driveways and cross-street stop lights keeps interstate traffic flowing safely via ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: In how many directions may vehicles travel on highway entrance and exit ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Every entrance and exit ramp carries traffic strictly one way — never turn around on one.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What is your speed goal on an entrance ramp and acceleration lane before merging?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Accelerating up to highway pace before sliding into a gap prevents forcing fast cars to slam brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: When is stopping at the end of an acceleration lane ever acceptable?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Merging from a dead stop into highway speeds is perilous unless bumper-to-bumper traffic leaves zero gap.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: While through drivers should make room, who legally yields if no highway gap opens for a merging car?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Through-lane highway traffic holds legal priority — never muscle into an occupied lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: When should you get into your exit side lane, where do you slow down, and what sign governs ramp speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Hold highway speed until entering the deceleration lane, then match the yellow ramp advisory speed.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Contrast where acceleration and deceleration lanes sit — and the job of each one?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Entrance ramps end with acceleration lanes to build pace, while exit ramps begin with deceleration lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: Which three dangerous moves are forbidden if you overshoot your exit — and what is the right fix?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Reversing along an interstate shoulder or median turnaround invites fatal high-speed impacts.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: How does an interchange connect two busy highways without stoplights across main lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Grade-separated bridges and ramps let drivers switch highways smoothly once they read overhead signs.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Name the four common interchange layouts pictured in the Missouri Driver Guide?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Missouri pioneered America's first Diverging Diamond in Springfield alongside classic cloverleaf, diamond, and directional ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What unusual lane position happens briefly inside a Diverging Diamond Interchange — and what guides you through?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Crossing briefly to the left eliminates opposing left-turn conflicts onto freeway entrance ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What mental state is highway hypnosis, and what sights and sounds bring it on?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Unchanging straight scenery plus droning tire, wind, and engine hum lull brains into zoned-out microsleeps.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What active eye habit prevents highway hypnosis — and what must you do if sleepiness creeps in?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Shifting gaze across mirrors, signs, and traffic fights tunnel stare until you exit for rest.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: How does severe drowsiness compare with drunk driving — and what should a very sleepy driver do?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Cracking windows or blasting music cannot cure exhaustion — stop at a rest area and sleep.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: What single shared solution does the Missouri guide prescribe for both highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Exiting onto a rest stop or service area beats gambling against nodding off at seventy.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: What common mental lapse causes many highway crashes — and what mindset counters it?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Treating open highway miles as autopilot leaves you flat-footed when debris or brake lights appear.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: When may you stop on a highway shoulder — and what lights plus two visual distress signals help?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Blinking hazards paired with a propped hood or white antenna cloth broadcast breakdown trouble clearly.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Together with emergency flashers, which two non-electric distress signals does page thirty-nine suggest on the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Even if your battery dies, a raised hood and fluttering white cloth stay visible.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Why is making yourself and your stalled vehicle unmistakable so critical after a highway breakdown?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Approaching drivers often mistake an unlit stopped car for moving traffic until impact.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: When mechanical trouble hits at highway speed, what are your first two priorities?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Using remaining rolling momentum to clear live lanes beats coasting to a stop in traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: If your car dies where leaving the roadway is impossible, which two blind spots must you avoid stopping past?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Cresting hills or rounding blind curves at highway speed gives oncoming traffic zero stopping sightline.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: Where do emergency flares go relative to a disabled vehicle — and what message do they send?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Advance flares give fast traffic early runway to merge over before reaching your bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: What roadway tire-changing ban applies — and which three exterior parts can hold a white distress cloth?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Never crouch beside live lanes changing a flat; tie white cloth to antenna, mirror, or handle.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Modern cars often lack tall whip antennas — which two other exterior parts does page forty-one list for a white cloth?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Tying white fabric onto your left mirror or door handle signals distress on antenna-free cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How is a standard stop sign shaped and colored, and what action does it require?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Rolling slowly past an octagon still counts as running a stop sign and risks hitting unseen cross traffic.
sec09-card-sec09-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Red octagon, white letters, full stop

visual_sync.text_span: Red octagon, white letters, full stop

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: How is a yield sign shaped and colored, and how must you handle intersecting traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Slowing early lets you stop smoothly when cars occupy the lane or merge cleanly when open.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: What visual differences in sides and letter colors separate a stop sign from a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Distinct silhouettes let drivers tell a mandatory stop from a yield from behind or in snow.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: What separates your legal obligation at a stop sign from your obligation at a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Treating a stop sign like an empty-road yield fails behind-the-wheel tests and causes blind corner wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Where do you halt when a white stop line sits past the sign post, and where when none exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Halting back at a recessed post when a forward stop line exists blocks your view of cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: In what one-two-three priority order do you pick your exact stopping spot at a stop sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Memorizing that exact sequence keeps your bumper off pedestrian paths and out of cross-street lanes on exam day.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What mistake has happened if you face a Wrong Way sign, and how must you fix it?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Continuing forward even a hundred yards against divided highway flow creates a deadly head-on collision.
sec09-card-sec09-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Oncoming lane; pull off, turn back

visual_sync.text_span: Oncoming lane; pull off, turn back

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What rule does a Do Not Enter sign enforce at a road opening, and what does One Way indicate?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Exit ramps and downtown grids pair both signs so turning drivers never turn into opposing lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How does encountering a Wrong Way sign differ from seeing a Do Not Enter sign at an opening?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: One stands guard at the threshold before you turn, while the second warns you already crossed inside.
sec09-card-sec09-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Do Not Enter prevents; Wrong corrects

visual_sync.text_span: Do Not Enter prevents; Wrong corrects

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Where are lane control signs mounted, and how do they assign movements to individual lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Spotting overhead turn-only arrows early prevents last-second swerves across solid white intersection lines.
sec09-card-sec09-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Side or overhead arrows assign lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Side or overhead arrows assign lanes

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Which path around a median nose or roadway obstruction does a Keep Right sign require?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Passing left of a raised island puts your car straight into oncoming left-turn or through lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What conditions does a posted speed limit sign assume, and when does Missouri law require going slower?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number on ice, blind hills, or crowded streets still earns a too-fast-for-conditions citation.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What is Missouri's normal minimum speed on an interstate, and what should you do if you cannot hold it?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Crawling under forty in seventy-mile freeway flow turns your rear bumper into a rolling roadblock.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Inside a Missouri city, town, or village with no speed sign posted, what legal limit applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Sidewalks, driveways, and intersections pack tightly inside town limits even where signs are spaced far apart.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Contrast Missouri's unposted municipal speed cap with its normal interstate minimum speed?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Pairing twenty-five in town against forty minimum on interstates keeps two high-yield Missouri numbers crystal clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Which Missouri body can raise or lower speed limits from uniform defaults, and for what two reasons?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Posted signs set by the Commission always override handbook defaults whenever local safety or traffic flow demands it.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What default top speed does the Missouri Driver Guide list for rural expressways?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Rural expressways sit five miles per hour above urban freeways and ten above lettered county routes.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Which two road categories share Missouri's sixty-mile-per-hour default maximum in the guide?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Both busy metro interstates and open non-lettered rural highways share that sixty-mile default tier.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What default maximum speed applies on Missouri's supplementary lettered roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Two-lane Route A, B, or Z blacktops feature narrower shoulders, farm driveways, and steeper hills than expressways.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Roughly how many miles of interstate cross Missouri, and why do urban stretches often post lower caps?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Frequent metro ramps and weaving traffic make lower urban speeds essential across Missouri's interstate network.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Which sign shape and road feature warn you ahead of time that railroad tracks are coming up?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Spotting the yellow circle and painted RXR early gives you room to listen and brake smoothly.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What traffic rule does a white X-shaped crossbuck enforce, and what does a small plaque underneath tell you?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Knowing whether two or three sets of rails cross the road warns you that a second train can hide.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do the shape and location of a railroad advance warning sign differ from a crossbuck?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: The yellow circle preps your foot downrange, while the white X marks the exact tracks where you yield.
sec09-card-sec09-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Round warns early; X sits trackside

visual_sync.text_span: Round warns early; X sits trackside

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What two deadly mistakes must you never make when approaching or starting across railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Stopping with your tail bumper overhanging live rails traps you if traffic ahead stays backed up.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Why must you avoid shifting gears while your tires are crossing railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Missing a shift or stalling mid-clutch leaves your vehicle stranded directly in a locomotive's path.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What is your legal duty at a crossing with alternating red flashers or a lowering gate?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Trying to beat a descending arm puts your car across rails seconds before the locomotive arrives.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does your legal duty at a standalone crossbuck differ from active red lights or lowered gates?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Passive crossings ask you to look and yield, whereas active flashers or gates command a mandatory halt.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: How many feet from the nearest rail must you stop for flashing lights or lowered gates, and what is banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet risks overhang strikes, and zig-zagging around gates is illegal and lethal.
sec09-card-sec09-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Stop fifteen to fifty; never dodge

visual_sync.text_span: Stop fifteen to fifty; never dodge

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: After one train clears a multi-track crossing, why watch the lights and adjacent rails before moving?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: A second locomotive running the opposite direction on parallel tracks is hidden behind the departing cars.
sec09-card-sec09-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Lights stay on; check second train

visual_sync.text_span: Lights stay on; check second train

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What specific shade identifies Missouri work-zone signs, and who or what directs cars through the zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent orange cuts through glare and dust so drivers spot flaggers and cones early.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: Name four common warning messages posted on orange Missouri work-zone signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Each legend previews a specific hazard from slick fresh tar and flying stones to upcoming merges.
sec09-card-sec09-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Road Work, Oil, Gravel, Lane Closed

visual_sync.text_span: Road Work, Oil, Gravel, Lane Closed

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Why should spotting orange work-zone signs immediately put you on high alert?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Workers and heavy machinery operate steps from moving bumpers with only cones or paint between them.
sec09-card-sec09-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Active crews on or beside road

visual_sync.text_span: Active crews on or beside road

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What five habits keep everyone safe while driving through any highway work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Narrowed lanes, lower limits, crew members on foot, and slow dump trucks entering traffic leave zero margin for phones.
sec09-card-sec09-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Drop distractions, obey signs, watch trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Drop distractions, obey signs, watch trucks

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What minimum fines hit drivers caught speeding or passing inside a Missouri state-road work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Those steep statutory floors stack on top of regular court fines to protect crews from reckless passes.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: How does recognizing Missouri's different work-zone setups help you behind the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Knowing whether cones guard a shoulder crew, a lane drop, or a moving convoy prevents surprise braking.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: How should you adjust as you approach a shoulder work zone where crews stay off the main lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Even without a lane closure, workers or mowers near the white edge stripe need a slower, calmer pass.
sec09-card-sec09-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Ease off speed passing shoulder work

visual_sync.text_span: Ease off speed passing shoulder work

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What two steps are required when a work zone closes one of the lanes ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Waiting until the cones hit your bumper or ignoring the temporary speed plaque causes taper-zone wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How does what a shoulder work zone asks of drivers differ from a full lane closure?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Keeping your lane while easing speed fits shoulder work, whereas closed lanes require merging plus posted slowdowns.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: How does a flagging operation manage traffic on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: With both directions taking turns down one open strip, disobeying either flagger sends you head-on into traffic.
sec09-card-sec09-F28.must_match_memory_hook: One lane shared; flaggers both ends

visual_sync.text_span: One lane shared; flaggers both ends

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What characterizes a mobile work zone, and what hazard should you expect beside the equipment?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Striping, patching, and sweeping crews creep or pause directly inside live lanes with workers on foot nearby.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: What trailing safety vehicle warns you as you catch up to a mobile work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: That buffer truck carries a Slow Vehicles legend and arrow board so highway traffic merges well back.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: When overtaking a mobile work zone, what guides your lane choice and what lies ahead of the shadow truck?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Cutting back right in front of the buffer vehicle puts you straight into the paint or patching convoy.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Contrast a two-lane flagging operation with a highway mobile work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Fixed flaggers alternate one shared lane, whereas rolling convoys rely on a trailing arrow-panel shadow truck.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: How do green and brown guide signs look, and which destinations do each point toward?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: White lettering on green steers highway navigation while brown flags parks, cultural landmarks, and historic sites.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: What colors and shapes identify motorist service signs, and what stops do they mark?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Spotting a blue hospital H or rest-area plaque lets tired or injured travelers exit safely without searching phones.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: What background color distinction separates guide signs from motorist service signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: All three use crisp white lettering, so background color alone separates navigation and parks from roadside help.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: Which official Missouri vehicle-check sign appears alongside guide and service signs in the driver manual?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Recognizing official inspection station plaques helps Missouri owners locate state-approved safety check bays.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: What single feature of a numbered highway route marker tells you its road classification?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Distinct shields instantly separate interstate freeways from U.S. highways, Missouri state routes, and county roads.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: What simple two-part habit keeps you from getting lost on unfamiliar highways?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Knowing your route numbers beforehand prevents panic lane dives across exit gores when GPS drops signal.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: How do odd-numbered and even-numbered highway routes align with compass directions?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Knowing I-55 runs north-south while I-70 runs east-west keeps your bearings straight at complex interchanges.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: On a three-digit Missouri interstate like I-270 or I-155, what does an even versus odd first digit mean?
