sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: An even beltway like I-270 or I-435 circles back to the main highway, whereas an odd spur heads into town.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: How does the leading digit split three-digit interstate routes between city loops and city spurs?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Checking just the first digit tells through-travelers whether a bypass reconnects ahead or dead-ends downtown.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Where do interstate exit numbers begin at zero, and in which compass directions do they climb?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Watching exit numbers count upward confirms you are heading east or north and shows exact miles to your exit.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: In which two travel directions do interstate exit numbers count downward?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: If your exit number is lower than the last sign while numbers are climbing, you are driving the wrong way.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Where sit emergency reference markers, what details do they display, and how closely are they spaced?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Keeping one marker always in sight lets stranded callers give nine-one-one dispatchers their exact route, direction, and tenth-mile.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: Before registering or renewing tags on many Missouri vehicles, what check is required unless an exemption applies?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Missouri requires non-exempt cars and trucks to pass a mechanical safety check before plates issue or renew.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: Who is allowed to run a Missouri safety inspection, and how can drivers recognize an authorized shop?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Look for the posted state inspection sign outside any licensed garage before booking your safety check.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: What mailed document helps you confirm whether your upcoming plate renewal requires a safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Reading your registration renewal postcard saves paying for an unnecessary inspection during an exempt year.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: How many registration years does a single Missouri safety inspection cover, and what event cuts that short?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: One passed safety check carries through two registration years as long as vehicle ownership stays unchanged.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: How do even and odd vehicle model years line up with calendar years for Missouri safety inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Matching model-year parity with the expiration calendar year spreads statewide inspection volume evenly across two-year cycles.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: What is the maximum dollar fee an authorized Missouri station may charge for a standard inspection versus a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: State law caps safety inspection charges at twelve dollars for regular vehicles and ten dollars for motorcycles.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: How does Missouri's safety inspection fee cap differ between standard vehicles and motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Two-wheeled motorcycles carry a ten-dollar ceiling rather than the twelve-dollar cap applied to other vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: What proof does a vehicle earn upon passing safety inspection, and how many days does it stay valid?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Finish your plate transaction within sixty days so your passed safety certificate does not expire in your folder.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: When does a safety inspection certificate provided by a Missouri dealer stay good for ninety days?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: So long as the Missouri dealer inspected the car within sixty days before purchase, you get ninety days.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: How does a standard station's sixty-day certificate window compare with a qualifying Missouri dealer certificate?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Dealer buyers gain thirty extra days beyond a normal station's sixty-day slip when inspected within sixty days pre-sale.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What age and odometer combination exempts a vehicle—even with an out-of-state title—from Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Cars inside ten years after their model year stay exempt until the odometer hits one hundred fifty thousand miles.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: Through which calendar year does a twenty seventeen model-year car under one hundred fifty thousand miles skip safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Adding ten full years onto model year twenty seventeen extends that low-mileage safety exemption right through twenty twenty-seven.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Which towed units, specialty tags, condition sales, and wholesale transfers never need a Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Missouri exempts every trailer, historic-plated collector car, junk or salvage project, and wholesale dealer-to-dealer transfer.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: Which MoDOT-registered commercial vehicles and statutory small vehicles also skip Missouri's standard safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Intrastate carriers registered under MoDOT rules and statutory low-speed vehicles both fall outside passenger safety checks.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: When does a truck registered at twenty-six thousand pounds or more for under twelve months skip safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Even if the renewal postcard prints an inspection item, short-term heavy tags starting April first onward skip it.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: What condition must a vehicle's braking system meet to pass a Missouri safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Weak, spongy, or uneven brakes stretch emergency stopping distances and fail state safety inspection immediately.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What minimum number and color of working headlights must a vehicle carry?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Driving with a burned-out or off-color headlamp cuts night visibility and makes oncoming cars misjudge your width.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: What rear lights and reflector visibility distance are required on a Missouri vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Dual red taillights and reflectors visible five hundred feet back keep parked or moving cars noticeable in darkness.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: What standard governs how a vehicle's turn signals and brake lights must function?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Inspectors check that every factory-installed blinker and brake lamp illuminates cleanly without disabled bulbs or wiring hacks.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: Which two steering-system flaws will keep a vehicle from passing safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Sloppy steering free-play delays emergency swerves while binding linkage can stick mid-turn.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: Which two tire conditions fail a Missouri vehicle safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Worn-smooth tread hydroplanes on wet pavement while mismatched tire sizes upset braking balance and stability.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: What must be true of a vehicle's horn and windshield wipers during safety inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: You need a clear audible horn to warn walkers or drifting drivers plus working wipers when storms hit.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: Which three exhaust-system components must be securely attached on a vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Securely routing fumes through an intact pipe, muffler, and tailpipe prevents deadly carbon monoxide cabin leaks.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: What two conditions must fuel lines, hoses, connections, and tanks meet at inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Loose fuel tanks or dripping fuel lines near hot exhaust metal create an extreme roadside fire hazard.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: Vehicles manufactured after what date must carry safety glass in every window?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Laminated and tempered safety glass keeps crash impacts from shattering into jagged shards across every cabin window.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What damage and clutter rules govern your windshield's viewing area, and what two exceptions are allowed?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Severe cracks or hanging items block sightlines; only required legal stickers and upper tinted-strip info signs qualify.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: Passenger cars built after what date must carry how many sets of front seat belts?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Passenger cars built after June thirtieth, nineteen sixty-four must keep two working front seat-belt sets installed.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: Vehicles built after which year must carry both an inside and an outside rearview mirror?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Post-nineteen-sixty-seven vehicles require both interior and exterior mirrors so drivers monitor rear and side lanes together.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: Which vehicles must retain their factory-installed air pollution control devices?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Removing catalytic converters or emissions hardware on post-nineteen-sixty-seven non-diesel cars fails state safety inspection.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: Does the post-nineteen-sixty-seven safety-inspection rule on factory air pollution devices apply to diesel vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Watch that fuel-type wording carefully because Missouri's post-sixty-seven pollution-device safety item excludes diesel engines.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: Match the three classic equipment cutoffs in chronological order across nineteen thirty-six, nineteen sixty-four, and nineteen sixty-seven?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Anchor glass to thirty-six, front belts to mid-sixty-four, and dual mirrors plus pollution gear to after sixty-seven.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: Which trucks are required by Missouri law to have rear mud flaps installed?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Heavy trucks registered above twenty-four thousand pounds lacking rear fenders throw rocks and spray without mud flaps.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: What is the maximum legal height above the ground for a passenger vehicle's bumpers?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Lifting passenger bumpers higher than twenty-two inches lets a car override crash zones in a collision.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: How are maximum bumper heights determined for commercial vehicles compared with passenger cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Instead of one flat twenty-two-inch cap, commercial truck bumper limits scale according to gross vehicle weight rating.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Beyond safety-inspection checklist items, what three exterior identification or warning items does Missouri law require?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Passing shop inspection is only part of road legality; proper plate mounting, illumination, and warning signs still apply.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: How must your Missouri license plates be mounted and maintained, and what rule governs decorative plate frames?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Dealership or novelty frames that obscure state names, expiration tabs, or characters violate Missouri plate visibility law.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: Where do plates mount when issued as a pair, and where does the single plate go on a trailer or motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Two-plate passenger vehicles mount front and rear, while motorcycles and trailers bolt their single plate on back.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: Where does a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds mount its single plate, and how does the rear get one?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Heavy trucks often pull trailers that hide rear bumpers, so their primary single tag belongs up front.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: While trailers and motorcycles mount their single plate on the back, which vehicle mounts its single plate on the front?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Remember heavy trucks over twelve thousand pounds as the lone front-mounted exception to rear single plates.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: How does a heavy-truck owner above twelve thousand pounds get a rear tag, and where does the first tag stay?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Missouri issues that second rear tag only upon specific owner request while keeping the original tag up front.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: What color lamp must illuminate your rear license plate, and from what distance must the plate be readable?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: A working white tag bulb ensures your rear plate stays legible from fifty feet during nighttime stops.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: When cargo sticks out more than five feet past the rear, what daytime flag and nighttime light are required?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Drivers misjudge long lumber or pipes without a sixteen-inch-square red flag by day or red lamp after dark.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.question_text: What maximum towline gap applies when towing another vehicle, and during what hours must both vehicles show lights?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.teaching_text: Keeping towed vehicles within fifteen feet and lighting both from half-hour post-sunset to pre-sunrise stops drivers cutting between.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.question_text: Which slow vehicles need a reflective emblem between sunset and half-hour pre-sunrise, and where does it mount?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.teaching_text: Mounting a clean reflective triangle centered at least four feet high warns fast night traffic of twenty-five-or-under equipment.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: Between the slow-moving vehicle emblem, projecting-load lights, and towing lights, which rule starts right at sunset?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Slow-moving emblems begin right at sunset whereas overhang and tow lights kick in thirty minutes after sunset.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.question_text: Between which exact calendar dates may Missouri drivers legally use studded snow tires?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.teaching_text: Metal tire studs chew up bare warm-weather asphalt, restricting legal Missouri use from November first to April first.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.question_text: Which windows may carry tint or sun-screening, and what light-blockage cap applies to front door glass?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.teaching_text: Limiting front side-window tint to sixty-five percent blockage preserves night mirror sightlines and eye contact at intersections.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.question_text: Residents of which Missouri city and four surrounding counties must complete vehicle emissions inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.teaching_text: Missouri concentrates tailpipe and onboard emissions checks across the city of St. Louis and its four neighboring metro counties.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.question_text: How frequently do emissions inspections run, and how does their model-year calendar match safety inspections?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.teaching_text: Aligning biennial emissions checks to the exact same even-and-odd schedule lets gateway drivers knock out both together.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.question_text: Regardless of model year, what ownership event normally triggers a required emissions check unless exempt?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.teaching_text: Selling a non-exempt car in the emissions region requires passing an emissions test even outside its renewal year.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.question_text: When do brand-new vehicles and first retail sales skip the at-sale emissions check?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.teaching_text: Sales during the model year or next year with under six thousand odometer miles skip at-sale emissions.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.question_text: How long do brand-new, never-previously-titled vehicles skip emissions unconditionally—and what keeps that waiver active?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.teaching_text: Your brand-new car stays emissions-exempt across its model year and following year provided ownership does not change.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: What mileage reading at the first biennial check extends a brand-new untitled vehicle's emissions waiver to four years?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Staying below forty thousand miles at that first two-year mark stretches a new car's emissions exemption four years.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: Which older model years are exempt from Missouri emissions testing for gasoline vehicles versus diesel vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Onboard diagnostics arrived a year later on diesels, setting ninety-five-and-older for gas and ninety-six-and-older for diesel.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: Above what manufacturer gross vehicle weight rating is a vehicle exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: Heavy-duty pickups and vans rated above eight thousand five hundred pounds GVWR skip gateway passenger emissions.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.question_text: Driving fewer than how many miles between biennial checks exempts a vehicle from emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.teaching_text: Cars driven sparingly—under twelve thousand miles across two years—qualify for a low-mileage emissions waiver.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.question_text: Vehicles powered exclusively by fuels outside which three standard fuels skip Missouri emissions testing?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.teaching_text: Pure electric, propane, or natural-gas cars running on alternative power skip gateway emissions checks completely.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.question_text: Which six specialty, bus, or two-wheel license plate categories are exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.teaching_text: Historic cars, street rods, motorcycles, motortricycles, school buses, and shuttle buses all skip gateway emissions testing.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.question_text: In which single county are gasoline-powered low-speed vehicles exempt from Missouri emissions inspection?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.teaching_text: Gasoline low-speed vehicles enjoy an emissions carve-out strictly inside Franklin County and nowhere else in the zone.

sec16-card-sec16-R20.question_text: How long must an emissions-area vehicle be based and driven outside the zone to qualify as exempt?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.teaching_text: College or military cars kept continuously outside the gateway zone for twenty-four months qualify for an out-of-area exemption.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Does Missouri treat driving as a constitutional right or an earned privilege, and how can you lose it?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Because holding a license is conditional on safe behavior, stacking traffic violations lets the state suspend or revoke your permission to drive.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What happens to your driving record when you are convicted of a traffic offense committed while your vehicle was moving?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Courts report moving-traffic guilty verdicts directly to the state agency, which logs violation points onto your permanent driver file.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: Does merely getting pulled over add points in Missouri, or what exact event puts points on your record?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: A roadside citation by itself adds zero points until a court enters a conviction and notifies the state agency.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What is the ultimate consequence of letting too many violation points pile up on your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Missouri's point system exists to flag repeat unsafe habits early and pull dangerous drivers off the road when totals climb.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Why can a speeding conviction add either two or three points to your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Municipal court convictions often carry fewer speeding points than county or state prosecutions for the exact same lead-foot habit.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: How many points is speeding worth on the Missouri Driver Guide's state-law violation list?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Whenever an exam question asks specifically about the state-law violation table, pick three points for speeding.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Why does one part of the point-system chapter mention two or three points for speeding while the table lists three?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: The chapter text compares municipal, county, and state courts, whereas the bulleted chart strictly displays state-statute point values.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: How many points hit your record for a careless and imprudent driving conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: A single four-point careless driving conviction lands you right on Missouri's twelve-month advisory letter threshold.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: How many points do you get for knowingly letting an unlicensed person drive a vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: You do not even have to sit in the driver's seat to earn four record points if you hand keys to someone unlicensed.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Which two violations in the Missouri point table both carry four points?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Grouping violations by point tier makes test recall effortless—both aggressive driving and handing keys to an unlicensed friend cost four.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: How many points are assessed for failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Passing stopped student buses carries five heavy points—more than speeding or careless driving—because children cross unpredictably.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What point total and license action can result from leaving the scene of a traffic crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Fleeing a collision dumps twelve points onto your record at once, instantly hitting Missouri's twelve-month revocation threshold.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: How many points does a felony involving a motor vehicle add to your Missouri record?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Using a car in a felony immediately drops twelve points onto your record, enough for an automatic one-year revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How many points are added for obtaining a driver license through misrepresentation?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Lying or using fake details to get a credential triggers the maximum twelve-point hit right out of the gate.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: How many points is driving on a suspended or revoked driver license worth?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Ignoring an active suspension or revocation drops twelve fresh points onto your record, turning a short timeout into a one-year revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Which four state-law violation examples in this chapter each carry twelve points?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Every twelve-point offense triggers immediate one-year revocation territory on its very first conviction without needing prior tickets.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What does the state send you if you accumulate four points within twelve months?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: That warning letter leaves your license active for now, alerting you that another ticket soon will push you toward suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: How many points within what number of months get your Missouri driving privilege suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Just two careless-driving convictions or three state-court speeding tickets inside a year and a half will park your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How does hitting four points in twelve months differ from hitting eight points in eighteen months?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Test makers love offering suspension as a trap answer for four points, so remember four only mails a warning advisory.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How long does an eight-points-in-eighteen-months suspension last on the first, second, and third or later time?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Each repeat point suspension adds another thirty days on the sidelines, capping out at ninety days from the third suspension onward.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Which three point-and-month combinations trigger a one-year revocation of your driving privilege?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Even if you dodge twelve points in a single year, steady ticket habits across two or three years still revoke your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: What simple math pattern connects Missouri's three point-revocation thresholds?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Start at twelve points in twelve months and step up by six points and one year each time to recall all three.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What key factor changes the requirements to reinstate your license after a point suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Intoxication-linked point losses require substance education and higher fees than ordinary speeding or careless-driving point suspensions.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: What two items reinstate your license after a point suspension or revocation that was NOT related to alcohol?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Non-alcohol point losses cost twenty dollars rather than forty-five and skip SATOP, though you still must file SR-twenty-two insurance.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: Which chapter of the Missouri Driver Guide covers the full details on filing SR-twenty-two proof of insurance?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Missouri cross-references its financial-responsibility rules so drivers know how long high-risk insurance filings must stay active.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Where in the guide are the reinstatement items listed when a point suspension or revocation involved intoxication?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Alcohol-triggered point actions pull in the forty-five-dollar fee, SATOP completion, and two-year SR-twenty-two filing from the alcohol chapter.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: When the state reinstates your driving privilege after a suspension or revocation, what number does your point total drop to?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: You do not restart with a clean zero—coming back at four points means one fresh ticket puts you near suspension again.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: Does the drop to four points happen at reinstatement itself, or only after a clean year of driving?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Your total steps down to four the day your license returns, and annual percentage reductions shrink that four over clean years.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: How much are your remaining points reduced after one full year of driving with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Staying ticket-free for twelve straight months trims a third off your active point balance.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: How much are your remaining points reduced after two consecutive years with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Keep your record spotless through a second straight year and the state slices half off whatever points remain.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: What happens to your point balance after three straight years with zero new points?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Three uninterrupted violation-free years clear every remaining active point off your Missouri balance.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: What is the year-by-year sequence of point reductions across three clean years?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Each clean twelve-month stretch takes a larger bite out of your remaining points until year three clears them completely.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: When three clean years drop your points to zero, do all past convictions vanish from your driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Erasing active points stops point suspensions, yet serious convictions remain permanently visible on your official history.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: Beyond points, what license action can follow a conviction for driving while your privilege is suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Sneaking behind the wheel during a thirty-day suspension can escalate your penalty into a full twelve-month revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What criminal charge and license penalty can hit if you keep driving during a revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Driving while already revoked crosses from traffic trouble into felony criminal exposure alongside another full year without privileges.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: What major extra risk separates driving while revoked from driving while suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Both violations risk a one-year revocation, yet driving during an active revocation exposes you to a felony record.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: If you miss a traffic court date, how many days does the court give you to pay fines before reporting you to the bureau?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: That mailed court warning gives you one thirty-day grace window to settle the ticket before your license gets pulled.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What happens if you still fail to resolve a missed traffic court date within those thirty days?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Once day thirty passes unpaid, state licensing officials get word from the court and shut off your license immediately.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Does a failure-to-appear suspension end after a set number of days, or what ends it?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Unlike a thirty-day point suspension, an unpaid-ticket suspension stays open indefinitely until both receipt and fee arrive.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: Why are you still suspended if you pay an overdue traffic fine at the courthouse and immediately drive home?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Settling the court fine is only half the fix—your license stays suspended until the bureau gets proof plus twenty dollars.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Which two ways can you submit your paid-ticket proof and reinstatement fee for a failure-to-appear suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: You can mail paperwork to the Driver License Bureau or hand-deliver it to the central office in Jefferson City.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: When convicted of failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students, how many points hit your record?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Alongside a court-ordered suspension, five violation points land on your record—already past the four-point advisory mark.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: What suspension comes with a first offense for failing to stop for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Even on a clean record with zero prior points, passing one stopped school bus triggers a court-ordered suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: On a first school-bus stop offense, is the court locked into ordering ninety days?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Ninety days is the standard benchmark on offense one, though the judge has discretion to set a different duration.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: Within a five-year window, what suspensions apply to a second and a third or later school-bus offense?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Inside five years, strike two locks in ninety days and strike three doubles the bench time to one hundred eighty days.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How do first, second, and third school-bus stop suspensions progress when repeats happen within five years?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Judicial flexibility disappears on repeat offenses within five years, locking in ninety days on the second and one-eighty on the third.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How do Missouri's three school-bus suspension lengths differ from the three eight-point suspension lengths?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: A very first school-bus violation starts at ninety days—where ordinary point suspensions only arrive on strike three.
